CAUSE AND EFFECT

因果

———————————

“All choices have a consequence. Unfortunately some consequences appear long after you’ve forgotten the choice you made.”

“所有选择都会产生后果。不幸的是，有些后果会在你忘记自己当初的选择很久之后才显现出来。”

—Anonymous

-匿名的

A close relationship can heal all the old wounds that affect our intelligence, creativity, personality, sexuality, money, life direction, self-expression and passion. 21 But it often involves re-experiencing the traumas that influenced these aspects of our lives in the first place. And there’s the rub! Instead of feeling our pain and being responsible for it, we often try to make our partners responsible for hurting us. Then we try to control their behaviour so they won’t do it again.

亲密关系可以治愈所有影响我们智力、创造力、个性、性欲、金钱、人生方向、自我表达和激情的旧伤。<sup>21</sup> 但这往往意味着要重新经历那些最初影响我们生活方方面面的创伤。问题就在这里！我们常常不是去感受自己的痛苦并承担责任，而是试图让伴侣为伤害我们负责。然后，我们试图控制他们的行为，以免他们再次伤害我们。

Let’s look at an example of this idea.

让我们来看一个例子来说明这个想法。

John and Mary have been common-law spouses for a little over a year, living cozily in a one-bedroom apartment. Everything is going fairly well except that John is becoming increasingly bothered by Mary’s tendency to leave the bathroom in a mess. At first he mentions these concerns to her in a light, humorous, manner. Even though they are considerate of each other in most other cases, Mary keeps forgetting to tidy up the bathroom after she uses it. Finally things come to a boil one morning when John discovers a messy bathroom and charges back out to the kitchen where Mary is making her breakfast. This dialogue follows:

约翰和玛丽同居一年多了，他们住在一间一居室的公寓里，过着温馨的生活。一切都还算顺利，只是约翰越来越受不了玛丽用完浴室后总是弄得一团糟。起初，他只是用轻松幽默的方式跟玛丽提起这件事。虽然他们平时都很体贴，但玛丽总是忘记用完浴室后收拾。终于有一天早上，事情爆发了。约翰发现浴室很乱，气冲冲地跑回厨房，玛丽正在那里做早餐。以下是他们的对话：

John: For Chrissake Mary, how many times do I have to ask you to clean up the bathroom when you’re through?

约翰：看在上帝的份上，玛丽，我到底要跟你说多少遍，用完浴室后才肯打扫？

Mary: I’m so sorry—I was going to clean it, but you were in such a hurry to get in the shower that I forgot.

玛丽：真对不起——我本来打算打扫的，但是你急着去洗澡，我忘了。

John: Well how much time does it take to put a toothpaste cap on, or to put your makeup in the cabinet?

约翰：那么，盖上牙膏盖或者把化妆品放进柜子里需要多少时间呢？

Mary: I said I was sorry, John. I just didn’t have enough time.

玛丽：约翰，我说过对不起了。我只是时间不够。

John: Well why don’t you get up five minutes earlier? I mean, hell, it only takes five bloody minutes to…

约翰：那你为什么不早起五分钟呢？我的意思是，见鬼，也就五分钟的事儿……

Mary: I’m lucky I can get up at all, with you playing that damn stereo full blast until three in the morning!

玛丽：你把那该死的音响开到凌晨三点，吵得我还能起床都算幸运了！

John: Oh come on, it wasn’t three in the morning—and you’re just trying to change the subject!

约翰：哦，拜托，现在又不是凌晨三点——你只是想转移话题！

Mary: I am not!

玛丽：我不是！

John: You are so!

约翰：你真是太棒了！

Mary: You always want everything your way, John. I live here too, you know? You can be really selfish sometimes!

玛丽：约翰，你总是想事事都按你的方式来。我也住在这里，你知道吗？你有时候真的很自私！

John: Hey, I’m not the one who leaves my stuff all over the apartment. You’ve turned the bathroom into a bloody obstacle course!

约翰：嘿，我又不是那个把东西乱扔在公寓里的人。你把浴室弄得跟个障碍赛道似的！

Mary: Oh, you’re just exaggerating!

玛丽：哦，你太夸张了！

John: I am not!

约翰：我不是！

Mary: You are too!

玛丽：你也是！

John: Am not

约翰：我不是

Mary: Are too! 22

玛丽：也是！22

Now how are John and Mary going to get through this one? It seems pretty obvious to observers that they just need to compromise a little bit and everyone would be happy. However, I have found that the problem with compromises is twofold. First of all, it does not completely satisfy either side, but leaves both sides feeling that they have settled for less than they truly wanted. The other problem, and I believe the more serious one, is that the issues which relate directly to the pain the situation triggered, never get addressed. In the case of John and Mary, the real reason they are fighting will not be given the chance to be resolved even if John turns down his stereo and Mary cleans up the bathroom. The truth is, neither John nor Mary are upset for the reasons that they think they are. To see what the real issue is, let’s have a look at some of John and Mary’s life experiences.

约翰和玛丽该如何度过难关呢？旁观者似乎都认为，他们只需要做出一些妥协，大家都会皆大欢喜。然而，我发现妥协的问题有两方面。首先，它无法让双方都完全满意，反而会让双方都觉得他们得到的远低于自己真正想要的。另一个问题，我认为也是更严重的问题，是那些直接源于双方痛苦的根源问题，始终没有得到解决。就约翰和玛丽而言，即使约翰调低了音响音量，玛丽打扫了浴室，他们争吵的真正原因也依然没有机会得到解决。事实上，约翰和玛丽生气的原因并非他们自认为的那样。为了弄清问题的症结所在，让我们回顾一下约翰和玛丽的一些人生经历。

When Mary was growing up, she was under the discipline of strict parents who decreed that children should be invisible. If Dad found a toy lying around, he would throw it in the garbage and take away all her toys for a month. Her mother always punished her if she did not put her clothes away. And if she left the toothpaste cap off the tube, it sent both her parents into a fit of angry lecturing. As she continued to suffer these reactions from her parents, Mary began to firmly believe that she was nothing more than a bother to them, and the less evidence of her presence in their lives the better. After a while Mary came to believe that her parents wished that she were dead, or at the very least invisible.

玛丽从小在严厉的父母管教下长大，父母认为孩子应该隐形。爸爸要是发现玩具乱放，就会扔进垃圾桶，然后没收她所有的玩具一个月。妈妈要是知道她没把衣服收好，就会惩罚她。如果她没盖好牙膏盖，父母也会勃然大怒，对她进行一番训斥。玛丽饱受父母的责骂，渐渐地，她开始坚信自己对他们来说只是个累赘，越少人注意到她的存在越好。久而久之，玛丽甚至觉得父母巴不得她死，或者至少让她隐形。

Thus after a year of intimate cohabitation, without being aware of it, Mary was re-experiencing the childhood pain of being told to be invisible—that her presence, or any sign of her existence, was a burden to her parents. Now John was giving her the same message, calling up all the old pain from her past. Mentioning the toothpaste cap was a painfully effective way to uncover old subconscious bruises; even though his criticism of one of her habits may have hurt her feelings, it would never have had such an impact on her if not for the history of criticism she endured in her youth, and the way she interpreted her parents’ behaviour as denying her importance to them. Most of her pain was old pain.

因此，在一年的亲密同居之后，玛丽在不知不觉中再次体验到了童年时期被告知要“隐形”的痛苦——她的存在，或者说她存在的任何迹象，对父母来说都是一种负担。如今，约翰也在向她传递着同样的信息，唤起了她过往所有的伤痛。提及牙膏盖这件事，如同揭开潜意识里旧伤疤一般，痛苦而有效；尽管他对她某个习惯的批评可能伤害了她的感情，但如果没有她童年时期遭受的批评，以及她将父母的行为解读为否定她的重要性，这件事绝不会对她造成如此巨大的影响。她的大部分痛苦都源于旧伤。

When John was young, he felt like he was constantly ignored by his parents and siblings. At dinner table conversations, his opinions seemed to go unheard. During discussions about where the family should go for vacations, his input was never requested and twice his birthday was almost completely forgotten. In a counselling session, he once claimed that he nearly died of a burst appendix before his parents took his sobbing complaints seriously enough to get him to a hospital. As far as John could remember, no matter how he tried to express himself—be it by tantrum, pouting, or even extreme illness—his family would either respond with irritation, or not at all.

约翰小时候总觉得自己被父母和兄弟姐妹忽视。餐桌上的谈话，他的意见似乎总是被忽略。讨论全家去哪里度假时，从来没有人征求过他的意见，他的生日甚至两次几乎被完全遗忘。在一次心理咨询中，他曾声称自己阑尾破裂差点丧命，直到父母重视起他的哭诉才把他送往医院。据约翰回忆，无论他如何表达自己——无论是发脾气、撅嘴，甚至是病得很重——家人要么不耐烦，要么干脆无动于衷。

Now living with Mary, John was being told once again that what he wanted was of very little relevance. He told Mary many times that a clean bathroom was important to him, but her repeated messiness was telling him that what he wanted was unimportant, and thus John himself was unimportant. He might as well not exist. Her mess broke through a dam that was holding back a flood of old childhood hurt.

和玛丽一起生活后，约翰再次被告知，他的需求无关紧要。他曾多次告诉玛丽，干净的浴室对他很重要，但她反复的邋遢却让他觉得，他的需求不重要，因此，约翰本人也变得无关紧要。他仿佛根本不存在。她的邋遢冲破了一道堤坝，淹没了他童年时期的伤痛。

When they met and fell in love, John and Mary both thought they had left the past and all its pain behind them. But that morning, both of them felt that they were once again being hurt for expressing their presence in the world. They were both in great pain, but instead of recognizing it and expressing it for what it was, they remained ignorant of the real issue and took their pain out on each other by fighting. This is such a widely accepted form of behaviour that most of us believe it is an intrinsic part of relationship; that’s the way it is and that’s the way it will always be.

约翰和玛丽相遇相爱时，都以为已经摆脱了过去的伤痛。但那天早上，他们却都感到，仅仅因为表达自己的存在，就再次受到了伤害。他们都痛苦万分，却没有正视并坦诚面对，而是选择视而不见，将痛苦发泄在彼此身上，互相争吵。这种行为模式如此普遍，以至于我们大多数人都认为这是人际关系中不可或缺的一部分；理所当然，也永远如此。

What is really happening in the above scenario is that John and Mary are trying to control their old hurt by controlling each other’s behaviours. Just like my childhood experience of squirming uncomfortably on a hard chair rather than facing the horrible taste of canned carrots, many couples would rather squirm around in the discomfort of Power Struggle than face the pain inside them. In my work as a counsellor, I have seen that one of the biggest relationship problems is our attitude towards pain. Every intimate relationship has its difficulties; every time these difficulties arise, there is some emotional pain accompanying it. It is this pain that causes the arguments, criticisms or accusations. If we are experiencing a difficulty in our relationships and we indulge in our anger, we will push each other away. After a while the difficulty disappears, and we become more peaceful again. But it is an uneasy truce, because in order to make the discomfort disappear we had to push our partner away. Allowing them to get closer might well be equated with inviting more pain.

上述情景的真正含义是，约翰和玛丽试图通过控制彼此的行为来控制过去的伤痛。就像我小时候宁愿在硬椅子上难受地扭来扭去也不愿忍受罐头胡萝卜的难吃味道一样，许多伴侣宁愿在权力斗争的不适中挣扎，也不愿面对内心的痛苦。作为一名咨询师，我发现人际关系中最大的问题之一就是我们对待痛苦的态度。每段亲密关系都会遇到困难；每次困难出现，都会伴随着某种情感上的痛苦。正是这种痛苦导致了争吵、批评或指责。如果我们在关系中遇到困难，并沉溺于愤怒，就会把对方推开。过一段时间，困难消失了，我们又恢复了平静。但这是一种不稳定的休战，因为为了消除不适感，我们不得不把伴侣推开。允许他们靠近，很可能就等于自找痛苦。

Whenever I push my wife away by fighting with her, I always feel terrible inside once the anger leaves me. I am guilty and ashamed, because in my fear I pushed away the most important person in my life. I sacrificed her to protect myself. And for what? The pain is still there inside me, waiting for another opportunity to make itself known. Fighting with my partner didn’t resolve anything; it just made us less trusting of each other, and less trusting of the love that brought us together. Instead of letting love heal our pain and bring us closer together, we let our anger drive us further apart. Imagine a tall glass of water. When you meet someone, that person is skimming the surface of the liquid; as you get to know him/her better, he or she begins to penetrate the surface, dropping down through the water. The closer you get to each other, the deeper the other person dives into your glass. Acquaintances stay close to the surface. Close friends go further down. But a significant relationship plunges down as far as you are willing to allow it. The deeper the person dives, the more she/he penetrates the masks and outer personas, more and more accurately uncovering your vulnerabilities. Once you both start to dive into the deeper realms, however, the vulnerable you and your vulnerable partner may not be so attractive.

每当我因为争吵而把妻子推开时，怒气消退后，我内心总是感到无比痛苦。我感到内疚和羞愧，因为恐惧让我推开了生命中最重要的人。我为了保护自己而牺牲了她。而这一切又是为了什么呢？痛苦依然深藏在我心底，伺机再次爆发。和伴侣争吵并没有解决任何问题；它只会让我们彼此更加不信任，也让我们更加不信任当初维系我们爱情的那份爱。我们没有让爱治愈伤痛，让我们更加亲近，反而让愤怒把我们越推越远。想象一下一杯高高的水。当你初次见到某人时，他/她就像漂浮在水面上；随着你对他/她了解的加深，他/她开始深入水面，沉入水底。你们越亲近，对方就越会沉入你的水面。泛泛之交停留在水面附近。挚友则会沉入更深的地方。而一段重要的关系，其深度取决于你愿意让它沉入多深。越是深入探究，就越能看穿伪装和外在人格，越来越准确地揭示你的脆弱之处。然而，一旦你们开始探索更深层次的自我，你和你的伴侣身上那种脆弱的特质或许就不那么吸引人了。

For many years I have likened relationships to a famous Clint Eastwood movie: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly . Only I take it one step further to The Sacred . When you first meet a significant person, mostly what you share is the good . During the Disillusionment stage, you begin to discover the so-called bad aspects of the other, as does she/he of you. At the tail end of this stage, leading into introspection, things often turn ugly . If you respond to the bad and the ugly in a healthy way, the beauty of the introspection stage will lead you to the revelation of the spiritual nature of your relationship. At first, however, we tend to react, rather than respond, to the bad . Instead of understanding, acceptance or forgiveness, we are often tempted by the easier road of…

多年来，我一直把人际关系比作克林特·伊斯特伍德的一部著名电影：《黄金三镖客》。但我更进一步，赋予它神圣的意义。初遇重要的人时，你们分享的大多是美好的一面。在“幻灭期”，你会开始发现对方所谓的缺点，对方也会发现你的缺点。在这个阶段的尾声，进入反思阶段，事情往往会变得糟糕。如果你能以健康的方式应对这些缺点，反思阶段的美好将引领你领悟这段关系的精神本质。然而，起初，我们往往对缺点做出反应，而不是做出回应。我们常常被诱惑去选择更轻松的方式……而不是去理解、接纳或宽恕。

***

ANGER

愤怒

———————————

“Anger is a brief madness.”

“愤怒是一种短暂的疯狂。”

—Horace

——贺拉斯

Anger is the essential ingredient to all Power Struggles, inciting us to actions such as ruthless attacks on our partner’s character, physical abuse, cold silences that turn the home into an ice palace, and all forms of loveless behaviour in between. It is one of the most widely accepted emotions in the world, and it is taken so seriously that few of us recognize that indulging in our anger or suppressing it in fear is futile. 23 It is not creative, inspiring, encouraging, intelligent, life-enhancing or beautiful. Anger tends to exclude rather than include, and never brings peace to a conflict. Lastly, it blocks out any awareness of loving, caring feelings inside the angry individual. So why would such a useless energy be the weapon of choice in Power Struggles?

愤怒是所有权力斗争的根本要素，它会驱使我们做出诸如无情地攻击伴侣的人格、肢体虐待、冷漠的沉默（将家变成冰宫）以及介于两者之间的各种冷酷无情的行为。它是世界上最被广泛接受的情绪之一，人们对它如此重视，以至于很少有人意识到，沉溺于愤怒或出于恐惧而压抑愤怒都是徒劳的。<sup>23</sup> 愤怒既不具有创造力，也不鼓舞人心，更谈不上智慧、提升生活品质或美好。愤怒往往排斥而非包容，也永远无法化解冲突。最后，它会蒙蔽愤怒者内心深处任何爱与关怀的感知。那么，为什么这种毫无用处的能量会成为权力斗争中的首选武器呢？

I have come up with two reasons regarding why we choose to be angry at our partners. The first explanation is that anger helps us numb out any painful feelings inside us, overriding all other emotions and even physical sensations. As an example of how powerful a painkiller anger can be, I have a friend who would become so enraged that somebody once smashed a two by four over his head in a fight and he didn’t feel a thing. He just kept on fighting.

我总结了我们为什么会选择对伴侣生气的两个原因。第一个原因是，愤怒能帮助我们麻痹内心的痛苦感受，压倒其他所有情绪，甚至包括生理感觉。举个例子来说明愤怒的镇痛作用有多强：我有个朋友，有一次在争吵中，有人用木板猛击他的头部，他却毫无感觉，依然继续战斗。

The second benefit of anger is that it is very efficient in controlling the other person’s behaviour by making them feel guilty. When a person feels guilty, they instinctively become afraid of the forthcoming punishment, and we all know how easy it is to control people when they are afraid. Regarding John and Mary’s “battle of the messy bathroom,” John tried to make Mary feel guilty about the clutter she created. In that way he hoped to control her behaviour so that she would be more neat and tidy. Why? So that there would be no mess to trigger his pain around his sense of being insignificant. At the same time it might also satisfy his old need to be important. He might have unconsciously reasoned that if Mary kept things neat for him, it would confirm that he was important to her. Meanwhile, Mary tried to make John feel guilty about playing his stereo too loud. If he felt bad, he might leave her alone about the bathroom and she wouldn’t have to feel her pain of being insignificant. Both of them were using anger to block out their pain, and make sure the other didn’t threaten their vulnerability again. It’s beyond my understanding what makes us think anger will accomplish these things, but what’s more amazing is how often we will keep resorting to anger when it is so obviously a useless tool for gaining happiness. The most important thing John and Mary’s anger blocked them from seeing was that at the root of the fight was a pain that both shared . It was the exact same pain of feeling unimportant. Like my colleague’s friends Ron and Betty, life was giving John and Mary a chance to revisit an old wound that had given birth to so many mistaken perceptions that they had about themselves, and nurse that wound with compassion and understanding.

愤怒的第二个好处是，它能通过让对方感到内疚来有效地控制其行为。当一个人感到内疚时，他们会本能地害怕即将到来的惩罚，而我们都知道，当人们感到恐惧时，控制他们是多么容易。就约翰和玛丽的“浴室脏乱之争”而言，约翰试图让玛丽为她造成的杂乱感到内疚。他希望以此来控制她的行为，让她更加整洁。为什么呢？这样就不会有杂乱的浴室来触发他因觉得自己微不足道而产生的痛苦。同时，这或许也能满足他长期以来渴望被重视的需求。他可能潜意识里认为，如果玛丽为他保持浴室整洁，就证明他在她心中很重要。与此同时，玛丽试图让约翰为他把音响开得太大声而感到内疚。如果他感到内疚，他或许就会不再纠缠她，让她不必再感受到那种因觉得自己微不足道而产生的痛苦。他们都试图用愤怒来麻痹自己的痛苦，确保对方不会再次触及自己的脆弱。我实在无法理解，为什么我们会认为愤怒能达到这些目的。更令人惊讶的是，明明愤怒显然无法带来快乐，我们却总是忍不住诉诸愤怒。约翰和玛丽的愤怒让他们看不到的最重要的一点是，争吵的根源在于他们共同的痛苦——那种觉得自己不重要的痛苦。就像我同事的朋友罗恩和贝蒂一样，生活给了约翰和玛丽一个机会，让他们重新审视那道曾经滋生了诸多自我误解的旧伤，并用同情和理解来抚慰它。

On the surface, it usually seems like the two combatants are on opposite sides, but all conflicts are motivated by one pain that is common to both sides. Once the two sides see that they are dealing with the exact same discomfort, the conflict begins to dissolve into understanding. Unfortunately, the willingness to face the pain is often a lot less accessible than the anger that is so easy to call upon for protection.

表面上看，冲突双方似乎立场对立，但所有冲突的根源都在于双方共同的痛苦。一旦双方意识到彼此承受着同样的痛苦，冲突便会逐渐消弭，走向理解。然而，不幸的是，直面痛苦的意愿往往远不如诉诸愤怒来寻求保护那样容易。

In a Power Struggle, anger can assume three modes of expression: attack, withdrawal, or passive aggression.

在权力斗争中，愤怒可以采取三种表现方式：攻击、退缩或被动攻击。

Attack is the overt, explicit expression of anger that can manifest as criticism, accusations, blame, threats, physical assault, ultimatums or just plain name-calling. However it comes out, there is no doubt that the person is angry, and wants you to suffer for the pain they believe you are causing them. I was once on vacation in Hawaii with my girlfriend, and we were deeply embroiled in a Power Struggle of the first magnitude. We did nothing, it seemed, except attack each other from morning until night. She would say that my bathing suit looked stupid, and I would retort that her entire being was stupid. She would attack my ability as an outdoorsman (“Don’t you have the brains to put up a simple tent?”), and I would attack her driving . She would insult my love making, and I would attack her driving. She became disgusted with my social ineptitude, and I told her that her driving sucked. What I lacked in imagination I made up for in sheer volume. The fighting reached critical mass when we were driving down a winding mountain road one rainy evening. We had been arguing off and on for about eight hours, when my girlfriend got an especially good shot past my defences. I was driving, so I was totally without an ingenious comeback. I was left with nothing else to do but slam on the gas pedal, turn to her and scream at the top of my lungs. At exactly the same moment she decided to scream at me. We were doing sixty miles an hour down a wet winding mountain road, screaming wordlessly in each other’s faces. We had run out of words, but we hadn’t run out of anger. To this day I don’t know how we didn’t get killed.

攻击是愤怒的公开、直接的表达，可以表现为批评、指责、责备、威胁、肢体攻击、最后通牒，或者仅仅是辱骂。无论以何种方式表现出来，毫无疑问，这个人是愤怒的，并且想要你为他们认为你给他们带来的痛苦付出代价。我曾经和女朋友在夏威夷度假，我们陷入了一场激烈的权力斗争。我们似乎除了从早到晚互相攻击之外什么也没做。她说我的泳衣看起来很蠢，我就反驳说她整个人都很蠢。她攻击我的户外运动能力（“你连搭个简单的帐篷都不会吗？”），我就攻击她的驾驶技术。她侮辱我的性技巧，我就攻击她的驾驶技术。她对我的社交能力感到厌恶，我就告诉她她的驾驶技术很烂。我虽然缺乏想象力，但我用大量的言语弥补了这一点。在一个雨夜，我们驱车行驶在蜿蜒的山路上，争吵达到了白热化。我们断断续续地争吵了大约八个小时，直到有一天，女友终于突破了我的防线，狠狠地回击了我。当时是我在开车，我根本想不出什么巧妙的反击。我别无选择，只能猛踩油门，转过身对着她声嘶力竭地咆哮。就在那一刻，她也开始对我大吼大叫。我们以每小时六十英里的速度在湿滑的蜿蜒山路上飞驰，彼此无声地对着对方咆哮。我们已经词穷，但怒火却丝毫未减。直到今天，我仍然不知道我们是怎么死里逃生的。

Later I realized that what we say when we are attacking someone is of little relevance. We use the words to be hurtful, while logically justifying the attack, but the attack itself isn’t logical. It is simply violence used to defend ourselves. All attacks are carried out in self-defence.

后来我意识到，我们攻击他人时所说的话其实无关紧要。我们用言语伤害他人，并试图在逻辑上为攻击行为辩解，但攻击本身并不合乎逻辑。它仅仅是出于自卫而采取的暴力行为。所有攻击都是出于自卫。

Withdrawal is a quiet form of anger, and my past favourite. Do not be fooled by the partner who is sitting quietly while the other violently rants and raves. There can be as much violent intent in silence as there is in open assault. In the example of Betty and Ron, it may have seemed on the surface that Ron was just some poor husband who had to suffer the tirades of a nagging wife. However, Ron was using a mixture of rebellion and indifference to fuel his wife’s rage, and petulance to make her look like the bad guy with him as the innocent victim.

退缩是一种隐忍的愤怒，也是我过去最常用的表达方式。不要被一方默默忍受另一方激烈咆哮的外表所迷惑。沉默中可能蕴含着与公开攻击同样强烈的暴力意图。以贝蒂和罗恩为例，表面上看，罗恩似乎只是个可怜的丈夫，不得不忍受妻子的唠叨。然而，罗恩却巧妙地运用反叛和冷漠来激起妻子的怒火，并用任性来让她看起来像个坏人，而自己则成了无辜的受害者。

Withdrawal used to be my favourite weapon because it was so versatile. I could withdraw and pout to show my partner how cruel she had been to me, thus making her feel bad about herself. I could withdraw and maintain a cold angry look, to inform my partner that I was angry but she was not worth wasting words on. My non-verbal message was “Just screw off and die.” I could also maintain a withdrawal pose of cool indifference; I could look right through the person, my blank face coldly stating that her existence was of no importance to me anymore and she could never hurt me again.

曾经，冷漠是我最爱的武器，因为它用途广泛。我可以冷漠地撅嘴，向伴侣展示她对我有多么残忍，让她感到羞愧。我可以冷漠地保持愤怒的表情，告诉她我很生气，但她不值得我浪费口舌。我的非语言信息是“滚蛋吧，去死吧”。我还可以摆出一副冷漠疏离的姿态；我可以视而不见，面无表情地冷冷地告诉她，她的存在对我来说已经无关紧要，她再也伤害不了我了。

Another great one was my “beaten into withdrawal” look. I would sink into a dark cloud of depression, informing my partner and the world at large that I had been wounded enough by their heartless cruelty—so please, just leave me alone to suffer. Whatever method of withdrawal is used, the external result is always the same: a wordless distancing of yourself from the person who seemed to cause you pain.

另一个绝妙的招数是我那副“饱受折磨、被迫退缩”的模样。我会陷入深深的抑郁之中，向我的伴侣和全世界宣告：我已经被他们冷酷无情的残忍伤透了心——所以，求求你们，让我一个人独自承受痛苦吧。无论采用何种退缩方式，最终的结果都是一样的：一种无声的疏离，与那个似乎让你痛苦的人保持着距离。

Passive aggression is a form of guerrilla warfare. You pretend to not be terribly bothered by the other person’s behaviour, but your remarks are infused with subtle criticisms, sarcasm, judgments, teasing or complaints. Another expression of passive aggression is to act extremely hurt, even to the point of tears, but never outright accuse the other person of deliberately hurting you. Your obvious portrayal of the innocent victim will leave your partner feeling like a villain or bully; and since you’re not actually accusing them of doing anything wrong, they don’t know what to defend themselves from. For instance, let’s look at a situation with a couple named Jamal and Mavis. Married three years, this is the second time that Jamal has forgotten Mavis’s birthday. When he enters the house, Mavis is wiping her red eyes with a tissue, and blowing her nose:

被动攻击是一种游击战。你假装对对方的行为毫不在意，但你的言辞中却暗藏着微妙的批评、讽刺、评判、戏谑或抱怨。被动攻击的另一种表现是装作极度受伤，甚至哭出来，但绝不会直接指责对方故意伤害你。你刻意扮演无辜受害者，会让你的伴侣觉得自己像个恶人或恶霸；而且由于你并没有真正指责他们做错了什么，他们也不知道该如何反驳。例如，我们来看一对名叫贾马尔和梅维斯的夫妇。他们结婚三年了，这已经是贾马尔第二次忘记梅维斯的生日了。当他进屋时，梅维斯正用纸巾擦着通红的眼睛，擤着鼻子：

Jamal: What’s the matter, honey?

贾马尔：亲爱的，你怎么了？

Mavis: (sniffling) Nothing. I’m all right.

梅维斯：（抽泣）没事。我很好。

Jamal: Did something go wrong at work? Is it because I’m late coming home? I told you the meeting was going to run late, remember?

贾马尔：工作上出什么事了吗？是不是因为我回家晚了？我跟你说过会议会晚点，记得吗？

Mavis: It’s not any of that. (sniff) Really, I’ll be okay.

梅维斯：都不是那些事。（抽泣）真的，我会没事的。

Jamal: Well tell me what it is. C’mon, please…

贾马尔：那你告诉我到底是什么。拜托，快说……

Mavis: It’s nothing, Jamal, Really, it’s not important.

梅维斯：没什么，贾马尔，真的，这不重要。

Jamal: Well, okay. If you’re sure then—

贾马尔：好吧。如果你确定的话——

Mavis: It’s just that it was my birthday today, and I thought we could go out for dinner.

梅维斯：只是因为今天是我的生日，我想我们可以出去吃顿饭。

Jamal: Your birthday! Oh no, not again!

贾马尔：你的生日！哦不，又来了！

Mavis: Yes, the second year in a row. But really, I understand you’ve been really busy at work, and you have a lot on your mind.

梅维斯：是的，连续第二年了。不过说真的，我知道你工作很忙，而且肯定有很多事情要操心。

Jamal: I’m really sorry, baby. But look, let’s go out on Saturday and celebrate your birthday, huh?

贾马尔：宝贝，我真的很抱歉。但是，我们周六出去庆祝你的生日吧，好吗？

Mavis: I can’t, I promised Mary I’d help her move on Saturday.

梅维斯：我不能，我答应过玛丽周六帮她搬家。

Jamal: How about Friday?

贾马尔：星期五怎么样？

Mavis: No, I don’t want to take away your poker night with your friends. No, let’s just forget it. I’ll get over it. [Just as Jamal gets up to put away his coat, Mavis adds] Just give me a few days.

梅维斯：不，我不想破坏你和朋友们的扑克之夜。不，我们还是算了吧。我会想通的。[贾马尔起身去放外套时，梅维斯补充道] 给我几天时间。

Jamal: [sitting back down] Honey, let me make this up to you. Please!

贾马尔：（重新坐下）亲爱的，让我补偿你吧。求你了！

Mavis: There’s nothing to make up, Jamal. I understand — you had an important meeting. That’s all there is to it. It’s only my birthday, it’s no big deal.

梅维斯：没什么好弥补的，贾马尔。我明白——你有个重要的会议。仅此而已。这只是我的生日，没什么大不了的。

Jamal: [hanging his head] I really feel like shit.

贾马尔：（低着头）我感觉糟透了。

Mavis: [allows herself a small, secret smile]

梅维斯：（露出一丝不易察觉的微笑）

Now you may be asking yourself after reading this, what’s the big deal here? Jamal was a jerk for forgetting Mavis’ birthday, and she was letting him know as nicely as she could. And that is the whole key to Passive Aggression. It almost never appears harmful on the surface, but if you look closely at the intent, you will see that Mavis was hurt. To protect herself from feeling deeper pain, she chose to secretly attack her lover, reducing him to the same status as excrement. That way she makes her pain his responsibility, so that she doesn’t have to deal with it. Although this does not look like the classic Power Struggle, such as we see on films and TV, it is still an attempt to avoid pain and control the other person by making him/her feel guilty. And that is a key intention behind anger: to make someone else feel guilty, and therefore responsible for the pain that you are feeling inside yourself . It then becomes their responsibility to make you happy.

读完之后，你可能会问自己，这有什么大不了的？贾马尔忘了梅维斯的生日，他确实有点混蛋，而梅维斯只是尽可能委婉地表达了自己的不满。这就是被动攻击的关键所在。它表面上几乎不会造成伤害，但如果你仔细分析其背后的意图，就会发现梅维斯其实受到了伤害。为了避免自己承受更深的痛苦，她选择暗中攻击自己的爱人，把他贬低得如同粪便一般。这样一来，她就把自己的痛苦转嫁给了他，从而逃避了痛苦。虽然这看起来不像我们在电影和电视中看到的那种典型的权力斗争，但它仍然是一种试图通过让对方感到内疚来逃避痛苦并控制对方的手段。而这正是愤怒背后的一个关键意图：让别人感到内疚，从而让他们为自己内心的痛苦负责。这样一来，让你快乐就成了他们的责任。

In the long run it doesn’t matter what form of anger you employ or have employed against you. If you feel angry, that anger is an attempt to insulate you from the pain beneath. If we could be honest and look at the pain, we might see that the old pain is asking us for acceptance, compassion and understanding. If we choose to attack or withdraw from our partner, we may not have to feel the pain, but we will not heal it or the limiting beliefs it fuels in us.

从长远来看，你对伴侣使用或曾经使用过的愤怒形式并不重要。如果你感到愤怒，那其实是一种试图将你与内心深处的痛苦隔离开来的尝试。如果我们能够坦诚地面对痛苦，或许会发现，旧日的伤痛其实是在寻求我们的接纳、同情和理解。如果我们选择攻击或疏远伴侣，或许可以暂时逃避痛苦，但却无法治愈它，也无法消除它在我们心中滋生的种种限制性信念。

Finally, there is one more reason that anger is such a popular tool when old pain, disguised as conflict, begins to arise. Anger allows us the marvellous opportunity to experience…

最后，当旧伤以冲突的形式再次浮现时，愤怒之所以如此受欢迎，还有另一个原因。愤怒让我们有机会体验……

***

BEING RIGHT!

我是对的！

———————————

“Would you rather be right or happy?”

你宁愿正确还是快乐？

—A Course in Miracles

——《奇迹课程》

As far as I’m concerned, if you don’t feel very powerful in a certain situation and you want to avoid experiencing the discomfort of inadequacy or insecurity, nothing beats being right for a quick fix. All you need to do is criticize, blame, judge, or “make wrong,” fuel one of these attacks with your righteous rage, and you’ll be pumped up with adrenaline in no time. You immediately feel like Clark Kent after he’s walked into a phone booth and donned the funny long johns. I remember a time when I was chastised by a friend for something I did that was obviously wrong. 24 The more he berated me, the worse I felt, and soon I was little more than a quivering mass of guilt and shame. Now these feelings are probably two of the least personally acceptable of all feelings, so needless to say I was in a wretched state. Suddenly, he made a slip, and my survival instincts leapt at the opportunity to weasel out of my pain. He started with the phrase, “As sure as the sun rises…” but before he could further berate my incompetence, stupidity, and selfishness, I angrily interrupted: “The sun doesn’t rise, stupid! The earth rotates! If you’re going to have an intelligent conversation, at least say something that makes sense. All you’re doing is making up stuff as you go along!” I continued in that vein for a couple of minutes, gleefully enjoying the feeling of righteousness while overwhelming the guy with my intellectual stick handling. Soon we were no longer talking about my mistake; instead I had him defending his own character deficiencies, most of which I was making up on the spot.

在我看来，如果你在某种情况下感到无力，又想避免体验那种无能为力或不安全感带来的不适，那么没有什么比“证明自己是对的”更能快速解决问题了。你只需要批评、指责、评判或“指出错误”，用你义愤填膺的怒火来煽动这些攻击，你就会立刻肾上腺素飙升。你会立刻感觉自己像克拉克·肯特走进电话亭，穿上那件滑稽的连体睡衣一样。我记得有一次，我因为做了一件明显错误的事情而被朋友责备。<sup>24</sup> 他越责备我，我的感觉就越糟糕，很快我就变成了一团颤抖的内疚和羞耻。这两种感觉大概是我个人最无法接受的两种感觉，所以不用说，我当时的处境糟透了。突然，他失言了，我的求生本能立刻抓住机会，想方设法摆脱痛苦。他以一句“就像太阳升起一样……”开头，但还没等他进一步指责我的无能、愚蠢和自私，我就愤怒地打断了他：“太阳根本不会升起，蠢货！地球在自转！如果你想进行一场有意义的对话，至少说点有道理的话。你只会胡说八道！”我就这样滔滔不绝地讲了几分钟，得意洋洋地享受着这种正义感，同时用我的智力优势彻底压制住了他。很快，我们不再讨论我的错误；取而代之的是，他开始为自己的人格缺陷辩解，而这些缺陷大部分都是我即兴编造的。

When you are trying to avoid your pain, just make yourself right about something—anything—that can make someone or something look wrong. If I can make my partner wrong, I can make myself right. Feeling right overrides the pain while my anger can keep my pride fuelled and my awareness hovering above any uncomfortable feelings. And don’t worry about that old saying: “Whom the gods would destroy, they first make proud.” If the gods try to destroy you, just get mad and make them wrong. Righteousness can even keep the gods at bay. 25

当你试图逃避痛苦时，就让自己在某件事上——任何事——显得正确，只要能让别人或事看起来不对劲就行。如果我能让我的伴侣显得错，我就能让自己显得对。正确的感觉能压倒痛苦，而我的愤怒则能让我保持骄傲，让我的意识凌驾于任何不适感之上。别担心那句古老的谚语：“神欲毁灭之人，必先使其骄傲。”如果神想要毁灭你，那就愤怒起来，让他们显得错。正义甚至可以让神明退避三舍。<sup>25</sup>

It’s been my experience that the flames of anger will die out in a few minutes unless you are feeding them with gasoline. Therefore you have to keep finding things wrong with your partner, and justifying your attacks on him/her with more righteous rationalizations. 26 But that’s a small price to pay to stay safe from the guilt, shame, and pain you have been carrying around for years. Your righteous anger can maintain your ignorance right up to death’s door if you want it to.

我的经验是，除非你火上浇油，否则愤怒的火焰会在几分钟内熄灭。因此，你必须不断地挑剔伴侣的毛病，并用更冠冕堂皇的理由来为你的攻击辩解。26 但为了摆脱多年来一直背负的内疚、羞耻和痛苦，这点代价微不足道。如果你愿意，你的义愤可以让你一直蒙昧无知到生命尽头。

Of course, if you want your relationship to actually function and flow in a loving, healthy direction, you may want to consider being responsible for your anger. It’s not as safe as hiding behind your righteousness, but taking the risk of 100% accountability will allow you to face your anger without throwing it on someone else, and discover what important feeling that anger is keeping you from experiencing. Being willing to peacefully confront the important feelings within you, no matter how uncomfortable, gives you the chance to reach even deeper, to more peaceful, loving feelings. It has been my experience that simply giving any feeling my full attention, no matter how painful it is, alleviates the pain and transforms the feeling into a more suitable experience. To do this consistently, a commitment is called for. I call it…

当然，如果你希望你们的关系真正健康发展，朝着充满爱的方向前进，你或许应该考虑为自己的愤怒负责。这虽然不如躲在正义的背后安全，但承担百分之百的责任能让你直面自己的愤怒，而不是把它发泄到别人身上，并发现愤怒究竟阻碍了你体验哪些重要的情感。愿意平和地面对内心深处的重要情感，无论多么不舒服，都能让你有机会触及更深层次、更平和、更充满爱的情感。我的经验是，只要全神贯注地关注任何一种感受，无论它多么痛苦，都能减轻痛苦，并将这种感受转化为更合适的体验。要做到这一点，需要一种承诺。我称之为……

***

THE LOVE INTENTION

爱的意图

———————————

“Love will find a way.”

“爱总会找到出路。”

—Proverb

-谚语

A basic premise in modern-day therapy is that, at any given time, and regardless of the circumstances, human beings are always doing their best. On the surface it may not appear to be the case, but all the clients I have met who were going through tough times always had in their hearts a desire to bring peace to the situation. This heart’s calling—often an unconscious desire—I call the Love Intention. The Love Intention is inspired by the urging of the Soul to learn how to truly love ourselves and each other. If we become aware of this intention, which exists in all situations, we have a chance to see the pain we are experiencing as an opportunity to grow beyond our present limitations. Without this understanding of pain’s purpose, every time it arises in our relationship it will throw us into a struggle for control by fight, flight, freeze or faint. When old pain is coming up, disguised as a difference of opinion, our subconscious patterns and beliefs might drive us, for instance, to say something nasty and stomp out of the room. On the other hand, the Love Intention would have us rise above that impulsive nastiness and be responsible for our discomfort, withholding blame or accusation and expressing words of understanding. In this way we become more peaceful, accepting individuals.

现代心理治疗的一个基本前提是，无论何时何地，无论境遇如何，人类总是在尽力而为。表面上看来或许并非如此，但我遇到的所有经历困境的来访者，内心深处都渴望为现状带来和平。这种来自内心的召唤——通常是一种无意识的渴望——我称之为“爱的意图”。“爱的意图”源于灵魂的召唤，促使我们学习如何真正地爱自己和他人。如果我们意识到这种存在于所有境遇中的意图，我们就有机会将正在经历的痛苦视为超越当前局限的成长契机。如果我们不理解痛苦的意义，那么每当痛苦在我们的关系中出现时，它都会让我们陷入一场争夺控制权的斗争，让我们做出战斗、逃跑、僵住或晕厥等反应。当旧伤复发，伪装成意见分歧时，我们潜意识的模式和信念可能会驱使我们说出一些难听的话，然后愤然离去。另一方面，爱的意图会让我们超越那种冲动的恶意，为自己的不适负责，不去责备或指责，而是表达理解。这样，我们就能变得更加平和、包容。

In the heat of a fight, it is always difficult to remember that the discomfort we are experiencing has its roots deep in our past. Yet it is vital to always remember that we are never upset for the reasons we think, otherwise we will continue to make our partners our enemies. 27 But why does it only come up with certain people at certain times? If it has nothing to do with our present relationships, why is it interfering with our lives now?

在激烈的争吵中，我们总是很难想起，我们所感受到的不适其实根源于我们深厚的过往经历。然而，至关重要的是，我们必须始终记住，我们生气的原因并非我们所认为的那样，否则我们只会继续与伴侣为敌。<sup>27</sup> 但为什么这种情绪只会在特定的人和特定的时间出现呢？如果它与我们目前的关系无关，为什么它会影响我们现在的生活呢？

A relationship is the best environment for an individual to heal his or her old psychological and emotional wounds. There are a lot of jokes about the painful ordeal of relationships (Q: Why do singles live longer than married people? A: Because they want to). But if we really look at relationships with an open mind and through the eyes of the heart, we would see them as a truly spiritual, healing path, and not the path of a masochist.

恋爱关系是个人疗愈过往心理和情感创伤的最佳环境。关于恋爱关系的痛苦考验，有很多玩笑（问：为什么单身人士比已婚人士寿命更长？答：因为他们想这样）。但如果我们真正敞开心扉，用心去看待恋爱关系，就会发现它是一条真正具有疗愈作用的精神之路，而非受虐狂的道路。

So why does the pain we experienced in our past stay with us over the years and not eventually just go away? Doesn’t time heal all wounds? Why doesn’t the pain go away in time? It would, I believe, if we respected its real purpose and responded to it in the most appropriate way. In my experience, pain has always preceded a step forward in consciousness, self-knowledge and emotional maturity. I resisted my pain, and buried it in the basement of the subconscious, because I was not ready to take the step or learn the lesson that was being offered. Until the step is taken, the pain will remain. Through Power Struggle, I attempt to make it the responsibility of the other person, mainly because I sense that my subconscious pain is too big for me. When I was younger I saw it as a threat to my wellbeing, if not my very life, and I carry that impression with me to the present day.

那么，为什么我们过去经历的痛苦会伴随我们多年，最终却不会消失呢？时间难道不能治愈一切伤痛吗？为什么痛苦不会随着时间流逝而消散？我相信，如果我们尊重痛苦的真正意义，并以最恰当的方式回应它，痛苦终会消失。以我的经验来看，痛苦总是意识觉醒、自我认知和情感成熟的先兆。我抗拒痛苦，把它埋藏在潜意识深处，因为我还没有准备好迈出那一步，也没有准备好接受它所提供的教训。除非我迈出那一步，否则痛苦将一直存在。通过权力斗争，我试图将痛苦转嫁给别人，主要是因为我感觉潜意识里的痛苦对我来说太过沉重。年轻的时候，我把它视为对我的身心健康，甚至是生命本身的威胁，这种印象一直延续至今。

To grow, one must go through pain. As children we simply reacted—understandably so—and so we did not grow in self-awareness. This growth might be easier if we did not get pain mixed up with suffering. At times I’ve seen within myself the capacity to transcend physical and emotional pain simply by focusing my heart and mind on something greater than the pain itself, while at the same time experiencing the pain fully. Choosing love, Truth, or the light of my soul and reaching for it with willingness and determination allowed the grace of life to lift me through my hurt to a place of peace, and a greater sense of myself. When I did not make that choice, I was left to struggle against the pain, the result being a long period of suffering before I could eventually numb myself to the hurt. I often assume that when pain arises my only options are to struggle and suffer with it, or else manipulate my partner into taking my pain away. My present relationship provides me with the opportunity to approach my past—and present—pain and in the face of it, choose something greater so that I might grow to know who I truly am. This opportunity is the Love Intention that exists within each and every Power Struggle.

成长需要经历痛苦。孩提时代，我们只是被动地做出反应——这可以理解——因此我们并没有在自我认知方面有所成长。如果我们不把痛苦与苦难混为一谈，这种成长或许会更容易。有时，我发现自己有能力超越身心的痛苦，只需将心神专注于比痛苦本身更伟大的事物，同时又全然地体验痛苦。选择爱、真理或灵魂之光，并以意愿和决心去追求它，生命的恩典便能将我从伤痛中托起，抵达平静之地，并让我更深刻地认识自己。如果我没有做出这样的选择，我只能与痛苦抗争，结果便是经历了一段漫长的痛苦时期，最终才能麻木自己，不再受其折磨。我常常认为，当痛苦来临时，我唯一的选择就是与之抗争，忍受痛苦，或者操纵伴侣来替我分担痛苦。而我现在的这段感情，让我有机会直面过去和现在的痛苦，并在痛苦面前选择更伟大的事物，从而更好地认识真正的自己。这个机会就是存在于每一次权力斗争中的爱的意图。

***

THE SHORTEST DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS OF YOU

你两点之间的最短距离

———————————

# ↩

“They shall travel far until the two become as one.”

“他们将远行，直到二人合二为一。”

—Paul Stokey, “The Wedding Song”

——保罗·斯托基，《婚礼之歌》

So far, we have looked at the pain that causes relationship conflicts, the way we try to control and suppress that pain through Power Struggles, the purpose of the pain’s existence, and the Love Intention that secretly resides behind this particular stage of the relationship. At this point I would like to share some insights on basic relationship dynamics that may be of vital importance to the understanding of anyone on this path. After that I would like to offer some concise, simple methods for moving through relationship conflicts that will enable us to confront our personal pain like the truly great people we are and reach beyond it to a higher level of relationship and love.

到目前为止，我们已经探讨了导致关系冲突的痛苦根源，我们如何通过权力斗争来控制和压抑这种痛苦，痛苦存在的意义，以及隐藏在关系特定阶段背后的爱的意图。接下来，我想分享一些关于基本关系动力学的见解，这些见解对于任何走在这条道路上的人都至关重要。之后，我想提供一些简洁易行的方法来化解关系冲突，使我们能够像真正伟大的人一样直面个人的痛苦，并超越痛苦，达到更高层次的关系和爱。

A further challenge that we face in resolving conflicts is the way two people will polarize over an issue. For the first month after my wife and I moved into our newly built house, I was amazed that we could not agree on anything! The disagreement over the angle of the sofa was just one of hundreds of issues that came up on which we held rigidly opposing views. Fortunately I teach about this stuff, so I was aware that two people in any kind of relationship will tend to go from somewhat opposed to completely opposite viewpoints on most life issues. Even knowing this, however, I was still impressed by how strongly these viewpoints could be maintained once the energy of Power Struggle entered into the situation. We had to keep reminding ourselves that we were merely seeing things from one of many perspectives, and that neither of us was right. In all conflicts, both parties are holding a point of view equally distant from the central point of conflict.

我们在解决冲突时面临的另一个挑战是，两个人往往会在某个问题上意见截然相反。我和妻子搬进新房后的第一个月，我惊讶地发现我们竟然什么都无法达成一致！沙发角度的分歧只是我们持完全相反观点的数百个问题之一。幸运的是，我教授这方面的课程，所以我知道，在任何关系中，两个人对大多数生活问题的看法都会从略有分歧发展到完全对立。即便如此，我仍然对权力斗争的能量介入后，这些观点能够如此坚定地维持下去感到惊讶。我们不得不不断提醒自己，我们只是从众多视角之一看待问题，而且我们谁都不是完全正确的。在所有冲突中，双方的观点都与冲突的核心点相距甚远。

Imagine that you are sitting across from your partner at a table. In the middle of the table, at exactly the same distance from both of you, is a hat. On your side the hat is red. On your partner’s side the hat is blue. You cannot see any part of the blue, nor can she/he see the red. If asked to describe what you see, your description would be different from your partner’s. The problems start in a Power Struggle when both of you are locked into your point of view, convinced that the other was looking at the hat the wrong way (“What are you? Colour blind? Any idiot could see that it’s red.” “That’s right, an idiot would see that! A normal person would see that it’s blue!”).

想象一下，你和你的伴侣坐在桌子对面。桌子中央，你们两人距离相同的位置放着一顶帽子。在你这边，帽子是红色的；在你伴侣这边，帽子是蓝色的。你看不到任何蓝色，你的伴侣也看不到红色。如果让你描述你看到的景象，你的描述肯定和你的伴侣的不一样。问题就出在权力斗争上，你们都固执己见，认为对方看帽子的方式不对（“你是色盲吗？谁都能看出它是红色的。”“没错，谁都能看出它是红色的！正常人肯定都觉得它是蓝色的！”）。

In truth of course, both of you are simply perceiving things from your own angle, insisting that you are right. But if you left your position and saw it from your partner’s point of view, you could combine it with your own and come up with the truth—it’s a red and blue hat! 28

事实上，你们俩都只是从各自的角度看待问题，并坚持认为自己是对的。但如果你们能跳出自己的立场，从对方的角度来看待问题，就能将两者结合起来，从而得出真相——原来是一顶红蓝相间的帽子！28

The problem with the position-taking in a Power Struggle is complicated by the fact that we are never upset for the reasons we think, and therefore whatever we are arguing about is never what we are really concerned about . But try telling this to a couple who are in the heat of a fight. Obviously they are suffering. If they were not wrestling with their pain they would be feeling peaceful and happy, and thus treating each other with love and respect. But when the pain begins to emerge, subconscious alarms go off, warning both of them that if they don’t push the other away they will be forced to suffer. Therefore they pick a less threatening issue and take opposing positions on it, locking themselves into a fight that ignores the real problem. This pushing-away tends to accentuate the polarities that already exist within all relationships.

权力斗争中立场选择的问题在于，我们并非总是因为自己认为的原因而生气，因此，我们争论的焦点往往并非我们真正关心的问题。但试着把这话告诉一对正在激烈争吵的情侣。显然，他们正在承受痛苦。如果他们不与痛苦抗争，他们本应感到平静和快乐，从而彼此以爱和尊重相待。但当痛苦开始显现时，潜意识里的警报就会响起，警告他们如果不推开对方，就会被迫承受痛苦。因此，他们会选择一个威胁性较小的问题，并就此采取对立立场，让自己陷入一场忽略真正问题的争吵之中。这种推开的做法往往会加剧所有关系中原本就存在的对立面。

If there were no conflict the polarities in a relationship could work together more or less in harmony. Just as a battery with only one pole doesn’t work, and no coin would exist without both a head and a tail, relationships would not exist unless there was a positive partner and a negative partner. Here is a chart that lays out the basic characteristics of the two types of people that make up one relationship.

如果没有冲突，一段关系中的两极就能或多或少地和谐共处。就像只有一极的电池无法工作，硬币也只有正面和反面一样，一段关系也离不开积极和消极的双方。下图列出了构成一段关系的两种人的基本特征。

Positive

积极的

Negative

消极的

Optimist

乐天派

Solution oriented

以解决问题为导向

Denies emotions

否认情绪

Producer

制片人

Praising

赞扬

Makes a good president

他会成为一位好总统

Loves everything

热爱一切

Broad perceptions

广泛的认知

Overlooks faults

忽略了缺陷

Expansive

广阔的

Tends towards generalities

倾向于概括

Pessimist (call themselves “realists”)

悲观主义者（自称“现实主义者”）

Problem finder

问题查找器

Indulges in emotions

沉溺于情绪

Director

导演

Critical

批判的

Makes a good vice president

是个不错的副总裁

More discriminating

更具辨别力

Penetrating perceptions

深刻的洞察力

Focuses on faults

关注缺陷
