收缩

Tends towards details

倾向于细节

It is really unfortunate that the Negative has such a bad public image, because they are of great value to this world. The Positives built the factories, but it was the Negatives that made us aware of the dangers of pollution, poor labour conditions and dangers to personal safety in the workplace. The Positives may have improved the quality of life in developed countries, but it was the Negatives that demanded something be done about the poor living conditions in other parts of the world. Without our Negative aspect, human beings would not be motivated to improve. On the other hand, if not for the Positive, we could well find ourselves steeped in the misery and negativity of unsolvable problems. It is the Positive that sees what’s possible, and has the energy to make the possible a reality. The Negative is the course corrector.

负面因素的公众形象如此糟糕，实在令人惋惜，因为它们对这个世界有着巨大的价值。正面因素建造了工厂，但正是负面因素让我们意识到污染的危害、恶劣的劳动条件以及工作场所的人身安全隐患。正面因素或许改善了发达国家的生活质量，但正是负面因素促使人们关注世界其他地区恶劣的生活条件。如果没有负面因素，人类就不会有进步的动力。另一方面，如果没有正面因素，我们很可能深陷于无法解决的问题带来的痛苦和消极之中。正是正面因素看到了可能性，并拥有将可能性变为现实的能量。负面因素则是航向修正者。

In personal relationships, it’s the negative that alerts the couple to an upcoming problem, sometimes days in advance of its arrival. The negative, being more emotionally attuned, will sense the emergence of an old pain making its way up into consciousness. They won’t necessarily recognize it for what it is though. When I’m the Negative in the relationship, I won’t alert my partner by saying, “Oh, oh, honey, I sense an old childhood pain emerging for us to heal!” Rather, I’m more tempted to say something like, “who keeps leaving all the goddamn lights on in this house? Do you think we have our own private generator in the backyard?” 29 That’s because the Negative may be subtly aware of the imminent crisis but is not necessarily willing to confront it, being as afraid of pain as the Positive counterpart. Negatives tend to feel many emotions, but not the most important feelings. In the above example, my wife would be the Positive. So does she immediately realize that my complaints are a signal about approaching old pain? Does she think, “Oh, oh, my honey is complaining about the lights. He must be sensing that the opportunity for a major healing of old wounds is about to be offered to us”? I’m afraid not. Her tendency would more likely be to run around and turn off all the lights—maybe even the electrical breakers for good measure—and light a few cheap candles to make her Negative hubby happy again. This is because Positives wish to avoid unpleasant situations at all costs, even if the unpleasant situations are screaming in their faces. They will respond to their Negative partner’s discomfort by removing the physical irritant, hoping that the whole problem will magically pass them by. If they can’t remove the irritant, they will deny its existence. A Positive could find himself sitting in the middle of a battlefield and respond to his Negative buddy’s terror with a simple, “Bombs? What bombs? Just ignore them and they’ll go away!”

在人际关系中，往往是消极的一方会提前几天就提醒伴侣即将出现问题。消极的一方情感更加敏锐，能够感知到旧伤正在浮现，逐渐进入意识层面。但他们未必能意识到问题的本质。如果我是关系中的消极方，我不会对伴侣说：“哦，亲爱的，我感觉我们之间有一段童年的伤痛需要疗愈！”相反，我更可能说的是：“谁老是把家里的灯都开着？你以为我们后院有私人发电机吗？”<sup>29</sup> 这是因为消极方可能隐约意识到危机即将到来，但未必愿意面对，因为他们和积极方一样害怕痛苦。消极方往往能感受到很多情绪，但唯独无法感受到最重要的那些。在上面的例子中，我的妻子就是积极方。那么，她会立刻意识到我的抱怨是在暗示旧伤即将出现吗？她会想：“哦，哦，我的爱人又在抱怨灯光了。他一定是感觉到了，我们即将迎来一个弥合旧伤的机会”吗？恐怕不会。她更有可能的做法是赶紧把所有的灯都关掉——甚至为了保险起见，可能还会把总闸也关掉——然后点上几根廉价的蜡烛，好让她的消极老公重新开心起来。这是因为积极的人总是想方设法避免不愉快的情况，即使这些不愉快的情况就在眼前。他们会通过移除刺激物来回应消极伴侣的不适，希望问题能奇迹般地消失。如果无法移除刺激物，他们就会否认它的存在。一个积极的人可能会发现自己身处战场中央，却对消极朋友的恐惧轻描淡写地说：“炸弹？什么炸弹？别理它们，它们自己就会消失！”

Since becoming aware of these polarities in relationships, I am convinced that Negatives would spend their time in heaven looking for dirt, while Positives would build rocking chairs in hell to get a comfy seat close to the fire.

自从意识到人际关系中的这些两极对立之后，我确信消极的人会在天堂里寻找污垢，而积极的人会在地狱里建造摇椅，以便在火堆旁找到一个舒适的座位。

In general, the polarities work pretty well in a relationship as long as both partners are willing to respect each other’s perceptions and accept the other’s input. The Negative will bring a problem into the light, and the Positive, after listening openly, will come up with a solution. The Negative will then pick out the problems with that solution and the Positive will refine it, coming up with a more workable and realistic answer to the problem. This process will go back and forth until the most satisfactory solution is uncovered. At the same time, you will also find the Negative becoming more optimistic and the Positive becoming more realistic. The relationship thus achieves a harmonious balance.

一般来说，只要双方都愿意尊重彼此的看法并接受对方的意见，这种两极分化的关系就能很好地运作。消极的一方会指出问题所在，而积极的那一方在认真倾听后会提出解决方案。之后，消极的一方会指出这个方案的不足之处，而积极的那一方则会对其进行改进，从而提出一个更切实可行、更现实的答案。这个过程会反复进行，直到找到最令人满意的解决方案。与此同时，你会发现消极的一方变得更加乐观，而积极的那一方则变得更加务实。最终，这段关系会达到一种和谐的平衡。

However, when an old wound begins to emerge, and the temptation to fight increases, the differences between the polarities is magnified and the desire to resist the pain results in mutual distancing from each other. This can begin weeks before any actual fighting occurs. After a particularly wonderful couple of weeks with my wife, I will notice that we are drifting slowly and subtly away from each other, neither of us aware of the moment when the wonderful feelings begin to dissolve. We are not angry or fighting with each other, but if I look very closely I will recognize that we are pushing each other away. Positives push away by becoming distant from their feelings, though they often appear cheerful and optimistic on the outside—a good enough act to fool even themselves. They may act detached, disinterested, or may even seem to be loving and caring, but they are not feeling love and concern because they are simply not feeling much of anything. Negatives push away by focusing on a problem that they perceive is affecting the relationship and dwelling on the emotions that this problem brings up—usually angry, irritating, or depressing emotions. Often, the problem on which the Negative focuses is not directly related to their partner’s character or behaviour. A Negative might begin to comment on the money situation, the repairs needed on the house, the barking of the next-door neighbour’s dog, or even the decay of the social structure in the nation. Put simply, the Positive attempts to avoid pain by denying its very existence, whereas the Negative will avoid it by reacting to the irritations and blowing them out of proportion, thereby distracting themselves from the real issue.

然而，当旧伤复发，争吵的冲动加剧时，双方的差异会被放大，而抗拒痛苦的欲望最终导致彼此疏远。这种情况可能在实际争吵发生前几周就开始了。比如，和妻子度过了几个特别美好的星期后，我会注意到我们正缓慢而隐晦地疏远彼此，我们都没有意识到那些美好的感觉是如何开始消逝的。我们并没有生气或争吵，但如果我仔细观察，就会发现我们正在互相推开。积极的人会通过疏远自己的感受来推开对方，尽管他们表面上往往显得开朗乐观——这种伪装足以欺骗他们自己。他们可能表现得冷漠、漠不关心，甚至看起来充满爱意和关怀，但他们感受不到爱和关心，因为他们内心深处几乎没有任何感觉。消极者会通过关注他们认为影响关系的问题，并沉溺于这个问题引发的情绪——通常是愤怒、烦躁或沮丧——来逃避现实。通常，消极者关注的问题与伴侣的性格或行为并无直接关联。他们可能会开始评论经济状况、房屋维修、邻居家狗的吠叫，甚至是国家社会结构的衰败。简而言之，积极者试图通过否认痛苦的存在来逃避痛苦，而消极者则会通过对琐事做出反应并夸大其词来逃避痛苦，从而转移自己对真正问题的注意力。

Sooner or later, that ancient pain within us keeps moving upward, begging for attention. Eventually push comes to shove, and the Power Struggle, which has been brewing for some time, begins in earnest. It always starts with a “situation” that has become intolerable for the Negative. Due to a very human tendency to react quickly, people rarely see that all situations are neutral. Your partner forgetting to pick up your dry cleaning is neither good nor bad, neither right nor wrong. Your boyfriend spending too much time with his friends doesn’t mean anything one way or the other. Until you give the situation meaning, it is absolutely neutral. Your interpretation of the situation determines whether it will be a problem or not. It is the emerging of an old pain that influences one’s negative interpretation. I have developed a model that describes the journey that relationships take, assuming that the relationship is functioning in at least a somewhat healthy fashion:

迟早，我们内心深处那份古老的伤痛会不断涌现，渴望得到关注。最终，矛盾激化，酝酿已久的权力斗争正式爆发。它总是始于某种令消极者难以忍受的“情境”。由于人类天生倾向于快速反应，人们很少意识到所有情境本身都是中性的。你的伴侣忘记取干洗的衣服，既非好事也非坏事，既非对也非错。你的男友花太多时间与朋友相处，也并不意味着什么。在你赋予情境意义之前，它本身是绝对中性的。你对情境的解读决定了它是否会成为一个问题。正是旧伤痛的重现影响了人们的负面解读。我建立了一个模型来描述人际关系的发展历程，前提是这段关系至少在某种程度上是健康的：

HAPPY

快乐的

PSEUDO HAPPINESS
伪幸福
(Denial, cautious relating, avoidance of expressing any negative concerns)
（否认、谨慎的交往、避免表达任何负面担忧）

CHAOS
混乱
(Increased polarizing, power struggle, competition,)
（日益加剧的极化、权力斗争、竞争）

PROCESS
过程
(Effective communication, sharing of emerging feelings, responding to one’s pain, “joining”)
（有效沟通、分享涌现的感受、回应他人的痛苦、“加入”）

HAPPINESS

幸福

Of course the happiness soon progresses into a state of denial ( pseudo-happiness ), which moves to chaos , to process , to happiness , etc., etc.. But the operative word here is “evolves.” This means that the chaos stage which produces Power Struggles is a forward movement to ever-greater levels of happiness and intimacy in a relationship. Let’s follow the development of a Power Struggle with our friends John and Mary. Watch how maintaining either position, especially in times of crisis, stunts the relationship and blinds both sides to the real opportunity that is being offered. Mary, the Negative in this case, has just turned a situation into a problem.

当然，这种快乐很快就会演变成一种否认的状态（伪快乐），然后又会陷入混乱，进入处理阶段，再回到快乐，如此循环往复。但这里的关键词是“演变”。这意味着，产生权力斗争的混乱阶段，实际上是关系中幸福感和亲密感不断提升的进步过程。让我们跟随约翰和玛丽这对朋友，看看权力斗争是如何发展的。你会发现，尤其是在危机时刻，坚持己见会如何阻碍关系的发展，并让双方都看不到真正的机会。在这个例子中，玛丽扮演的是消极的角色，她刚刚把一个情境变成了一个问题。

Mary: Did you see our electricity bill today? It was a hundred dollars more than the last one!

玛丽：你今天看到我们的电费账单了吗？比上一张多了100美元！

John: Well it is wintertime, honey. We’re using more lights now.

约翰：亲爱的，现在是冬天了，我们用灯比较多。

Mary: But a hundred dollars? And our heating bill was twice what it was last month. We’ll never be able to afford a vacation at this rate.

玛丽：可是才一百美元？而且我们的暖气费是上个月的两倍。照这样下去，我们根本负担不起度假。

John: Sure we will. I’ll just put in some more overtime; we’ll be okay.

约翰：当然可以。我再加点班，肯定没问题。

Mary: But there’ll be less time for us. You’re putting in so much overtime right now that we hardly see each other as it is.

玛丽：但是我们相处的时间会减少。你现在加班太多，我们本来就很少见面。

John: Sweetheart, we see each other all the time—we live together, for God’s sake.

约翰：亲爱的，我们经常见面——我们住在一起，看在上帝的份上。

Mary: Yeah, but we never go anywhere or do anything anymore.

玛丽：是啊，但我们现在哪儿也不去，什么也不做了。

John: We went out last weekend to the Jenkins’ for dinner.

约翰：上周末我们去詹金斯家吃晚饭了。

Mary: I mean just the two of us. We always stay home and watch a film, or go to one of our friend’s places for dinner. I feel like we’ve become an old married couple.

玛丽：我是说就我们俩。我们总是待在家里看电影，或者去朋友家吃饭。我觉得我们就像一对老夫老妻一样。

John: Well we can go out this Friday—just the two of us. We’ll go to Armani’s for a nice supper.

约翰：那我们周五可以出去——就我们俩。我们去阿玛尼餐厅吃顿好的。

Mary: John, you’re so unrealistic! We can’t afford Armani’s.

玛丽：约翰，你太不切实际了！我们买不起阿玛尼。

John: I really think you’re taking this electrical bill a little too seriously, sweetheart.

约翰：亲爱的，我觉得你对这张电费账单有点太认真了。

Mary: It’s not the electrical bill—it’s us! You’re never around anymore. I feel like we’re strangers.

玛丽：不是电费的问题——是我们！你总是不在家。我觉得我们像陌生人一样。

John: Oh God! Look, we need milk for tomorrow morning. I’m going to go for a walk down to the store and pick some up. Can I get you anything?

约翰：哦，天哪！你看，我们明天早上需要牛奶。我打算去商店买一些。你需要什么吗？

Mary: Yes! A new husband!

玛丽：是的！我嫁了个新丈夫！

John: [Rolls his eyes, sighs loudly, shrugs his shoulders and leaves]

约翰：[翻了个白眼，重重地叹了口气，耸了耸肩，离开了]

This couple is not even close to what the real issue is about. On the surface it may seem to any listener that John is this really nice guy living with a whining nag who is impossible to please. In most cultures, Negatives are not appreciated for their ability to recognize problems, but are more often see as problem makers . Positives are perceived as happy, good, decent sorts. But why does he want to get out of the apartment? Does he have some sort of milk addiction that he can’t live without it? Of course not; he wants to get away because he’s beginning to feel some bad feelings. No one can bring a Positive down into the pits of negativity like their Negative partner. Once that happens the really ugly stage of Power Struggle can begin, with anything from vicious attacks to equally vicious silences. If John had a shorter fuse, he would have stayed to duke it out with Mary, justifying his attack with the righteous conviction that she started it. As it is John is now probably scurrying down the street, distancing himself from the threat of pain as quickly as possible. If he is thinking about a problem at all, it’s that the only problem he has in his life right now is waiting for him to come back with the milk so she can dump on him some more.

这对夫妻的遭遇根本没触及问题的本质。表面上看，约翰似乎是个和蔼可亲的人，却和一个爱抱怨、怎么都取悦不了的女人住在一起。在大多数文化中，消极的人不因其发现问题的能力而受到赞赏，反而常常被视为制造问题的人。积极的人则被认为是快乐、善良、正直的人。但他为什么要离开公寓呢？难道他有某种牛奶成瘾症，离不开它吗？当然不是；他想离开是因为他开始感到一些不好的情绪。没有人比消极的伴侣更能把一个积极的人拉入消极的深渊。一旦这种情况发生，权力斗争的丑陋阶段就会开始，从恶毒的攻击到同样恶毒的沉默，无所不包。如果约翰的脾气没那么暴躁，他就会留下来和玛丽争吵，并以“是她先动手的”这种正义感来为自己的攻击辩解。约翰现在大概正沿着街道飞奔而去，尽可能快地远离那可怕的威胁。如果他还在想着什么问题，那就是他现在生活中唯一的烦恼就是等着她拿牛奶回来，好让她再往他身上泼一顿。

How many people would see that John is in as much pain as Mary, and that the electric bill bothers him as much as it does her? And what observer could ever see what is really happening, which is that both Mary and John are being called to deal with a very old, very deep sense of unworthiness—or maybe something even more painful? But if they insist on looking no further than the surface problem, John will continue walking away from his beloved and Mary will continue to chase after him with an ever-growing list of complaints. John and Mary are simply following the standard human policy for dealing with pain: indulgence or denial. One will indulge in the anxiety, anger, and discontent that the problem stimulates, while the other will suppress those same emotions and run away from the problem by denying its seriousness. Once the pain begins to emerge:

有多少人会注意到约翰和玛丽一样痛苦，电费账单也同样让他烦恼不已？又有谁能真正看清真相：玛丽和约翰都在面对一种根深蒂固的、由来已久的自卑感——或许是某种更加痛苦的东西？但如果他们只关注表面问题，约翰就会继续远离他心爱的人，而玛丽也会继续追着他，抱怨的清单也越来越长。约翰和玛丽只是遵循着人类应对痛苦的惯常做法：要么沉溺其中，要么逃避现实。一个会沉溺于问题带来的焦虑、愤怒和不满，而另一个则会压抑这些情绪，否认问题的严重性，从而逃避现实。一旦痛苦开始显现：

The Negative zeros in on the biggest irritant available, establishes the “problem,” and expresses it to the Positive.

负面因素会集中精力找出最大的刺激因素，确定“问题”，并将其表达给正面因素。

The Positive often responds to his/her partner’s behaviour by denying that there are any problems (except for the ones in their Negative partner’s head).

积极的人常常会通过否认存在任何问题来回应伴侣的行为（除了消极的伴侣脑海中存在的问题）。

The Negative counters by insisting that there are very big and possibly unsolvable problems affecting the very future of the relationship.

否定方则反驳说，存在一些非常大且可能无法解决的问题，这些问题会影响这段关系的未来。

The Positive tries to find solutions.

积极方力求找到解决方案。

The Negative explains why each solution that is offered won’t work.

否定部分解释了为什么提出的每个解决方案都行不通。

The Positive tries to cheer his/her partner up.

积极的人会努力让伴侣开心起来。

The Negative refuses to be cheered up, and often resents the Positive’s condescending attitude—which has been bugging the Negative for some time now, come to think of it!

消极的人拒绝被鼓励，并且常常对积极的人居高临下的态度感到不满——仔细想想，这种态度已经困扰消极的人一段时间了！

The Positive goes for a walk, intending to come back when the negative is feeling better.

积极的人出去散步，打算等消极的人感觉好些后再回来。

The Negative sits and fumes until the partner returns from his/her walk, and then resumes shoving the problem into the partner’s face. All the while, the intensity of the discomfort is growing, until

消极的一方会一直坐在那里生气，直到伴侣散步回来，然后继续把问题一股脑地塞到伴侣脸上。与此同时，这种不适感也在不断加剧，直到……

The Positive succumbs to his/her anger, and war is declared.

正方屈服于愤怒，战争爆发。

Positives will rarely admit to the existence of the problem. They choose to remain oblivious to negative feelings. To John’s mind, they don’t have money, electrical bills, or relationship problems; they have Mary problems. John will hold righteously to his position—which is, of course, the right point of view. He will look at Mary as the problem maker , not the problem recognizer, and react to her emotionalism with cool reasoning, pouring Positive oil over the troubled waters. From her position Mary will see John as insensitive, uncaring, and blind to what is important.

积极的人很少会承认问题的存在。他们选择对负面情绪视而不见。在约翰看来，他们遇到的问题不是钱、电费或人际关系问题，而是玛丽的问题。约翰会坚定地维护自己的立场——当然，这才是他的观点。他会把玛丽视为问题的制造者，而不是问题的发现者，并用冷静的理性来应对她的情绪化，用积极的心态来平息纷扰。而玛丽则会认为约翰冷漠无情，对真正重要的事情视而不见。

Therein lies a crucial message: How you are treated in any given relationship is determined by the position you take. In a Power Struggle your position automatically causes you to see your partner taking the opposing one and reacting to your behaviour from that place. Therefore, if you do not like the way the relationship is going, you need only leave your position and move toward harmony. Typically your partner will change as well. If your partner is not changing in your eyes, it is often because you are clinging to your position. There are occasions when the partner’s behaviour does not seem to change, but it no longer bothers you; there are also instances of the partner taking a few hours, days, sometimes weeks, to shift from their position. Whatever the outcome of you letting go of your position, it is always to your benefit to do so, for there is only the false security of righteousness and pride to be experienced in holding on to your point of view. Letting go allows for the freedom to grow in wisdom and maturity.

这其中蕴含着一个至关重要的信息：你在任何一段关系中受到的对待都取决于你所采取的立场。在权力斗争中，你的立场必然会让你看到伴侣采取相反的立场，并以此为出发点对你的行为做出反应。因此，如果你不喜欢这段关系的走向，你只需要放下你的立场，走向和谐。通常情况下，你的伴侣也会随之改变。如果你的伴侣在你眼中没有改变，那往往是因为你仍然固执己见。有时，伴侣的行为看似没有改变，但你却不再为此烦恼；有时，伴侣需要几个小时、几天，甚至几周的时间才能转变立场。无论你放下立场的结果如何，这样做总是对你有益的，因为坚持己见只会带来虚假的正义感和骄傲。放下立场才能让你获得成长的自由，变得更加智慧和成熟。

***

CAN WE TALK?

我们可以谈谈吗？

———————————

“I don’t wanna talk about it—how you broke my heart….”

“我不想谈这件事——你是如何伤透我的心的……”

—Danny Whitten, “I Don’t Want to Talk About It”

——丹尼·惠顿，《我不想谈论这件事》

Imagine that the solution to Mary and John’s problem exists at a point presently beyond their imagination, where their money difficulties will be alleviated and the pain at the heart of their real issue will be healed.

想象一下，玛丽和约翰的问题的解决方法存在于他们目前无法想象的地方，在那里，他们的经济困难将得到缓解，他们真正问题的核心痛苦也将得到治愈。

All Power Struggles begin cleverly disguised as a situation that is presented to the relationship. The following chart may help you to see the leviathan that lurks in the depths beneath the seemingly placid pond of the situation that arises:

所有的权力斗争都巧妙地伪装成关系中呈现的一种情境。以下图表或许能帮助你看清潜藏在看似平静的情境之下的庞然大物：

SITUATION (NEUTRAL)
情况（中性）
(electrical bill arrived)
（电费账单已到）

PROBLEM (BUTTON IS PUSHED)
问题（按钮已按下）
(Mary: we can’t afford it, we don’t have enough money)
（玛丽：我们买不起，我们钱不够）
(John: Mary is unhappy and I don’t know how to fix that)
（约翰：玛丽不高兴，我不知道该怎么让她高兴）

REAL ISSUE (OLD EMOTION ARISES)
真正的问题（旧情复燃）
(Mary, sadly: It’s my fault—I’m so worthless.)
（玛丽悲伤地说：都是我的错——我太没用了。）
(John, sadly: It’s my fault—I’m so worthless.)
（约翰悲伤地说：都是我的错——我太没用了。）

TRAUMA (SOURCE OF THE PAIN)
创伤（痛苦的根源）
(Mary/John: I’ve felt valueless ever since I can remember)
（玛丽/约翰：我从记事起就觉得自己毫无价值）

CHOICE
选择
(Mary/John: I stopped loving myself)
(玛丽/约翰：我不再爱自己)

Mary and John can make another choice to love themselves by being accountable for the pain they carry, letting the other off the hook, and expressing their individual hurts in a way that allows the pain to surface into awareness. Once the pain surfaces, they can burn through it by experiencing it peacefully, without reaction, and by giving love to each other. The easiest way to do this is to communicate .

玛丽和约翰可以选择另一种爱自己的方式：坦然面对自己所承受的痛苦，不再责怪对方，并以一种能够让痛苦浮现出来的方式表达各自的伤痛。一旦痛苦浮现，他们就可以通过平和地体验它、不加反应，并彼此给予爱来化解它。最简单的方法就是沟通。

But if both John and Mary are convinced that the other is looking at the situation wrong, they will focus on proving this, which will only heighten the conflict, possibly leading to all-out war. It will definitely keep each of them from moving closer to their own souls. Eventually, John and Mary will succumb to anger, and a fight will ensue with both sides accusing the other of being the cause of the problem. Possibly they will let off a bunch of pent-up steam, or continue the fight for a few days. This might even be the beginning of the end of the relationship. Or maybe the problem will blow over and by the time John comes back from his walk they will be back to “normal” with each other. One thing is certain: the pain that was the real cause of the problem will not be healed. It will remain inside them and wait for another opportunity to make its presence known.

但如果约翰和玛丽都认定对方对情况的看法有误，他们就会专注于证明这一点，这只会加剧冲突，甚至可能导致全面战争。这无疑会阻碍他们各自的内心世界。最终，约翰和玛丽都会被愤怒吞噬，爆发争吵，双方都指责对方才是问题的根源。他们或许会借此发泄积压已久的怒火，也可能争吵持续数日。这甚至可能是这段关系走向终结的开始。又或许，问题会自行消散，等约翰散步回来，他们之间又会恢复“正常”。但有一点可以肯定：真正导致问题的根源——内心的伤痛——并不会就此愈合。它会一直潜藏在他们心中，伺机再次爆发。

A truly effective solution would be for the couple to allow the underlying pain to emerge, and deal with it in a healthy way. Since many of us never learned how to do this, it might seem easier to avoid the whole issue altogether. However it is possible for us to leave our positions in order to find a place of agreement and harmony within all of our relationships. Of course without an intention to find a true solution to any disagreement, the paths through such conflicts will go unused. Again, as with demands and expectations, intention is the key to success. Once your intention is clear in your mind, the way through can be found with effective communication. Imagine if we rewound the interaction between John and Mary and employed another approach.

真正有效的解决办法是让夫妻双方允许潜在的痛苦浮现出来，并以健康的方式处理它。由于我们很多人从未学会如何做到这一点，所以完全回避问题似乎更容易。然而，我们完全可以放下成见，在所有关系中找到共识与和谐。当然，如果没有真正解决分歧的意愿，解决冲突的途径就无法发挥作用。再次强调，就像要求和期望一样，意图是成功的关键。一旦你的意图清晰明确，有效的沟通就能找到解决之道。试想一下，如果我们倒叙约翰和玛丽的互动，并采用另一种方法，结果会如何呢？

Mary: Did you see our electricity bill today? It was a hundred dollars more than the last one!

玛丽：你今天看到我们的电费账单了吗？比上一张多了100美元！

John: Well it is wintertime, honey. We’re using more lights now.

约翰：亲爱的，现在是冬天了，我们用灯比较多。

Mary: But a hundred dollars? We’ll never be able to afford a vacation at this rate.

玛丽：可是一百美元？照这样下去，我们永远也负担不起度假了。

John: Sure we will. I’ll just put in some more overtime; we’ll be okay. What’s the matter, Mary? Are you okay? ( John starts to LISTEN )

约翰：当然可以。我再加点班，没问题的。玛丽，你怎么了？你还好吗？（约翰开始倾听）

Mary: No, I’m feeling very angry. This electricity bill really bothers me. It just makes me feel like we’re never going to get ahead. ( Mary starts paying attention to her uncomfortable emotions that were laying just below her anger. )

玛丽：不，我非常生气。这张电费单真让我心烦。它让我觉得我们永远也摆脱不了困境。（玛丽开始注意到隐藏在愤怒之下的那些不安情绪。）

John: I know, sweetheart. It bothers me, too. But I don’t want it to ruin our weekend together. I want us to have some fun! Hell, we deserve it. ( John has now set an intention for both of them to come out of this happy—he’s choosing to connect with Mary, heart-to-heart. ) Look, maybe I can ask for a raise on Monday.

约翰：我知道，亲爱的。我也很烦恼。但我不想让它毁了我们的周末。我想我们好好玩玩！我们值得拥有这份快乐。（约翰现在下定决心，希望他们俩都能开心——他选择和玛丽敞开心扉地交流。）你看，也许我周一可以要求加薪。

Mary: No, it’s not the bill that’s bugging me, or all the overtime you’re doing. This is a problem I’ve had plenty of times in my life. I’ve felt like such a loser my whole life. ( Mary chooses not to blame her partner for the problem, thus allowing her to see her inner process )

玛丽：不，让我烦恼的不是账单，也不是你加班太多。这个问题我这辈子遇到过很多次了。我一直觉得自己是个彻头彻尾的失败者。（玛丽选择不责怪伴侣，从而让伴侣得以审视自己的内心世界。）

John: It sounds like you don’t feel like you’re worth much. I just want you to know that you’re worth a lot to me. You’re the most precious thing in my life. ( John listens more closely, and seeks to identify the important feelings. He endeavours to join Mary in her pain and comforts her with sincere appreciation )

约翰：听起来你觉得自己没什么价值。我只想让你知道，你对我来说非常重要。你是我生命中最珍贵的人。（约翰更加仔细地倾听，试图找出玛丽内心深处的感受。他努力体会玛丽的痛苦，并用真诚的感激之情安慰她。）

Mary: Thanks, but I just wish I could feel that for myself. Ever since I was a kid I felt worthless. ( She’s not saying “I felt LIKE,” but instead is saying more directly, “I felt worthless” ) No matter how much I tried, I always thought I was just a burden—especially with my father. I would try to be a perfect daughter around him, but every time he had to buy me new clothes or something he’d always bitch about how much I was costing him. I felt so… so… ( Mary keeps sharing her deeper feelings and getting a stronger sense of their origin. )

玛丽：谢谢，但我真希望自己也能有这种感觉。从小我就觉得自己一文不值。（她不是说“我感觉像”，而是更直接地说“我觉得自己一文不值”）无论我怎么努力，我总觉得自己是个累赘——尤其是在我父亲面前。我努力在他面前做一个完美的女儿，但每次他要给我买新衣服什么的，他总是抱怨我花了他多少钱。我感觉……感觉……（玛丽继续倾诉她内心深处的感受，并逐渐意识到这些感受的根源。）

John: Unwanted?

约翰：不受欢迎的人？

Mary: Yeah, exactly!

玛丽：对，没错！

John: I know what you mean. With me it was my mother. She was always complaining about how poor we were. She hardly ever smiled at me or appreciated me. It was like I had no value around her. I’ve felt like that a lot in my life—completely valueless. (John is recognizing Mary’s feelings as his own now, and feeling it as deeply as he can )

约翰：我明白你的意思。我的情况是这样的，我母亲总是抱怨我们家有多穷。她几乎从不对我笑，也不欣赏我。在她眼里，我好像毫无价值。我一生中经常有这种感觉——觉得自己一文不值。（约翰现在意识到玛丽的感受正是他自己的感受，并深深地体会着。）

Mary: Me too. Valueless. But you’re so talented, John!

玛丽：我也是。没价值。但你真的很有才华，约翰！

John: Yeah? Then how come I have to put in a bunch of hours overtime for a measly electric bill? I scrimp and save so we can have a lousy two week vacation, and then come back and work my ass off for another year. It feels so…so… meaningless.

约翰：是吗？那为什么我得加班加点才能交得起那点可怜的电费？我省吃俭用，就为了那可怜的两周假期，然后回来又得拼命工作一年。感觉这一切都太……太……没意义了。

Mary: That’s my middle name—meaningless. I really think I was born with absolutely no usefulness, purpose or meaning. So often I’ve wanted to split up with you because I thought you deserved someone better. ( Both keep going deeper, moving towards a peaceful completion )

玛丽：那是我的中间名——毫无意义。我真的觉得我生来就毫无用处、毫无目的、毫无意义。我常常想和你分手，因为我觉得你值得更好的人。（两人继续深入交流，最终走向平静的结局）

John: You never told me that! Honey, you’re perfect for me. Since I met you I’ve started to see that maybe I am worth something. ( Anyone for some great lovemaking? )

约翰：你从来没跟我说过！亲爱的，你简直就是我的完美伴侣。自从遇见你，我开始觉得我或许还有点价值。（有人想来点激情四射的吗？）

It’s easy to see that this conversation is turning out a whole lot better than the previous one. 30 All it took was for one person to let go of a position. In this case, John decided to stop being Superman and started to care about his partner’s feelings. Because he was sincere and not manipulative, Mary stopped indulging in her negativity and began expressing the essential feelings that were really bothering her. Unless Negatives do this, they tend to feel everything except the really important feelings. It could also have happened the other way; if Mary had immediately taken responsibility for her feelings, releasing any burden from John to do something, she could then delve deeper into the source of the pain, and express her more essential feelings. John would then be able to feel that they were on the same side and “join with her” in exploring the hurt. This would eventually lead to greater intimacy with each other, and instead of running out for milk, John might well have come up with a number of good reasons to stay in that night! 31

显而易见，这次谈话比上次好得多。<sup>30</sup> 这只需要一个人放下执念。在这个例子中，约翰决定不再扮演超人，开始关心伴侣的感受。因为他真诚而不耍手段，玛丽不再沉溺于消极情绪，开始表达真正困扰她的那些核心感受。除非消极的人这样做，否则他们往往会感受到除真正重要感受之外的一切。事情也可能反过来发展；如果玛丽立即承担起自己感受的责任，不再让约翰承担任何责任，她就能更深入地探究痛苦的根源，表达她更核心的感受。这样，约翰就能感受到他们站在同一阵线上，并“与她一起”探索伤痛。这最终会加深彼此的亲密感，而约翰或许就能找到许多待在家里的好理由，而不是像往常那样跑出去买牛奶！<sup>31</sup>

Now some astute reader might have noticed John and Mary shifting the blame off each other, and placing it on their parents. Although most of our early traumas were experienced with our parents, but Mary acknowledged her feelings of uselessness, purposelessness, and meaninglessness as coming into the world with her when she was born. They are, after all, feelings that are common to all of humanity, regardless of how we were parented. But even if one or both of them did not release the blame completely, the point is that this communication between them was a first step towards personal accountability. Naturally they could take it further and relieve their parents altogether of the responsibility for their pain, and this will be covered further in the chapter on Introspection. For now my intention is to offer a basic approach to communication that can help end the torture of Power Struggles in relationships.

一些细心的读者或许已经注意到，约翰和玛丽互相推诿，把责任都推给了父母。虽然我们早期的创伤大多与父母有关，但玛丽承认，她与生俱来的无用感、无目标感和无意义感是与生俱来的。毕竟，无论我们如何被养育，这些感受都是全人类共通的。即便他们中有人或两人并未完全放下责任，关键在于，他们之间的这种沟通是迈向个人责任的第一步。当然，他们也可以更进一步，彻底免除父母对他们痛苦的责任，这一点将在“内省”一章中详细探讨。现在，我的目的是提供一种基本的沟通方法，帮助人们结束关系中权力斗争带来的痛苦。

In my marriage, I have tried both approaches—position taking (i.e. trying to be right), and communicating. I am a very proud man, so I have a deeply ingrained tendency to try and prove I am always right, but it has never given me a moment of peace—even when I actually was right! Only when I let go of my position and reach out to another person with a sincere intention to partake in real heart-to-heart communication do I ever come to happiness.

在我的婚姻中，我尝试过两种方法——坚持立场（也就是努力证明自己是对的）和沟通。我是一个非常骄傲的人，所以根深蒂固地想要证明自己永远是对的，但这从未给我带来片刻的平静——即使我真的是对的！只有当我放下立场，真诚地与对方进行真正心与心的交流时，我才能获得真正的幸福。

I have discovered eight important questions that can guide an individual through the process of truly effective, conscious communication. It is in the form of questions because questions allow one to search one’s soul, whereas pointers and direction can often lead one to developing formulae. My experience has taught me that there is no formula for True Partnership. Everything hinges on the responses we make moment by moment.

我发现了八个重要的问题，它们可以引导人们进行真正有效、有意识的沟通。之所以用问题的形式呈现，是因为问题能让人深入内心，而指点和方向往往容易让人养成固定的模式。我的经验告诉我，真正的伙伴关系没有固定的模式。一切都取决于我们每时每刻的回应。

Eight Guiding Questions for Conscious Communication

八个引导意识沟通的问题

1. What do I want?

1. 我想要什么？

2. What misunderstanding must be cleared up first?

2. 首先需要澄清什么误会？

3. What emotions can I express with absolute Truth?

3. 我可以用绝对真理表达哪些情感？

4. How can I respond to this emotion?

4. 我该如何应对这种情绪？

5. What feeling is beneath this emotion?

5. 这种情绪背后隐藏着什么感觉？

6. Is my feeling, or that of my partner, familiar to me?

6. 我或我的伴侣的这种感觉，我是否感到熟悉？

7. What is the history of this feeling?

7. 这种感觉的历史是什么？

8. Can I respond to this feeling in a loving way?

8. 我能否以爱的方式回应这种感觉？

When I respond to these questions with the honesty in my heart, problems within my relationship are resolved. I have also discovered that problems that appear to have nothing to do with my relationship can be resolved through conscious communication with my partner.

当我坦诚地回答这些问题时，我们关系中的问题就迎刃而解了。我还发现，一些看似与我们的感情无关的问题，也能通过与伴侣的真诚沟通得到解决。

The eight guiding questions for effective communication offer important principles I have discovered through my own experiences, 32 as well as from the influences of such great pioneers as Carl Jung, Chuck Spezzano, and Gay and Kathlyn Hendricks. Let’s examine the points of this model one at a time.

这八个有效沟通的指导性问题，包含了我从自身经验中总结出的重要原则，32 同时也受到了卡尔·荣格、查克·斯佩扎诺、盖伊和凯瑟琳·亨德里克斯等伟大先驱的影响。让我们逐一审视这个模型的各个要点。

1. What do I want? This is probably the most important question I can ask myself when faced with any communication issue. For me, the greatest challenge is to stay focused on the purpose of the communication. 33 The quickest route to a harmonious agreement is found when even just one person keeps his/her mind and heart focused on the goal of ending the separation caused by the Power Struggle. Therefore, if I set an intention in my mind that includes a harmonious outcome whereby both parties win, and I make a heartfelt commitment to that goal, that is invariably what happens. Even though it is often impossible to see at first, in every conflict there is a way through to satisfaction and harmony for both parties. In fact, there is no way through at all unless both parties get through together. Thus, I ask myself: What do I want? Do I want to be right or be happy? Do I want conflict or harmony? Defensiveness or trust? Isolation or intimacy? Do I want to win or do I want us both to win? Would I prefer compromise or complete resolution? My answer to this question ultimately ends up as “I want true peace.”

1. 我想要什么？这或许是我在面对任何沟通问题时最应该问自己的问题。对我而言，最大的挑战在于始终专注于沟通的目的。33 达成和谐协议的最快途径，在于即使只有一方能够全心全意地专注于结束权力斗争造成的隔阂这一目标。因此，如果我心中设定一个包含双方共赢的和谐结果的意图，并真心实意地致力于实现这一目标，那么结果必然会如此。尽管一开始往往难以察觉，但每一次冲突都存在着让双方都满意和和谐的解决之道。事实上，除非双方携手共进，否则根本无路可走。因此，我会问自己：我想要什么？我想要证明自己是对的还是想要快乐？我想要冲突还是和谐？我想要防御还是信任？我想要孤立还是亲密？我想要赢还是想要我们双方都赢？我更倾向于妥协还是彻底解决？我对这个问题的最终回答是“我想要真正的和平”。

It is a basic principle of personal accountability that whatever you have in your life is exactly what you want. If you are preoccupied with the goal of winning, what you want is to engage in a win/lose conflict; but playing win/lose only leads to guilt for the winner, and likely bitterness, resentment and a desire for revenge on the part of the loser. Think about it: how good could you feel if you made your partner the loser in an argument? Do you think it would end there? S/he would probably be waiting for a chance to get even. 34 Playing win/win ensures a happy and harmonious relationship where you and your partner feel secure in the knowledge that you are looking out for each other’s best interests.

个人责任的基本原则是：你生活中拥有的一切，正是你想要的。如果你一心只想赢，你就会想要陷入一场输赢之争；但这种赢输之争只会让赢家感到内疚，而输家则很可能心怀怨恨、愤懑，甚至想要报复。想想看：如果你在争吵中让你的伴侣成为输家，你会感觉如何？你觉得事情会就此结束吗？他/她很可能会伺机报复。<sup>34</sup> 双赢之道才能确保你们的关系幸福和谐，让彼此都感到安心，因为你们都在为对方的利益着想。

Contrary to some very strongly held views in society, I feel that there are no bad people in an inter-personal conflict. Be it between a partner, friend or associate, there are only two parties doing the very best they can at any given moment to experience happiness and belonging. In many counselling sessions, I have heard one partner describe the other in a very bad light. The one they fell head over heels in love with is now the most evil wretch to ever walk the planet. In my experience, it is always my pain that is causing me to see my partner in a harmful light. When conflicts arise, it is very helpful to remember that my partner is as innocent as I am. One way I found to do this is to remember that the sun shines equally on both of us; in that way I can also remember that my heart loves us both equally, and sees us as the same. When I am tempted to see someone as wrong or bad, I do my best to remember to ask myself: “How would my heart see this person?” 35 In my heart and soul I know there are no bad guys.

与社会上一些根深蒂固的观点相反，我认为人际冲突中没有坏人。无论是伴侣、朋友还是同事之间，都只有双方在尽力而为，渴望获得幸福和归属感。在许多咨询中，我听到一方对另一方极尽贬低之能事。他们曾经深爱的人，如今却成了世上最邪恶的人。就我的经验而言，总是我的痛苦让我以负面的眼光看待我的伴侣。当冲突发生时，记住我的伴侣和我一样无辜，这非常有帮助。我发现一个方法是记住阳光平等地照耀着我们两个人；这样我也能记住，我的心同样爱着我们两个人，视我们为一体。当我想要把某人视为错误或坏人时，我会尽力问自己：“我的心会如何看待这个人？”35 在我的内心深处，我知道世上没有坏人。

In order to ensure that the mutually beneficial goal that I set is reached, it is important that I do not settle for the illusory peace of a compromise. When my wife and I settle for compromise, the only satisfaction I feel is in knowing that she lost just as much as I did. Compromise may often seem like the best solution available, but it actually makes both sides feel like they’ve lost, because they both accepted less than what they knew in their hearts was truly possible. Once we start trusting the power of our heart’s intention, we will begin to see miraculous results being born out of what at first seemed like a hopeless deadlock.

为了确保我设定的互惠互利的目标得以实现，我不能满足于妥协带来的虚假平静。当我和妻子妥协时，我唯一的满足感来自于她和我一样都失去了很多。妥协或许看似最佳方案，但实际上却让双方都感到自己有所损失，因为他们都接受了低于内心真正渴望的方案。一旦我们开始相信内心意愿的力量，我们就会看到奇迹般的结果从最初看似毫无希望的僵局中诞生。

To be able to witness these kinds of miracles, I have to keep reminding myself that I am not being asked to solve the problem. Problems have built-in mechanisms for resolving themselves. Once the feelings that the problem made us aware of are resolved, the problem magically transforms itself into a gift, a life lesson, or a new opportunity for abundance. A perfect example of this came from two friends of ours who were in the clutches of a serious money problem. With him out of work and a child on the way, the stress led to some bitter quarrels. In her mind, he was incompetent (“not man enough to take care of a family”), and in his mind she purposely got pregnant without his consent so she could run away from life (“Hide out in the house and watch soap operas all day”) while he sweated away at some unrewarding job. Underneath these accusations, she was feeling that it was her fault there was no money, while he thought the same about himself. In their guilt, they each thought they themselves should have the answer to their money problem. In the nick of time, they decided to sit down and communicate responsibly. As they did, it came out that they both were convinced that they were useless failures. Joining each other in that pain, they cried some tears and mourned their loss of a happier youth. They spent the night comforting each other. A few days later he was offered a great job that suited his gifts and talents.

为了能够见证这类奇迹，我必须不断提醒自己，我并非被要求去解决问题。问题本身就蕴含着自我解决的机制。一旦问题引发的那些感受得到化解，问题本身就会神奇地转化为一份礼物、一次人生历练，或是一次通往富足的新机遇。我们两位朋友的经历就是一个很好的例子，他们曾深陷严重的经济困境。男方失业，妻子又即将临盆，压力之下，两人爆发了激烈的争吵。女方认为男方无能（“根本没资格养家糊口”），而男方则认为女方故意瞒着他怀孕，是为了逃避现实（“整天躲在家里看肥皂剧”），而他却只能在毫无回报的工作中苦苦挣扎。在这些指责的背后，女方觉得没钱是自己的错，男方也同样这么认为。在愧疚的驱使下，他们都认为自己应该能够解决经济问题。千钧一发之际，他们决定坐下来认真沟通。沟通中，他们坦白自己都觉得自己一无是处，是个失败者。他们感同身受地体会着这种痛苦，流下了眼泪，缅怀着逝去的美好青春。他们整夜互相安慰。几天后，他获得了一份非常适合他才能和天赋的好工作。

To me, getting the job was not the miracle. The miracle was that my two friends found love in the heart of the darkness. They realized that they didn’t have a money problem. Their problem was a lack of trust in life, a trust they lost through some trauma. Once they gave up thinking that it was their job to solve the problem, they could deal with what was important; the problem, being no longer necessary, transformed itself into the gift of faith in life. The key to this transformation was in their realization that what they really wanted was for their child to have happy, loving parents.

对我而言，找到工作本身并非奇迹。真正的奇迹在于，我的两位朋友在黑暗深处找到了爱。他们意识到，他们并非缺钱，而是缺乏对生活的信任——这种信任源于某种创伤。一旦他们不再执着于解决问题，便能专注于真正重要的事情；问题本身不再必要，反而转化为对生活的信念。这种转变的关键在于，他们意识到自己真正渴望的是孩子拥有幸福、充满爱的父母。

2. What misunderstandings must be cleared up first? Maybe my partner came home late because she got a flat, or had to take care of a sick friend and had no time to call. Or maybe she stayed out because she thought I didn’t really care if she came home or not, while I was thinking that she was out with someone she liked more than me. Clearing up misunderstanding makes assumptions irrelevant, and assumptions are often the fuel for accusations. Once all the facts are in the open, you can begin to deal with the real source of aggravation, such as “what are we experiencing that makes us think one doesn’t care for the other?”

2. 首先需要澄清哪些误会？也许我的伴侣晚归是因为她车子抛锚了，或者她要照顾生病的朋友，没时间打电话。又或许她之所以在外待着，是因为她觉得我不在乎她是否回家，而我却以为她和她更喜欢的人在一起。澄清误会可以消除臆测，而臆测往往会成为指责的导火索。一旦所有事实都摆在眼前，你就可以开始处理真正令人恼火的根源，例如“我们究竟经历了什么，才会觉得一方不在乎另一方？”

3. Within this conflict, what emotions can I express with absolute Truth? I am expressing an absolute truth when I make a statement that does not feed a conflict. If I am describing a feeling without making anyone else responsible for what I am feeling, I am stating an inarguable truth. On the other hand, saying to my wife, “I’m mad at you for coming home late,” can feed the conflict and therefore is an arguable statement. She may have a reason for being late that would diffuse my anger immediately. I am actually angry because of why I think she’s late. My anger may have been catalyzed by my wife’s tardiness, but it could not have been created by it. I have tons of anger inside me, just looking for an opportunity to happen. Her actions may have been an excuse for my anger but certainly not the cause of it.

3. 在这种冲突中，我能以绝对真理表达哪些情绪？当我表达的陈述不会加剧冲突时，我就表达了绝对真理。如果我描述一种感受，而不将这种感受归咎于任何人，那么我就是在陈述一个无可辩驳的真理。另一方面，对妻子说“你回家晚了，我生气了”，可能会加剧冲突，因此这是一个可以争辩的陈述。她或许有迟到的理由，而这些理由会立即平息我的怒火。我真正生气的原因，是我认为她迟到的原因。我的怒火或许是妻子迟到引发的，但它并非怒火的根源。我内心积压着大量的怒气，只是在寻找爆发的机会。她的行为或许是我愤怒的借口，但绝非愤怒的起因。

A more accurate truth would be, “When you didn’t come home on time, I became angry.” Even better, “Your being late helped me become aware of how angry I feel inside.” Or how about “I’m really pissed off! It’s not your fault—I’m just feeling really mad at myself!”? Taking 100% responsibility for your emotions allows you the opportunity to speak indisputable truths. Anything less than 100% leaves you susceptible to the weaknesses of blame, judgment, righteousness and defensiveness. 36

更准确的说法应该是：“你没按时回家，我生气了。” 更好的说法是：“你迟到让我意识到自己内心有多生气。” 或者说：“我真的很生气！这不是你的错——我只是对自己很生气！”？ 完全掌控自己的情绪，才能让你有机会说出无可辩驳的真相。任何低于百分之百的掌控都会让你容易陷入指责、评判、自以为是和自我防御的陷阱。<sup>36</sup>

It is the nature of relationship crises that the problem appears to be coming from the outside towards us, but I have found that any conflict in a relationship represents a conflict within myself. Carl Jung coined the phrase “projection” to suggest that everything that we see outside of us is actually our inner process being played out on the stage of the outside world. In the trainings I facilitate, I sometimes have people check in with what they are feeling, and then look at the group they are in. Invariably, those that are feeling fear will perceive a very threatening group of people around them. Those that are angry tend to see a lot of faults in their group. One person who was feeling extremely peaceful and happy claimed that her group was populated by angels.

人际关系危机的本质在于，问题似乎来自外部，指向我们。但我发现，任何关系中的冲突都代表着我内心的冲突。卡尔·荣格创造了“投射”一词，指出我们所看到的外部世界，实际上都是我们内在过程在外部世界舞台上的展现。在我主持的培训中，我有时会让学员觉察自己的感受，然后观察他们所在的群体。通常情况下，感到恐惧的人会觉得周围的人充满威胁。而感到愤怒的人则往往会看到群体中存在诸多缺陷。一位感到无比平静和快乐的人甚至声称，她的群体里都是天使。

I have repeatedly found the principles of projection to be true, and do my best to see all relationship conflicts as a reflection of my own process. If I am dealing with a deep sense of abandonment and loneliness—which is a very human experience—the person I am with will often appear distant and indifferent to me. Being 100% responsible for my feelings makes it possible for me to free myself from the trap of thinking that my source of unhappiness, and happiness, is outside of me. Expressing that responsibility with an absolute truth allows for a deeper understanding of what I am really experiencing.

我反复验证了投射的原理，并尽力将所有关系冲突都视为自身经历的反映。如果我正经历着深深的被抛弃感和孤独感——这是一种非常普遍的人类体验——那么我身边的人往往会显得疏远冷漠。百分之百地为自己的感受负责，使我能够摆脱“快乐和不幸的根源都来自自身之外”这种思维陷阱。以绝对的真诚来表达这种责任，让我能够更深刻地理解自己真正的感受。

Anger is usually the first emotion to be expressed in a conflict. 37 Anger usually blocks more important feelings, but it is good to be aware of it, and feel it as completely as you can without harming anyone 38 with it. Along with anger, fear and sadness, are usually involved. Simply stating “I am feeling ________,” and stating the emotion that you are aware of, begins the inward journey. To say, “I feel like ________” or “I feel that ________,” or “You make me feel ________” are three examples of avoiding your feelings, and they often encourage argument.

在冲突中，愤怒通常是最先表达的情绪。<sup>37</sup> 愤怒往往会掩盖更重要的感受，但意识到它的存在并尽可能充分地感受它，同时又不伤害任何人，是有益的。<sup>38</sup> 除了愤怒，恐惧和悲伤通常也伴随着愤怒。简单地说“我感觉____”，并表达你所意识到的情绪，就能开启一段内省之旅。而说“我感觉像____”、“我觉得____”或“你让我感觉____”则是逃避自身感受的三种例子，它们往往会引发争吵。

4. How can I respond to this emotion? With this question, you can choose to give up a tendency to react to the uncomfortable emotions and discover ways to respond that bring more peace, joy, and love into your life. Typically, no emotion can remain in your body for more than six minutes, unless you’re making a home for it there. You can give emotions a home by denying them, justifying them, fearing them, or indulging in their drama. However, if you simply focus your awareness on an emotion, without any judgment whatsoever, the emotion would begin to transform into a higher form of energy. A great way to respond is to verbally express what you are feeling with as much openness and acceptance as you can. This necessitates that you go past giving the history of what you’re feeling, and express the depth, texture, and effects of the emotion without falling into the trap of indulgence.

4. 我该如何回应这种情绪？通过这个问题，你可以选择放弃对不适情绪的过度反应，并探索能为你的生活带来更多平和、喜悦和爱的回应方式。通常情况下，除非你刻意为之，否则任何情绪都无法在你的身体里停留超过六分钟。你可以通过否认、辩解、恐惧或沉溺于情绪的戏剧性来为它“安家”。然而，如果你只是将注意力集中在某种情绪上，不加任何评判，这种情绪就会开始转化为更高层次的能量。一个很好的回应方式是尽可能地以开放和接纳的态度，用语言表达你的感受。这意味着你需要超越对感受的描述，表达情绪的深度、质感和影响，同时避免陷入沉溺的陷阱。

More often than not, you will be doing this with the support of your partner. But there is the possibility that your partner will not be supportive due to lack of trust, or because she/he is in reaction to the emerging feelings. Since it would still be beneficial for you to complete your process and not suppress your feelings, I will describe a way to respond to emotions and feelings at the end of this chapter.

大多数情况下，你会得到伴侣的支持。但你的伴侣也可能因为缺乏信任，或者因为你涌现出的情绪而不支持你。鉴于完成这个过程而不是压抑自己的感受仍然对你有益，我将在本章末尾介绍一种应对情绪和感受的方法。

5. What feeling is beneath this emotion? Once you respond to the emotion in an effective way, you may find that the problem has dissolved, leaving you with a sense of closeness to your partner (or whomever you were in conflict with). You just needed to feel all your anger, or your sadness, or your fear, and now you feel better. You’re on your way to more loving, intimate connection with each other.

5. 这种情绪背后隐藏着什么感受？一旦你有效地应对了这种情绪，你可能会发现问题已经迎刃而解，让你与伴侣（或任何与你发生冲突的人）之间产生一种亲近感。你只需要感受所有的愤怒、悲伤或恐惧，现在你感觉好多了。你们正朝着更加充满爱意、更加亲密的联结迈进。

There are often times, however, when after you have dissolved the emotion, you discover a doorway into something much vaster. This is what I call the realm of “emptiness feelings,” the feelings we first became aware of as we began our struggle for complete “self-consciousness.” 39 Such experiences as loneliness, helplessness, hopelessness, and feeling lost (to mention a few) are aspects of the human experience, but they appear to be so deep and endless that you may have a primal fear of feeling them. When we were children, throwing a tantrum was a good way of distancing ourselves from the depths of these emptiness feelings.

然而，很多时候，当你消解了某种情绪之后，你会发现一扇通往更广阔世界的大门。我称之为“空虚感”的领域，这种感觉最初是在我们开始追求完全的“自我意识”时觉察到的。<sup>39</sup> 孤独、无助、绝望和迷失感（仅举几例）等体验都是人类经验的一部分，但它们似乎如此深邃无尽，以至于你可能对感受它们产生一种本能的恐惧。当我们还是孩子的时候，发脾气是让我们远离这些空虚感深渊的好方法。

These emptiness feelings are at the heart of your core beliefs. Expressing one of these feelings to the best of your abilities allows you to maintain an important awareness of both the experiencer and the experience. Why is this important? When first confronting these primary feelings it might seem as if you are facing an endless emptiness. This perception can be so intense that it could induce the fear that you will be consumed by these feelings. Imagine you were a drop of rain about to fall into the ocean. Could you maintain your sense of yourself as an individual drop, while at the same time being a part of—or one with—the ocean? When you approach the emptiness feelings, you are like that raindrop, and thus the fear of being consumed. But what if you could experience the feeling without fear, but rather with acceptance? Without the fear to feed your perceptions you could then, for example, see powerlessness not as an enemy, but simply as a part of your humanness. Then you could relax into the center of that feeling and discover the peace and joy of your soul, which resides there.

这些空虚感源于你的核心信念。尽你所能地表达其中一种感受，能让你保持对体验者和体验本身的重要觉察。这为什么重要呢？当你初次面对这些原始感受时，你可能会觉得仿佛置身于无尽的空虚之中。这种感知可能非常强烈，甚至会让你害怕被这些感受吞噬。想象一下，你是一滴即将落入大海的雨滴。你能否在保持自身作为一滴雨滴的独立意识的同时，又与大海融为一体？当你接近空虚感时，你就像那滴雨滴，因此会产生被吞噬的恐惧。但如果你能不带恐惧，而是以接纳的态度去体验这种感受呢？如果没有恐惧来滋养你的感知，你就能将无力感视为人性的一部分，而不是敌人。然后，你就能放松地沉浸于这种感受之中，发现你灵魂深处蕴藏的平静与喜悦。

6. Is my feeling, or that of my partner, familiar to me? Typically you will sense immediately that the feeling you are experiencing has been inside you—in exactly the way you are feeling it—for a long time. At first you may think that you had never been that powerless, or that valueless, in your whole life; but with openness comes an awareness of the history of that specific feeling. It becomes a familiar one that you can sense as very old—sometimes even ancient. Getting that sense of familiarity makes it easier to let the other person off the hook for “making” you feel it.

6. 我或伴侣的这种感觉对我来说是否似曾相识？通常你会立刻意识到，你正在经历的这种感觉，其实早已在你内心深处存在了很久——而且是以你现在所感受到的那种方式。起初，你或许会觉得，自己这辈子从未如此无力或如此渺小；但随着你敞开心扉，你会逐渐意识到这种感觉的由来。它会变得似曾相识，你会感觉到它非常古老——有时甚至可以说是远古的。这种熟悉感会让你更容易原谅对方“制造”了这种感觉。

Of course there are some people 40 who will insist that even if it is a familiar feeling, they would not have to feel it if that so-and-so didn’t do something to make them feel it. Sure, I’ve felt unworthy and valueless ever since I was a kid. Everybody feels that sometimes. But you don’t have to make me feel more insignificant! The point is that the feeling came first and, wanting to be healed, began to rise up into your consciousness. When that happens, a neutral situation—and all situations are neutral—was interpreted through the experience of valuelessness. The trick of the ego is to make itself think that the situation came first, but it is always the feelings and emotions that come first, followed by a situation to help you become aware of them.

当然，有些人会坚持认为，即使这种感觉很熟悉，如果不是因为某人做了什么让他们产生这种感觉，他们就不会有这种感觉。没错，我从小就觉得自己一文不值，毫无价值。每个人都会有这种感觉。但你没必要让我觉得自己更微不足道！关键在于，这种感觉先出现，并且渴望被治愈，于是开始浮现到你的意识中。当这种情况发生时，一个原本中性的情境——所有情境本身都是中性的——却被解读成了无价值感。小我的诡计在于让自己认为情境先于情感出现，但实际上总是感觉和情绪先于情境出现，情境的出现是为了帮助你意识到它们。

Now there is always the possibility that you are not in touch with any emotions or feelings. In this case the other person will be expressing them for both of you. If you listen closely, you can identify what it is that the other is experiencing. If you can’t identify any feeling, keep asking your partner to tell you more until you finally do understand. Once you identify it, you can recall a time when you felt like that, and the feeling will come more into your awareness. This will allow you to begin to “join” with your partner.

当然，你也可能完全感受不到任何情绪或感受。在这种情况下，对方会替你们双方表达出来。如果你仔细聆听，就能辨别对方正在经历什么。如果你无法辨别任何感受，那就继续询问你的伴侣，直到你最终理解为止。一旦你辨别出来，就可以回忆起自己曾经有过类似感受的时候，这种感受会更加清晰地浮现在你的意识中。这将使你开始与你的伴侣“融为一体”。

7. What is the history of this feeling? The word familiar has its roots in the word family . It is in the family environment where you first developed your beliefs, these being constructs of thought, picture and feeling. It is also in the family that you first began to consciously experience feelings and emotions. Emotions such as anger, sadness, and anxiety are a mental reaction to the experience of the uncomfortable feelings. 41 These were all experienced in your childhood with members of your family around. The most significant figure is the caregiver (usually Mom, sometimes Dad or a relative) followed by the authoritarian (often Dad, sometimes Mom or a relative). Brothers, sisters, and other relatives follow. You can have significant emotional experiences, both positive and negative, with any of them that will be instrumental in forming personal beliefs. When it is time to grow past that belief, the painful feeling attached to it will emerge and be projected onto a suitable situation, which often appears as a crisis—such as a conflict with a significant person. You can see why it is important to recognize the history of your feelings, so you can be aware of the opportunity to transform the limiting belief into a much more loving one.

7. 这种感觉的由来是什么？“熟悉”一词源于“家庭”。你最初是在家庭环境中形成你的信念，这些信念是由思想、图像和感觉构建而成的。你也是在家庭中开始有意识地体验各种感觉和情绪。愤怒、悲伤和焦虑等情绪是对不适感受的一种心理反应。<sup>41</sup> 这些感受都是你在童年时期与家人相处时体验到的。最重要的角色是照顾者（通常是母亲，有时是父亲或亲戚），其次是权威者（通常是父亲，有时是母亲或亲戚）。兄弟姐妹和其他亲戚也紧随其后。你与他们中的任何一个人都可能产生重要的情感体验，无论是积极的还是消极的，这些体验都将有助于你形成个人信念。当需要超越某个信念时，与之相关的痛苦感受就会浮现出来，并投射到合适的场景中，这通常表现为危机——例如与重要人物发生冲突。你就能明白为什么认识自己的情感历史很重要，这样你才能意识到有机会将限制性的信念转化为更有爱的信念。

Sharing this history with your partner in communication provides a twofold reward. First, it takes the other person off the hook as your antagonist, and allows him/her to be on your side. Since the history of that feeling proves its existence before you had met the other person, s/he can no longer be blamed for creating the feeling in you. Second, sharing the history of your experience allows you to be more clearly aware of it in detail.

与伴侣分享这段经历会带来双重好处。首先，它能减轻对方作为对立面的指责，让他/她站在你这边。因为这段经历证明这种感觉在你认识对方之前就已经存在，所以对方就不能再被指责是你产生这种感觉的原因了。其次，分享这段经历能让你更清晰、更详细地了解它。

8. Can I respond to this in a loving way? Once you have consciously chosen to face your deepest feeling, you can begin to dissolve the fear into your love intention. There is no place you go where love won’t come to find you. For example, if you can bring your full focus to the feeling of powerlessness and give it your acceptance, you are choosing love instead of fear.

8. 我能否以爱的方式回应这种感受？一旦你有意识地选择面对自己内心深处的感受，你就可以开始将恐惧融入你的爱的意愿之中。无论你走到哪里，爱都会找到你。例如，如果你能将全部注意力集中在无力感上，并接纳它，你就是在选择爱，而不是恐惧。

By making a conscious choice for love in the midst of a seemingly overwhelming feeling, you are choosing something greater than the feeling, while at the same time consciously maintaining a sense of who you truly are. I have found the results of such a choice to be truly phenomenal and sometimes frightening. I always thought I was most afraid of painful feelings. After learning to respond to them peacefully, the pain was always transformed into the rebirth of an inherent gift which I had lost and forgotten, an important life lesson that made my purpose clearer, and access to a greater level of fun and creativity. The result is so beautiful that it becomes a matter of whether I can stand having it that good! In truth, I am more afraid of love than I am of the emptiness. Like my friend Chuck Spezzano used to say, “How good can you stand it?” The answer to that question is a moment to moment choice.

在看似难以承受的情绪中，当你清醒地选择爱时，你选择的不仅仅是这种感觉，而是更伟大的东西，同时也清醒地保持着你真实的自我。我发现这样的选择带来的结果令人惊叹，有时甚至令人恐惧。我一直以为我最害怕的是痛苦的情绪。但在学会平和地应对它们之后，痛苦总是会转化为一种我曾经失去和遗忘的内在天赋的重生，一种重要的人生课程，它让我更清楚地认识到自己的人生目标，并让我获得更高层次的乐趣和创造力。结果如此美好，以至于我甚至开始怀疑自己是否能够承受如此美好的感觉！事实上，我更害怕爱本身，而不是空虚。就像我的朋友查克·斯佩扎诺常说的那样：“你能承受多好的爱？”这个问题的答案取决于你当下的选择。

While I was discovering the power of such a choice, another wonderful realization occurred to me. Whenever I chose to respond to pain with acceptance, I discovered my wife right there with me, making the same choice. Since then I have become aware that every time I choose to be completely responsible for my feelings, my wife is beside me, sharing the same pain and bringing love and acceptance to it with the same level of commitment as I am offering. Soon after discovering this miracle of partnership I came up with a simple shortcut, which I must admit I do not always take.

当我逐渐领悟到这种选择的力量时，我又有了另一个美好的感悟。每当我选择接纳痛苦时，我都会发现我的妻子就在我身边，和我做出同样的选择。从那时起，我意识到，每当我选择完全承担起自己感受的责任时，我的妻子都会在我身边，与我分担痛苦，并以和我一样的投入，给予我爱和接纳。在发现这种奇妙的伴侣关系后不久，我想到了一个简单的捷径，但我必须承认，我并非总是会选择它。

The shortcut is:

快捷方式是：

a) Be aware of the emotion behind the conflict and sink into the acceptance of simply feeling it, as well as the emptiness feelings below.

a) 意识到冲突背后的情绪，并接受这种情绪，以及随之而来的空虚感。

b) Love my wife.

b) 我爱我的妻子。

Of course my scientific mind finds this too simplistic, maybe even airy-fairy, but when I forget I have a scientific mind, it works surprisingly well! After all, being my perfect mirror, Su Mei is always reflecting back to me exactly what I’m feeling inside. If I am feeling pain, I will see it in her. By loving her, I am loving my pain and thus I am loving myself. 42 My model suggests that the willingness to feel your feelings responsibly is the key to communication, and thus an effective route through Power Struggle. It may seem to you that your personal makeup is designed against doing just that. I will go into the possible reasons for that in the next chapter. For now, I simply want to establish an understanding around the importance of feeling. If you are positive, you will simply not want to feel, and if you are negative you will think you are already feeling. All I can say is that truly feeling your feelings with an intention to bring peace to them will allow you to feel closer to, and more in love with, your partner, friend, relative, or the guys at work.

当然，我的科学思维会觉得这过于简单，甚至有点不切实际，但当我忘记自己有科学思维时，它却出奇地有效！毕竟，苏美就像一面完美的镜子，总是能准确地反映出我内心的感受。如果我感到痛苦，我会在她身上看到。爱她，就是爱我的痛苦，从而也爱我自己。我的模型表明，愿意负责任地感受自己的情绪是沟通的关键，也是化解权力斗争的有效途径。你或许会觉得，你的性格似乎天生就不适合这样做。我会在下一章探讨其中的可能原因。现在，我只想阐明感受的重要性。如果你总是积极乐观，你就会不想去感受；如果你总是消极悲观，你会觉得自己已经感受到了。我只能说，真正地感受自己的情绪，并努力让它们平静下来，会让你与伴侣、朋友、亲人或同事更加亲近，也更加爱他们。

There are two more things I want to share with you regarding the adventure of conscious communication. The first is that sometimes people who use these methods claim that they seem to work initially, but don’t hold up in the long run. One client stated that they sincerely followed the guidelines and were rewarded with wonderful results, only to be caught up in the “same old shit” the next day. As this was the same result I experienced, it led me to see that the waves of conflict can come in twos, sometimes—but rarely—threes. It is best to be prepared for that second wave, and keep trusting the communication/feeling process. When aligned with your sincere intention, it will always lead you to a better place.

关于正念沟通的探索之旅，我还想和大家分享两点。首先，有些人使用这些方法时，起初似乎有效，但长期来看却不尽如人意。一位客户说，他们真心实意地遵循了指导原则，也获得了令人欣喜的结果，但第二天却又陷入了“老一套”的困境。由于我也经历过同样的情况，这让我意识到冲突的浪潮可能会两波接一波地袭来，有时——但很少——甚至三波。最好是为第二波浪潮做好准备，并继续信任沟通和感受的过程。只要你的意图与你的真诚相符，它总会引领你走向更好的未来。

The second point I want to share is that I have tried to memorize these guidelines; I have taped them to my refrigerator door, bathroom mirror and kept them by my bedside table. I have even taught courses on effective communication skills over the past ten years. Yet when an intense emotional issue arises in my close relationships, my notes are rarely around and my memory all but completely fails me. Conflicts are so packed with pain, emotion, anger, pride, fear, and guilt, that the temptation to revert to primal defence mechanisms can be overwhelming. In those times, willingness to be wrong seems to be the equivalent of daring my partner (i.e. “the enemy”) to blow my brains out. Being totally accountable for my behaviour and that of my partner’s is like admitting that I’m the bad guy and should be punished while at the same time relieving my partner of any culpability in the situation. When it comes right down to the intense heat, numbing coldness, or overwhelming emotionalism of a Power Struggle, it is difficult to keep a clear head. The guidelines, if remembered at all, seem flimsy or trivial, and we can lose sight of our heart’s goal altogether. So what’s the use of offering these pointers?

我想分享的第二点是，我曾努力记住这些准则；我把它们贴在冰箱门上、浴室镜子上，还放在床头柜上。过去十年里，我甚至还教过有效沟通技巧的课程。然而，当亲密关系中出现激烈的情绪冲突时，我的笔记往往不在身边，记忆也几乎完全失效。冲突中充满了痛苦、情绪、愤怒、骄傲、恐惧和内疚，以至于人们很容易被原始的防御机制所诱惑。在那种情况下，愿意承认错误似乎就等同于挑衅我的伴侣（也就是“敌人”），让他们把我爆头。完全承担自己和伴侣的行为责任，就如同承认我是坏人，应该受到惩罚，同时又免除了伴侣在这件事上的任何责任。当权力斗争的激烈程度、冷酷程度或令人窒息的情绪爆发时，保持清醒的头脑是很难的。这些指导原则，即便有人记得，也显得苍白无力或无关紧要，我们甚至可能完全忘记自己真正的目标。那么，提供这些建议又有什么用呢？

The above principles and guidelines are intended to open our minds to the possibility of absolute resolution of any conflict. Many of us never conceived of anything greater than compromise in interpersonal communication. We grew up with the slogan that relationship was a matter of “give and take,” whereas this model offers the possibility for “give and receive.” I don’t want to take anything from my partner—I’d feel like a thief. I’d much rather receive what she offers me freely. But even after reading these principles thoroughly, you may believe that it is only an ideal, something that works in theory but has no place on the planet, much less your own relationships. I encourage you to put these guidelines to the test. Listen to your partner as if it was your own mind talking to you. Take an emotional risk. You have nothing to lose but your righteous position and the uncomfortable tension of interpersonal strife. With the appropriate intention, these guidelines have worked for myself and many other people over and over again. I know their value.

以上原则和指导原则旨在帮助我们敞开心扉，认识到彻底解决任何冲突的可能性。我们中的许多人从未想过人际沟通中除了妥协之外还有什么更好的方式。我们从小就被灌输“有付出有回报”的观念，而这种模式则提供了“付出与接受”的可能性。我不想从伴侣那里索取任何东西——那样我会觉得自己像个小偷。我更愿意接受她无条件给予我的东西。但即便你仔细阅读了这些原则，你或许仍然会认为这只是一种理想，一种理论上可行但在现实生活中行不通的方法，更遑论运用到你自己的人际关系中。我鼓励你尝试这些指导原则。倾听你的伴侣，就像倾听你自己的心声一样。承担一些情感上的风险。你不会失去的只是你自以为是的立场以及人际冲突带来的不适感。只要用心，这些指导原则已经一次又一次地帮助了我以及许多其他人。我知道它们的价值。

I also know that when emotions and fears arise, doubt infiltrates our commitment to a harmonious resolution. That is why it is vital for us to continually ask ourselves the most important question throughout our attempt to communicate; as a matter of fact, it is probably the most important question in the world: “What do I want?” As you penetrate the deeper levels of the human mind, you find that all things manifested in the world are done through will. It is our heart’s willingness to see the possibility of a complete and transformational resolution of conflict in any given situation, and the determination to accept nothing less, that ultimately allows the Truth of who we are to manifest itself and thereby resolve any problem. I have been in a number of unsolvable situations whereby I scratched up enough courage to commit to that Truth, and I have been witness to miracles thereafter. Situations that showed no signs of hope, much less resolution, were somehow concluded successfully, with both parties emerging as happy winners.

我也知道，当情绪和恐惧涌上心头时，怀疑会侵蚀我们对和谐解决问题的决心。因此，在沟通的过程中，我们必须不断地问自己一个至关重要的问题；事实上，这或许是世界上最重要的问题：“我想要什么？”当你深入探索人类心灵的深处，你会发现世间万物皆由意志所驱动。正是我们内心渴望看到在任何情况下冲突都能得到彻底且具有变革意义的解决，并决心绝不接受任何妥协，最终才能让我们的真我得以显现，从而解决任何问题。我曾多次身处看似无解的困境，但我鼓起勇气，坚定地相信真我，并亲眼见证了之后发生的奇迹。那些看似毫无希望，更遑论解决的局面，最终却以某种方式圆满解决，双方都从中获得了幸福。

There were also many times when I had no such courage. More than the Truth, I wanted to remain safe behind my walls, or else I wanted to be right more than happy. In those times I sacrificed loved ones and turned them into enemies, withdrawing from or attacking them without compassion. The result was never harmonious or satisfying; its reward was the isolation of separation. These unhappy results did not occur because of mistakes that I made. Mistakes are an inevitable part of learning. No, they ended up unhappy because of what I wanted from the communication.

也有很多时候，我没有这样的勇气。比起真理，我更想待在自己的围墙之内，或者说，我更想证明自己是对的，而不是追求真正的快乐。在那些时候，我牺牲了挚爱之人，将他们变成了敌人，冷酷无情地疏远或攻击他们。结果从来都不是和谐或令人满意的；它带来的只有孤立和分离。这些不幸的结局并非源于我的错误。错误是学习过程中不可避免的一部分。不，它们最终的不幸源于我对沟通的期待。

Therefore, there is one last suggestion that has saved my ass on more occasions than I can remember, and it is that when all else fails…surrender! Once, an issue arose in my marriage that brought us to the brink of divorce. The attempts at communication had gone on for a month, and even with my precious notes, I kept hitting the brick wall of despair. When at last it looked like the only thing to do was call a lawyer, I suddenly remembered the quote, “Love your enemy.” Following that another quote came to mind, this from Julius Caesar: “l have seen the enemy and the enemy is me.” I looked at my wife and realized that I had made her my enemy—the source of what threatened my safety and well-being. Really what was threatening my peace was my own destructive tendencies, such as my self-doubts, unworthiness, pride, feelings of isolation, jealousy, loneliness and yes, my self-hatred. It was these and other such inner demons that threatened my happiness, and in that moment I realized that these judgments and limitations could not be the Truth. Only feelings and thoughts that inspired love, happiness, and a true communion with my partner could point to the Truth.

因此，我还有最后一个建议，它曾无数次救我于水火之中，那就是：当所有方法都失效时……投降！有一次，我的婚姻出现了一个问题，几乎让我们走到了离婚的边缘。我们尝试沟通了一个月，即使我做了笔记，也依然碰壁，陷入绝望的深渊。当我觉得唯一的办法就是找律师时，我突然想起了那句名言：“爱你的敌人”。紧接着，我又想起了凯撒的一句名言：“我已看见敌人，而敌人就是我自己。”我看着我的妻子，意识到我已经把她当成了我的敌人——威胁我安全和幸福的根源。实际上，真正威胁我内心平静的是我自身的破坏性倾向，比如我的自我怀疑、无价值感、骄傲、孤独感、嫉妒、寂寞，以及，是的，我的自我憎恨。正是这些以及其他类似的内心挣扎威胁着我的幸福，在那一刻我意识到，这些评判和限制绝不可能是真理。只有那些能够激发爱、幸福以及与伴侣之间真正联结的感受和想法，才能指向真理。

Finally I reached out beyond those oppressive influences and, envisioning a beautiful light in my imagination, called out to my soul, asking that it give me the words to say. Because more than anything else at that moment, I wanted the Truth. And from the depths of my pain came a tearful appreciation for my wife, and an expression of how important she was to me. Every word of it was true, and although I had said pretty much the same thing before, it had had no effect. Before I had been saying the right thing, but only to manipulate my partner, because I was still protecting myself from her as if she were my enemy. She was wrong and I was right. If we had stayed there, I can easily see that we would have been stuck there for years. But by some incredibly good fortune, I forgot my personal investments and remembered what was important, and so surrendered to what was best for both my wife and me. The result was an internal shift, a sense of movement out of the deadlock and back onto the path of a relationship that worked. Will I remember to surrender the next time such an intense conflict arises? I sincerely hope so, but there is no way that I can realistically guarantee it.

最终，我挣脱了那些压抑的影响，在想象中描绘出一道美丽的光芒，向我的灵魂呼唤，请求它赐予我该说的话。因为在那一刻，我最渴望的莫过于真相。痛苦深处涌起一股泪水，表达了对妻子的感激之情，以及她对我有多么重要。我说的每一个字都是真心话，虽然我以前也说过几乎同样的话，但却毫无作用。以前我说的都是对的，但那只是为了操控我的伴侣，因为我仍然像对待敌人一样保护着自己。她错了，我是对的。如果我们继续这样下去，我很容易就能预见到我们会陷入这种僵局多年。但幸运的是，我忘记了个人的执念，记起了什么才是最重要的，于是我顺从地选择了对我和妻子都最好的道路。结果是内心发生了转变，一种摆脱僵局、重回正轨的感觉。下次再遇到如此激烈的冲突时，我还能记得顺从吗？我衷心希望如此，但实际上我无法做出任何保证。

It seems that the most important key to all communication is surrender. Once you surrender to the Truth (whether you call the Truth God, Heaven, the Universe, Love, Jesus, the Buddha, Krishna, Fred, etc.), your soul can guide you. It will put the words in your mouth, and take you step by step through the process to the light of union with your partner. Sometimes you will be guided to reveal a deep level of pain that you have carried seemingly forever. Sometimes it will guide you to reach out to the other with love, appreciation, and gratitude. Sometimes it will guide you to release your partner from the prison of your expectations. However you are directed, it will always lead you towards the centre of your being where you and your partner (and everyone else in the world) are one.

沟通的关键似乎在于臣服。一旦你臣服于真理（无论你称之为上帝、天堂、宇宙、爱、耶稣、佛陀、克里希纳、弗雷德等等），你的灵魂便能指引你。它会引导你开口，一步步带领你走向与伴侣合一的光明。有时，它会指引你揭示内心深处似乎永远背负的痛苦；有时，它会指引你以爱、欣赏和感恩之心去关怀对方；有时，它会指引你将伴侣从你期望的牢笼中解脱出来。无论你受到怎样的指引，它最终都会引领你走向你存在的中心，在那里，你与你的伴侣（以及世间万物）融为一体。

My suggestion to any couple experiencing the Disillusionment stage of relationship and are caught up in Power Struggle or control games is to seriously study the principles of conscious communication and understand them as much as possible. Then, in the heat of a serious conflict, trust your heart and soul to guide you, and your sincere surrender will put those techniques in the hands of your Soul—who definitely knows how to use them better than you do. As in all things, when you know what you want, the how is revealed. You might feel more encouraged to practice conscious communication if you were to realize the alternative. If you do not resolve the Power Struggle in a harmonious manner, you will be facing the possibility of pushing the relationship into the third form of misguided behaviour...

对于任何正经历关系幻灭阶段、深陷权力斗争或控制游戏的伴侣，我的建议是认真学习并尽可能深入地理解有意识沟通的原则。然后，在激烈的冲突中，相信你的内心和灵魂会指引你，你真诚的臣服会将这些技巧交到你的灵魂手中——它肯定比你更懂得如何运用它们。正如所有事情一样，当你明白自己想要什么时，方法自然就会显现。如果你意识到另一种选择，你或许会更有动力去实践有意识的沟通。如果你不能以和谐的方式解决权力斗争，你很可能会将这段关系推向第三种误入歧途的行为模式……

***

REVENGE

复仇

———————————

“Revenge is a dish best served cold.”

“复仇最好是冷着吃。”

—“Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan.”

——《星际迷航II：可汗之怒》。

The tendency towards revenge is usually present even in the early stages of Power Struggle, when you unconsciously try to hurt your partner in order to alleviate some of your own suffering. There is an icy pleasure that comes with revenge, but this behaviour can quickly become addictive. For one thing, it is simply too easy to turn your attention to getting even, compared to the effort it takes to rise above your pain. Why not just comfort yourself with the knowledge that your partner is suffering at least as much as you are? The problem is that you will add the guilt of hurting someone close to you to your pain, and this will tempt you to exact even more revenge on your partner. If you listen to some people in the throes of an especially violent divorce, you would question whether the two ever cared for each other at all. The fight over money and property, although rationalized with reason and logic, is almost always a vengeful attempt at punishment.

即使在权力斗争的初期，复仇的倾向通常也已出现，你会不自觉地试图伤害伴侣，以减轻自身的痛苦。复仇会带来一种冰冷的快感，但这种行为很容易上瘾。一方面，与克服痛苦所需的努力相比，将注意力转移到报复上实在太容易了。为什么不安慰自己说，你的伴侣至少和你一样痛苦呢？问题在于，你会将伤害亲近之人的内疚感加重自己的痛苦，这会诱使你对伴侣进行更彻底的报复。如果你听听那些正经历激烈离婚的人的诉说，你会怀疑他们是否曾经真正爱过彼此。对金钱和财产的争夺，即使用理性和逻辑来解释，几乎总是出于报复心理。

I learned how early revenge can appear in our childhoods from my son when he was three years old. Although he was one of the most easy-going three-year-olds in the world, Harmon did give us some difficulty in one area—he NEVER wanted to go to bed. If he could have it his way, he’d keep going until the early hours of the morning, with my wife and I heading off to bed and reminding him to turn off all the lights before he retired. Even if he did go to bed, he never slept until about eleven or twelve. One night I became determined that Harmon would go to bed at a normal hour. At eight o’clock I picked him up and put him into his bed. He came out of the room. I put him back. He came out again. I put him back. By nine thirty he was very upset and I was very tired. Through the whole ordeal, I had managed to remain calmly determined. I put him back into his room, and this time he did not come out. He cried for a while and I went to sit down in the living room, prepared to go back upstairs should he make another break for it. Finally he stopped crying and became quiet. Very quiet.

我从儿子身上学到，报复的苗头在童年时期就已初露端倪。他三岁的时候，虽然是世界上最乖巧懂事的孩子之一，但哈蒙在某一方面却让我们头疼不已——他从来不肯睡觉。如果可以的话，他会一直玩到凌晨，我和妻子只能先去睡觉，提醒他睡前关灯。就算他真的上了床，也总是要到十一二点才睡。一天晚上，我下定决心要让哈蒙按时睡觉。八点钟，我把他抱起来放到床上。他又跑了出来。我把他放回去。他又跑了出来。我又把他放回去。到了九点半，他非常生气，我也筋疲力尽。尽管如此，我还是努力保持冷静和坚定。我把他放回房间，这次他没有再出来。他哭了一会儿，我走到客厅坐下，准备着如果他再次逃跑就立刻上楼。最后他停止了哭泣，安静了下来。非常安静。

Too quiet. There is a certain kind of quiet which makes parents immediately suspicious, though it sounds like any other kind of quiet to the untrained ear. With this particular kind of quiet, you don’t dare go to sleep, or you might very well wake up with the house burned down all around you. I went back upstairs and opened the door to Harmon’s room. He was in bed, quietly tearing the wallpaper off of the wall. How did I know this was revenge? His face was peaceful, and when he looked up at me there was no anger in his eyes. I knew it was revenge from the way that I felt . I was stung by a deep hurt, the kind of hurt that makes you want to ask with teary eyes, “How could you do this to me?” My son must have felt that he had lost the struggle, and therefore had no recourse but to get even with me and thus hang on to some sense of personal power. 43

太安静了。有一种安静，会让父母立刻起疑心，尽管在不熟悉的人听来，它和其他的安静没什么两样。在这种特别的安静下，你根本不敢入睡，否则很可能醒来时发现房子已经烧毁了。我回到楼上，打开哈蒙的房门。他躺在床上，正静静地撕扯着墙上的墙纸。我怎么知道这是报复？他的表情很平静，抬头看我时，眼里没有一丝怒意。我从自己的感受中知道这是报复。我感到一阵深深的刺痛，那种痛楚让你想含泪质问：“你怎么能这样对我？”我的儿子一定觉得自己输了，所以除了报复我，以此来保留一丝力量之外，别无他法。<sup>43</sup>

There are simple signs to let you know if revenge is involved in your interactions with your partner. Whenever you feel that your partner’s actions are an attempt to hurt your feelings, whenever you feel stung, betrayed, or humiliated by your partner’s words or actions, there is a very good chance that the Power Struggle has turned into vengeance. Whenever you get a certain smug satisfaction from your partner’s discomfort, or worse, a sense of glee, you are seeking revenge on him or her. You may even hear a spiteful voice disguised in rationality using phrases like “I just want her to know how it feels when she does that to me,” or “Good, I’m glad he’s hurt. maybe he’ll know better next time,” or “This is the only way she’ll ever learn not to treat people that way,” or “Well he hurt me first.” We tell ourselves these things because we know revenge is not good for anybody, but we can’t be the bad guys. Therefore we rationalize our behaviour to make us look like the good guys, meting out judgment to the wicked.

有一些简单的迹象可以让你判断与伴侣的互动中是否掺杂了报复心理。每当你感觉伴侣的行为意在伤害你的感情，每当你感到被伴侣的言语或行为刺痛、背叛或羞辱时，权力斗争很可能已经演变成报复。每当你从伴侣的不适中获得某种沾沾自喜的满足感，甚至更糟的是，感到一丝幸灾乐祸时，你就是在寻求报复。你甚至可能会听到一个伪装成理性的声音，里面充满了恶意，比如“我只是想让她知道她那样对我是什么感觉”、“好，我很高兴他受伤了。也许他下次会吸取教训”、“这是她唯一能学会不那样对待别人的方法”、“好吧，是他先伤害我的”。我们这样告诉自己，是因为我们知道报复对任何人都没有好处，但我们又不想做坏人。因此，我们会为自己的行为辩解，让自己看起来像个好人，惩罚那些作恶的人。

It is crucial that you recognize these signs of revenge in your relationship and choose another course of action. If you examine why you are in your relationship, you will realize that you are not there to hurt anyone. It does not matter who “started it,” because no one is to blame. The pain inside you is calling to be accounted for. When the pain arises and you choose to compound it with more pain, you have lost your direction, and may need to review your purpose in the relationship. If you choose not to respond to the pain in a more mature way than you did as a three or four year old, you cannot mature emotionally; you will live your life defensively, without trust, and all the subtle forms of revenge will become a way of life. Remember, revenge is a two-edged sword that injures the one who wields it as deeply as their target. And although it is extremely easy to succumb to, revenge is not the path of least resistance. It is the path of greatest resistance to the love you want to experience. If you choose revenge, it will ultimately lead you in the deadly direction of Assumed Inadequacy, 44 where the marriage vows change from “I do” to “Why bother?”

至关重要的是，你要意识到这段关系中出现的这些报复迹象，并选择其他应对方式。如果你审视一下自己为何身处这段关系中，就会明白你并非想要伤害任何人。是谁“先挑起的”，这并不重要，因为没有人应该为此受到责备。你内心的痛苦正呼唤着你去面对。当痛苦涌上心头，而你却选择以牙还牙、雪上加霜时，你就迷失了方向，或许需要重新审视你在这段关系中的意义。如果你选择用比三四岁孩童更成熟的方式来应对痛苦，你就无法在情感上成熟；你会生活在防御之中，缺乏信任，所有隐晦的报复手段都会成为你生活的一部分。记住，报复是一把双刃剑，它会像伤害受害者一样深深地伤害施暴者。虽然很容易屈服于报复，但它并非阻力最小的道路。它是阻碍你获得渴望之爱的最大阻力。如果你选择复仇，最终会将你引向“假定不足”的致命方向，44 婚姻誓言也会从“我愿意”变成“何必呢？”

It would be wiser for you to examine the areas of your relationship where you (consciously or unconsciously) try to hurt your partner with words or actions. Coming home late and not calling to let him/her know can be just as effective a form of revenge as a spiteful statement or name-calling. Become aware of your weapons of revenge, and reveal them to your partner. Ask your partner what words or actions really hurt him/her, and make a promise to be more conscious of—and responsible for—your behaviour. Throw down your weapons and choose peace.

你最好审视一下你们关系中哪些方面你（有意或无意地）用言语或行为伤害了伴侣。晚归而不打电话告知，其报复效果可能与恶语相向或辱骂不相上下。意识到你有哪些报复的手段，并坦诚地告诉伴侣。问问伴侣哪些言语或行为真正伤害了他/她，并承诺更加注意自己的言行，并为此负责。放下你的报复手段，选择和平相处。

***

A WINNER WITH AN ATTITUDE

一个拥有态度的赢家

———————————

“If you want a glimpse of your destiny, look at your attitude.”

“如果你想窥见自己的命运，那就看看你的态度。”

—Anonymous

-匿名的

To end this chapter, I would like to return to the issue of pain. One of the biggest lessons that my relationship has taught me has been the necessity of developing a whole new attitude towards the pain that an intimate relationship can bring up. Beside the old heartbreaks and wounds that reach back to my infancy, I have also discovered deeper levels of primary pain that come from being in a human body. These seem to stem from the feeling of isolation that so many of us experience, regardless of how many friends and loved ones we have around us. The fact is that even the most emotionally balanced of individuals may experience loneliness, helplessness, despair, jealousy, and emptiness (to name a few) in their lives. I call this type of hurt “the pain of being human,” and will explore this later on. At this time I simply want to suggest that in order to benefit from our relationships we may want to develop a different approach towards pain itself, maybe something like…

在本章结尾，我想再次探讨痛苦这个话题。我的感情经历教会我最重要的一课，就是必须对亲密关系可能带来的痛苦培养一种全新的态度。除了那些可以追溯到童年的旧伤痛之外，我还发现了更深层次的、源于身为人类的原始痛苦。这些痛苦似乎源于我们许多人都会经历的孤独感，无论我们身边有多少朋友和爱人。事实上，即使是最情绪稳定的人，也可能在生活中感受到孤独、无助、绝望、嫉妒和空虚（仅举几例）。我把这种痛苦称为“身为人类的痛苦”，稍后我会对此进行探讨。此时此刻，我只想提出，为了从我们的关系中受益，我们或许应该培养一种不同的对待痛苦的方式，比如……

***

PROCESS

过程

There are many signals that you are being offered an opportunity to relax into Process, the typical signals being feelings of anxiety, irritation, or anger. For now, let’s just say that any kind of physical or emotional discomfort is actually an invitation to directly experience Process. Here are the steps.

有很多信号表明你有机会放松身心，进入“过程”之中，典型的信号包括焦虑、烦躁或愤怒等情绪。目前，我们只需将任何形式的生理或情绪不适都视为直接体验“过程”的邀请即可。以下是具体步骤。

1. Notice your discomfort.

1. 注意你的不适感。

2. Locate where you are feeling it in your body.

2. 找到你身体上感觉到这种感觉的部位。

3. Put your hand over that location to help you keep your attention there (optional).

3. 将手放在那个位置上，帮助你将注意力集中在那里（可选）。

4. Relax and accept the feeling completely, exactly as you feel it.

4. 放松，完全接受这种感觉，如你所感受的那样。

5. Relax deeper into it, as recognition grows that the feeling is actually an energy, vibrating, pulsating, or radiating in a specific way. It is neutral, neither good nor bad.

5. 随着你逐渐意识到这种感觉实际上是一种能量，它以某种特定的方式振动、脉动或辐射，你可以更深入地放松自己。它是中性的，既非好也非坏。

6. Relax into the heart, or center, of the energy and you will come to the peaceful, joyful power of your essence. Welcome that power to grow in your awareness, and let Process take you wherever it takes you.

6. 放松身心，感受能量的中心，你就会触及到你本质中那平和喜悦的力量。欢迎这股力量在你的觉知中成长，让过程引领你走向任何你想去的地方。

7. Appreciate how amazing the experience is, and how what you thought was a ‘bad feeling’ is actually this wondrous power.

7. 欣赏这种体验的奇妙之处，并意识到你原本以为的“不好的感觉”实际上是一种奇妙的力量。

8. When you feel complete, think about the problem or conflict that seemed to be the cause of your discomfort. If you still feel anxious, irritated, angry, or in any way uncomfortable, you are free to react emotionally, or relax back into process.

8. 当你感觉一切就绪后，思考一下让你感到不适的问题或冲突。如果你仍然感到焦虑、烦躁、愤怒或任何不适，你可以自由地做出情绪反应，也可以放松下来，继续思考。

9. As an individual grows in emotional maturity, he or she sees more clearly that there are always only two options in life: Accept what is (and respond with Process), or reject what is (and react with a fight, flight, freeze, or faint reaction). One option leads to peace, and the other suffering.

9. 随着个体情感成熟度的提高，他或她会更清楚地认识到，人生只有两种选择：接受现实（并以积极的方式应对），或者拒绝现实（并以战斗、逃跑、僵住或麻木等反应来应对）。一种选择带来平静，另一种选择则带来痛苦。

# ↩

CHAPTER 4

第四章

INTROSPECTION

内省

———————————

“I’m starting with the man in the mirror. I’m asking if he’ll change his ways.”

“我首先要问的是镜子里的自己。我想问问他是否愿意改变自己的行为方式。”

—Michael Jackson, “Man in the Mirror”

——迈克尔·杰克逊，《镜中人》

There is a point in our lives where we come to realize that, contrary to The X-Files , the Truth is not “out there.” No one is going to fulfill our needs, no one is going to make us happy, and no one is to blame for the hurts we experienced in our lives. After looking at every external possibility, we gradually come to the conclusion that there is only one place left to look for the causes and effects of our life experiences: within. Beyond the encounter with disillusionment is the next step in the soul’s process of its evolution, which I have called the Introspection Stage.

人生中总有那么一个时刻，我们会意识到，与《X档案》的情节相反，真相并不“存在于外部世界”。没有人会满足我们的需求，没有人会让我们快乐，也没有人应该为我们人生中的伤痛负责。在探寻了所有外部可能性之后，我们逐渐得出结论：探寻人生经历的因果关系，只剩下一个地方：那就是内心。经历幻灭之后，便是灵魂进化的下一个阶段，我称之为内省阶段。

My daughter, Tara, is five years old at the time of this writing. She loves to draw pictures of people, but primarily little girls. Typically her little girls are bigger than the houses she draws. 45 Tara still seems to perceive a largeness in herself that is reflected in her drawings, although she will probably lose this sense of grandeur as she begins to relate more and more to the world around her. The houses will grow and the little girls will shrink. It reminds me of an experience that I had when I was five years old, sitting on the curb on a beautiful sunny day.
