When I realized that I was being strongly urged from within to be myself, the doubt set in with its favourite mantra: “I can’t.”

刚开始做这份工作时，我感觉自己缺乏创造力和灵感，也不确定自己与灵魂的连接。因此，我只能依赖其他优秀导师的方法，或多或少地照搬他们的做法。在第一次工作坊之前，我提前准备好了课程安排，以便知道每个小时该做什么。一想到要站在一群人面前，却不知道下一步该做什么，我就感到恐惧。当学员提出问题时，我会回想之前哪位老师是如何回应类似问题的，然后重复他或她说过的话和做过的事。总的来说，这种方法一开始效果还不错——大概持续了一天。之后，我对这份工作感到厌倦，并且尴尬地发现自己在重复其他老师的话语和理念。有人指出，我甚至连站姿和走路的姿势都像极了那些老师。我所做的一切都不是真正的我。当我意识到内心深处强烈地渴望做回自己时，怀疑又随之而来，伴随着它最爱的咒语：“我做不到。”

As time went on I continued to experience inner disruptions while my heart gently encouraged me to be true to myself, to be more spontaneous, to trust my creative genius, and to give the gifts I was born to give. Meanwhile my doubt screamed back that I didn’t know how to do any of those things, that I was going to fail miserably and publicly embarrass myself. My need for approval from the participants was attacking my heart’s call to “be myself.” What good would being myself do? I can’t just stand there and “be,” silently waiting for some creative idea to come in. What if nothing comes into my mind? People will get impatient—they’ll walk out! What if there’s a limit to what I have to give, and I’ve already reached that limit?

随着时间的推移，我内心的挣扎不断，而我的内心却温柔地鼓励我忠于自我，更加随性，相信自己的创造力，并发挥我与生俱来的天赋。与此同时，我的怀疑却在呐喊：我根本做不到这些，我会惨败，会当众出丑。我渴望得到参与者的认可，这正在与我内心“做自己”的呼唤背道而驰。做自己又有什么用呢？我不能只是站在那里“存在”，默默地等待灵感降临。万一我什么也想不出来呢？人们会失去耐心——他们会离开！万一我能付出的已经有限，而我已经达到了极限呢？

I remember one particular workshop during which my doubts assailed me relentlessly for five days straight. Throughout the first day I was constantly being told that I would never make it. That I had run out of material and reached the limits of my creativity. That there was nothing new I could give people, and everyone would leave by day three. Over the next few days the voice kept telling me that everything I was doing was wrong, insufficient, or phoney. On the fifth day when the workshop ended, my voice of doubt was mercilessly informing me that I had failed; that I should start looking through the newspapers for a different job—I was washed up as a facilitator. Maybe I could get my old job back as an office manager, because the word would soon get out that I had flopped as a workshop leader. It did not matter that over half of the participants were approaching me with enthusiasm and gratitude for a wonderful five-day experience. My doubt told me these people were just being kind or patronizing—or worse, that I had actually fooled them. 88

我记得有一次工作坊，我的疑虑连续五天如影随形，无情地折磨着我。第一天，我就不断听到自己肯定撑不下去。我的素材已经用尽，创意也走到了尽头。我没有什么新东西可以分享，大家到第三天就会离开。接下来的几天，那个声音不断告诉我，我做的每件事都是错的、不够的，或者很虚假。到了第五天工作坊结束时，我的疑虑之声无情地告诉我，我失败了；我应该开始翻报纸找份新工作——我作为培训师的生涯已经结束了。也许我可以回去做办公室经理，因为很快就会传开，大家都知道我作为工作坊主持人失败了。尽管超过一半的学员热情洋溢地向我表达了对这五天美好体验的感激之情，但这都无济于事。我的疑虑告诉我，这些人只是出于好意或居高临下——或者更糟，我真的骗了他们。

For some reason I did not give up on my career, and within a month I was enjoying new heights of creativity, inspiration, and fun in my work. But often I would be revisited by my doubts and go through the same torment all over again. It was through these processes that I began to understand the nature of doubt. What I discovered was:

不知为何，我并没有放弃我的事业，一个月后，我的工作就达到了新的高度，充满了创造力、灵感和乐趣。但很多时候，疑虑会再次袭来，让我重蹈覆辙，再次经历同样的煎熬。正是在这些过程中，我开始理解疑虑的本质。我发现：

1) Doubt is always present in your mind. Since all these thoughts are ego-thoughts their purpose, with doubt at their roots, is to reinforce your ego’s control over your perceptions, thereby blocking out your soul’s influence. In your relationship, this means that you will look at your partner with doubting eyes. How close can you get to someone when you are looking at them in that way?

1）怀疑总是萦绕在你的脑海中。由于所有这些想法都源于自我，它们的目的，也就是怀疑本身，是为了强化自我对感知的控制，从而阻碍灵魂的影响。在你们的关系中，这意味着你会用怀疑的眼光看待你的伴侣。当你用这种眼光看待一个人时，你们之间又能有多亲近呢？

2) The voice of doubt gets louder as you approach an important point of transformation. For example, you may want to break through some personal barrier that keeps you from being more sexually intimate in your primary relationship. Doubt has the ability to handcuff you—or inhibit some other part of your body from being able to move—in response to your soul’s encouragement to step closer.

2）当你接近一个重要的转变点时，怀疑的声音会越来越大。例如，你可能想要突破某种个人障碍，这种障碍阻碍了你在主要伴侣关系中更亲密地相处。怀疑会像手铐一样束缚你——或者抑制你身体的某些部位，使你无法回应内心深处想要更进一步的渴望。

3) Doubt projects trauma from your past into your future. If you fall off a horse, doubt will assure you that you are going to fall off every time you try to ride one for the rest of your life. If you failed in some area of a previous relationship, doubt will try to convince you that you will fail this time as well.

3）怀疑会将你过去的创伤投射到你的未来。如果你从马上摔下来，怀疑会让你确信，你余生每次骑马都会摔下来。如果你在上一段感情中某个方面失败了，怀疑会让你相信，这一次你也会失败。

4) Doubt is used by the ego to maintain a limiting perception of yourself, and block out awareness of your essential nature. Often this is blamed on the partner, but it is really doubt that blocks a person’s essential nature.

4）怀疑是自我用来维持对自身局限性认知、阻碍觉察自身本质的一种手段。人们常常将此归咎于伴侣，但实际上是怀疑阻碍了一个人认识自身的本质。

5) Doubt often uses facts to increase a sense of fear in you. If you want to leave your job to pursue your calling, doubt will remind you that unemployment is high in this country, you do not have enough money to support yourself, and there are not many opportunities for success in the field you want to enter. Statistics are very often the ego’s favourite source of factual evidence to discourage you from taking risks. In relationships, doubt will use the other person’s behaviour, body language, or facial expressions as evidence that there is no hope of getting closer.

5）怀疑常常利用事实来加剧你的恐惧感。如果你想辞职去追求自己的理想，怀疑会提醒你，这个国家的失业率很高，你没有足够的钱养活自己，而且在你想要进入的领域里，成功的机会并不多。统计数据往往是自我最喜欢用来阻止你冒险的事实依据。在人际关系中，怀疑会利用对方的行为、肢体语言或面部表情来证明你们之间没有进一步发展的希望。

6) All doubt is self-doubt. In other words, if you were to say “I can’t trust my mate to love me; I keep thinking that s/he will hurt me sooner or later,” you are actually saying that you cannot trust yourself. What you call “trusting” your mate is really the expectation that she/he will behave a certain way that does not threaten you, or bring up old pain in you. In fact, you are not trusting that you have the strength within you to handle the pain, or the sense of self value that would allow you to love yourself.

6）所有的怀疑都是自我怀疑。换句话说，如果你说“我无法相信我的伴侣会爱我；我总是觉得他/她迟早会伤害我”，实际上你是在说你无法相信自己。你所谓的“信任”伴侣，实际上是期望他/她会以某种方式行事，不会威胁到你，也不会勾起你过去的伤痛。事实上，你并不相信自己有足够的力量去承受痛苦，也不相信自己有足够的自尊去爱自己。

7) Self-doubt is the glue that binds you to your Family Loyalties. Because doubting who you truly are leads to insecurity, you will find it much easier to use the security of belonging to your family in order to reinforce the identity you have assumed. Any time you wish to grow beyond that identity, your doubt will be waiting at the threshold, trying its best to keep you contained within the boundaries of the identity you had moulded yourself to in your family.

7）自我怀疑是维系你对家庭忠诚的纽带。因为怀疑真实的自我会导致不安全感，你会发现利用家庭归属感带来的安全感来强化你已接受的身份认同要容易得多。每当你想要超越这个身份认同时，你的怀疑就会在门槛外徘徊，竭尽全力将你禁锢在你于家庭中塑造的身份框架之内。

8) When you succumb to doubt, you stop trusting life. When you stop trusting life, you start trusting death. This leads to the desire to simply give up on yourself and your life (death temptation).

8）当你屈服于怀疑时，你便不再信任生命。当你不再信任生命时，你便开始信任死亡。这会导致你想要放弃自己和生命的念头（死亡诱惑）。

9) Doubt supports the scarcity conviction: that you are not valuable enough to be loved or to succeed in your life. This scarcity leads to competitive instincts and compulsions, dilemmas, fear of risk, and utter discouragement—all because of the voice of doubt stating that you do not have enough of what it takes to love or to be loved.

9）怀疑强化了匮乏感：你觉得自己不够有价值，不值得被爱，也不值得在生活中取得成功。这种匮乏感会导致竞争本能和强迫症、两难困境、对风险的恐惧以及彻底的沮丧——这一切都源于怀疑的声音，它告诉你，你没有足够的条件去爱，也没有足够的条件去被爱。

10) When doubt is integrated with love, it becomes the seed of discernment. At that point, doubt becomes innocent questioning, which allows you to perceive the nature of all things and choose what is most appropriate for you. Before doubt is merged with the light of your Soul, you can often make choices from a sense of false loyalty, self-deceit, naïveté, weakness of habit, or fear, all of which increase your doubt’s power over you. When the soul transforms doubt, whatever you are presented meets the scrutiny of one who is innocent, and therefore cannot be deceived or misled. Doubt, then, can also be seen as a teacher of discernment.

10）当怀疑与爱融合，它便成为辨别力的种子。此时，怀疑化作无辜的疑问，使你得以洞察万物的本质，并选择最适合自己的道路。在怀疑与你灵魂之光合一之前，你常常会出于虚假的忠诚、自欺欺人、天真幼稚、习惯的软弱或恐惧而做出选择，而所有这些都会增强怀疑对你的控制力。当灵魂转化怀疑时，你所面对的一切都将经受来自纯真灵魂的审视，因此不会被欺骗或误导。由此可见，怀疑也可以被视为辨别力的导师。

If you can remember that doubt always manifests itself most strongly at times when you are called to take a big step in your life, it will make doubt less intimidating. By restating your commitment to the Truth, you will find the strength to step through your doubts into a more expansive sense of who you are. Remember that doubt will use the traumas and mistakes (which it will call “failures”) of your past and project them onto your future. This will tempt you to shy away from what’s ahead of you, and have you running back to something in your past that typically offers an illusory sense of security.

如果你能记住，怀疑总是在你人生需要迈出重要一步的时候最为强烈，那么它就不会那么可怕了。通过重申你对真理的承诺，你将找到力量，克服怀疑，更深刻地认识自我。记住，怀疑会利用你过去的创伤和错误（它称之为“失败”），并将它们投射到你的未来。这会诱使你逃避未来，让你回到过去那些通常能提供虚假安全感的事物中。

When applying this understanding of doubt to your relationship, you will know that your doubts are trying to keep you from greater depths of love when you become aware of one or more of the following:

当你将这种对怀疑的理解运用到你的感情关系中时，你会意识到，当你意识到以下一种或多种情况时，你的怀疑正试图阻止你进入更深层次的爱：

1. You experience the temptation to move away from your partner and toward a stronger romantic interest, or begin to fantasize about having a “better” partner.

1. 你会受到诱惑，想要远离你的伴侣，追求更强烈的恋爱对象，或者开始幻想拥有一个“更好”的伴侣。

2. You sense that you are unable to go any further in the partnership, because you doubt your or your partner’s willingness to change (all doubt is self-doubt).

2. 你感觉你们的关系无法继续发展下去，因为你怀疑自己或伴侣是否愿意改变（所有的怀疑都是自我怀疑）。

3. You perceive that your future with your mate holds more of the same difficulties you’ve been dealing with, and you don’t think you can handle any more hardships (Assumed Inadequacy).

3. 你认为你和伴侣的未来会面临更多你一直在面对的困难，你认为自己无法承受更多的困难（假设能力不足）。

4. You begin to recognize a pattern of personal “failures” that you have followed in all your relationships, and a thought is triggered that this is as far as you’ll ever get in your life, so why not just give up (death temptation)?

4. 你开始意识到自己在所有人际关系中都存在着某种个人“失败”的模式，于是你开始思考，这就是你人生所能达到的极限了，所以为什么不干脆放弃呢（死亡的诱惑）？

Doubt is the main instigator of the idea that there is no point in going on in the present relationship, that you don’t really love each other, and, come to think of it, you got together for all the wrong reasons, so you might as well give up, because there’s no hope in this relationship. Best to leave and find somebody else—somebody who really loves you. Doubt reminds us of how beautiful the Glamour Stage is, and resurrects our fantasy partner in our minds. It will either superimpose that fantasy onto someone outside the relationship, or tell us that the fantasy person is out there somewhere, waiting.

怀疑是导致人们觉得这段感情毫无意义、彼此并不相爱、甚至当初在一起的理由都是错误的，最终选择放弃的罪魁祸首。这种怀疑会促使人们觉得这段感情没有希望，不如离开，去找一个真正爱你的人。怀疑会让我们想起恋爱初期的美好，并唤醒我们心中对理想伴侣的幻想。它要么会将这种幻想强加于感情之外的某个人身上，要么会告诉我们，那个理想伴侣就在某个地方，等待着我们。

When talking about this point in the Introspection Stage, the question is often raised “But what if the right thing to do is to leave the relationship? How can you tell when you are listening to your heart, and when it is the voice of doubt talking to you?” The best answer I can come up with is “listen closely.” Is the voice a loving one or is it coming from fear?

在谈到内省阶段的这一点时，人们常常会问：“但如果离开这段关系才是正确的做法呢？如何分辨你是在倾听内心的声音，还是在听从内心的怀疑之声？” 我能想到的最好答案是“仔细聆听”。这声音是充满爱意的，还是源于恐惧？

The heart is very discerning, and only directs you toward what will enhance your awareness of your soul. Doubt is not concerned with the choice you make (no matter what you decide, it’ll tell you that you were wrong), so long as the choice is made from fear. Keep your mind focused on your heart’s love of the Truth, and no matter what you are faced with in your relationship, your heart will guide you to the best possible direction for everyone involved. You will then see that doubt is not your enemy. Like the “Dweller on the Threshold,” it waits for you to reach a crucial stage in your life where you are being called to grow beyond the limits of your preconceived identity. It steps forward and challenges you to turn back to the “safety” of your independence, for it is the ego’s nature to preserve itself in separation, and thus it craves independence from the intimacy of love and true, conscious partnership.

心拥有敏锐的洞察力，它只会指引你走向那些能够提升你灵魂觉知的事物。怀疑并不关心你的选择（无论你做出什么决定，它都会告诉你你错了），只要你的选择是出于恐惧。将你的心专注于你内心对真理的爱，无论你在人际关系中面临什么，你的心都会指引你走向对所有相关人员都最有利的方向。那时你就会明白，怀疑并非你的敌人。它如同“门槛上的守卫者”，等待着你到达人生的关键阶段，那时你被召唤去超越你预设身份的局限。它出现并挑战你，让你回到独立的“安全区”，因为自我本性就是在分离中保存自身，因此它渴望脱离爱的亲密和真正觉知的伴侣关系。

Do not wrestle with this Dweller; it feeds on the aggression. Be still. Listen to its “truths” and be aware of the fear and pain it awakens in you. Accept it for what it is, and keep calling for the Truth. There is no place you can go where you could be inaccessible to the light of your own soul. As you trust life and keep choosing your heart, you will see that your doubt also serves the Truth, and its function is to strengthen your commitment to your soul’s purpose. Without fire, the potter cannot make a clay vessel suitable for water. Without the flames of doubt, your soul cannot turn you into a strong enough vessel to carry all its light.

不要与这潜伏者搏斗；它以攻击性为食。保持静默。聆听它的“真理”，觉察它在你心中唤起的恐惧和痛苦。接受它的本来面目，并不断呼唤真理。无论你身处何地，你都能触及自身灵魂的光芒。当你信任生命，并不断选择跟随你的内心，你就会明白，你的怀疑也服务于真理，它的作用在于强化你对灵魂使命的坚定信念。没有火，陶匠无法制作出适合盛水的陶器。没有怀疑的火焰，你的灵魂也无法将你塑造成足够坚固的容器，承载它所有的光芒。

Perhaps this is just a false belief of mine; so, as with everything written in this book, I ask you to examine the point I wish to make through the eyes of your heart to verify its validity. My point is that I do not believe your soul is necessarily concerned with the state of your relationship. I am not convinced that it cares whether you are with the “right” person, or how well you get along with each other, or if you are in a relationship at all. So when you get stuck in life and cannot find the strength or desire to move closer to your partner, don’t turn relationship into a religion, whereby you have to make it work or you will be punished as a sinner. Don’t trap yourself in the belief that you have to stay with this person for life. If you are not free to leave a relationship, then you are not free to stay either. In this case staying because you think it is “right” is choosing to sacrifice.

也许这只是我个人的错误观念；所以，就像本书中所有其他观点一样，我请你用心去审视我想表达的观点，以验证其真伪。我的观点是，我不认为你的灵魂必然会关注你与伴侣的关系状态。我不认为它会在意你是否和“对的人”在一起，或者你们相处得如何，甚至你们是否身处一段关系之中。所以，当你陷入困境，找不到力量或动力去靠近你的伴侣时，不要把这段关系变成一种宗教，仿佛你必须努力维系它，否则就会像罪人一样受到惩罚。不要让自己陷入必须与这个人共度一生的信念中。如果你没有离开一段关系的自由，那么你也没有留下的自由。在这种情况下，仅仅因为你认为这样做“正确”而留下，实际上是一种牺牲。

Your soul’s concern for you is that your choices be made in line with your purpose. If staying in your relationship will support your purpose, your soul will completely affirm any steps you take in that direction. If leaving is in line with your purpose, that is what your soul will encourage. Your heart and soul are not concerned with your personal motives for staying or going, but only with what will help you realize who you really are. As long as you are willing to accept your heart’s choices, what is truly best for you in your relationship situation will be made clear to you.

你的灵魂关心的是，你的选择是否与你的目标相符。如果留在这段关系中能帮助你实现目标，你的灵魂会完全肯定你朝着这个方向采取的任何行动。如果离开符合你的目标，你的灵魂也会鼓励你这样做。你的心和灵魂并不关心你留下或离开的个人动机，它们只关心什么能帮助你认识真正的自己。只要你愿意接受你内心的选择，那么在你们的关系中，真正对你最好的选择就会清晰地展现在你面前。

52 我把这个统计数据告诉了我一位特别不满的已婚朋友，她回答说：“分房睡？我真希望我和我丈夫睡在不同的星球上！”

53 其中大多数都是 Chuck Spezzano 博士在其“视觉心理学”模型中称为“死亡区”的症状。

55 In large quantities, as a matter of fact.

55 事实上，数量很大。

56 Karpman was involved with Transactional Analysis in the sixties when he made a basic design called the Drama Triangle.* It had a word on each corner: Victim, Persecutor, Rescuer. I changed it to suit the purposes of this book. * Stephen Karpman, “Script Drama Analysis.” Transactional Analysis Bulletin 4, 26 (April, 1968).

62 你对一个用热敷肿胀肩膀的人有什么期望？

64 And how about the possibility that, as a Rescuer trying to save you, the Victim, your only solution is to completely remove yourself from the situation, thus leaving your partner a victim of abandonment, or else the bitter Persecutor/Victim, blaming you for the misery you caused? Gets complicated, doesn’t it? Where do you think they got the ideas for all those soap operas?

64. 那么，作为试图拯救受害者的救援者，你唯一的解决办法是否就是彻底抽身而出，从而使你的伴侣成为被抛弃的受害者，或者成为怨恨的施害者/受害者，将你造成的痛苦归咎于你？这岂不是很复杂吗？你觉得那些肥皂剧的灵感都来自哪里？

When the burden was really big, I would partake in all four of the above indulgences. Because I was rarely doing what I wanted to do, and never really putting my heart into what I was doing, the resulting sacrifice demanded some form of compensation. 86 我曾多次听到客户坚信，如果他们继续维持那段关系，他们要么会死，要么会杀了他们的伴侣！许多带着这种想法离开的人，在之后的感情中变得更加谨慎和不信任。实际上，他们的一部分灵魂因为在面对人生挑战之前就离开了那段关系而死去。

87 For the sake of this understanding, I call any peaceful, harmonious, compassionate, encouraging, feeling, a loving feeling. A feeling that is uncaring, contractive, defensive, angry, numb, or depressed, a fear-based feeling.

87 为了便于理解，我将任何平和、和谐、慈悲、鼓励的情感称为爱的情感。而冷漠、收缩、防御、愤怒、麻木或沮丧的情感，则称为基于恐惧的情感。

88 In time I learned that my intention for facilitating workshops was greater than my doubts, and that this intention shone through with a grace that supports all sincere commitments. Thus, while I was distracted by my doubts, my soul was working through me, even using my pain as an offering to help others. People close to me knew of my inner torment and were actually inspired by my willingness to keep pushing through my doubts and doing my best to honour the Truth. It just goes to show you that trust is the alchemist’s stone that can turn leaden doubt to gold!

88 随着时间的推移，我逐渐明白，我举办工作坊的初衷远胜于我的疑虑，而这份初衷也以一种优雅的姿态闪耀着光芒，支撑着所有真诚的承诺。因此，即便我被疑虑所困扰，我的灵魂依然在默默地指引着我，甚至将我的痛苦化作奉献，去帮助他人。我身边的人了解我内心的煎熬，他们反而被我克服疑虑、竭尽全力去追求真理的决心所感动。这正说明，信任是炼金术士的石头，它能将铅般的疑虑化为黄金！

CHAPTER 5

第五章

REVELATION

启示

———————————

“Come with me, leave yesterday behind; and take a giant Step outside your mind!”

“跟我来，把昨天抛在脑后；迈出你思维之外的一大步！”

—The Monkees (A seventies rock band)

—蒙基乐队（一支七十年代的摇滚乐队）

It has only been in the last ten years that I have occasionally had the good fortune to journey into the realm of Sacred Partnership. I admit that I do not live in that realm and frequently find myself turning to learn more lessons in Introspection, Disillusionment, and even Glamour. 89 After bouncing back and forth among the levels, I found that even though the previous stages seem to be stepping stones leading in the direction of a true, conscious relationship, at any given time the path can take a sharp turn into another dimension of consciousness, delivering me directly to my destination. It’s like driving a car and following road signs that are directing you to New York City, when suddenly your car becomes a spaceship that lifts off into space, goes through a black hole, slingshots around a white sun, travels a million light years, and delivers you right into the heart of New York, New York. That is the best I can do to describe the experience of Revelation. Time-wise it is a very brief stage, but the effect it has on an individual’s life can be profound. Revelation is the experience that awaits you as you pass the threshold of the doubt that keeps you blinded to your true essence, and it is accessible at any time in your life, showing you that where you want to go is here.

近十年来，我才偶尔有幸踏入神圣伴侣关系的领域。我承认自己并不生活在那个领域，常常需要转向内省、幻灭，甚至是魅力，去学习更多。<sup>89</sup> 在各个阶段之间反复游走之后，我发现，尽管之前的阶段看似是通往真正觉知关系的垫脚石，但任何时候，这条路都可能急转直下，进入另一个意识维度，直接将我带到目的地。这就像开车，沿着路标前往纽约市，突然间，你的车变成了一艘宇宙飞船，升空进入太空，穿过黑洞，绕着一颗白太阳飞行，穿越百万光年，最终把你送到纽约市中心。这就是我对启示体验的最佳描述。从时间上看，这是一个非常短暂的阶段，但它对个人生活的影响却可能非常深远。启示是一种体验，当你跨越了让你对自身真正本质视而不见的怀疑的门槛时，它就会出现；它随时都可能发生在你生命中，向你展示你想要去的地方就在这里。

Imagine a poverty-stricken man who receives a letter that informs him he just won twenty million dollars—but because his perception of himself as a poor man does not allow him to imagine such a thing is possible, he doubts what the message is saying. He then asks a friend to read it and his friend tells him he has won twenty million dollars. Still the man doubts what he is told. A week later he is lying in bed, about to fall asleep, when his eyes pop wide open, his brain starts racing, and he springs up with the realization that he is a millionaire. Suddenly his life is completely changed. In fact he was a millionaire a week ago, but even though the evidence was in his hand, in his mind he was just a poor old man. The transition from poverty to financial wealth took less than a second. This is the power of Revelation.

想象一下，一个穷困潦倒的人收到一封信，信上说他中了2000万美元的大奖——但由于他自认为是个穷人，根本不相信这种事会发生，所以他怀疑信的内容。于是他请朋友帮忙读信，朋友告诉他确实中了2000万美元。但他仍然心存疑虑。一周后，他躺在床上，正要入睡，突然间，他猛地睁开双眼，大脑飞速运转，猛然意识到自己成了百万富翁。他的人生瞬间发生了翻天覆地的变化。事实上，一周前他就已经是个百万富翁了，但即便证据就在眼前，他心里仍然觉得自己只是个穷老头。从贫穷到富裕的转变，仅仅用了不到一秒钟。这就是启示的力量。

Revelation can be dramatic, or it can be subtle. It can fully enter your conscious awareness, or it can seep in without your complete knowledge of its presence. It is the force that creates the experience of learning, and allows all human beings to grow in consciousness. It has often been said that Revelations are the domain of the spirit; that they are impossible to earn, and unpredictable as to whom they will visit. I can never explain why I have been blessed with the few astounding epiphanies I have received—they certainly weren’t rewards for merit, I can tell you that! However, I am not so sure that Revelation is beyond human influence. To me, Revelation is simply my own soul making its presence known to me. When this occurs, what I thought to be true is seen in a clearer light, thereby revealing the falseness in my thinking, or refining the Truth within me.

启示可以是戏剧性的，也可以是微妙的。它可以完全进入你的意识，也可以在你毫无察觉的情况下悄然渗入。它是创造学习体验的力量，使所有人都能在意识层面成长。人们常说，启示是灵性的领域；它无法靠自身努力获得，也无法预知它会降临到谁身上。我永远无法解释我为何有幸获得那几次惊人的顿悟——我可以肯定地说，它们绝非功德的回报！然而，我并不确定启示是否完全不受人类的影响。对我而言，启示仅仅是我的灵魂向我展现它的存在。当这种情况发生时，我曾经认为的真理会以更清晰的视角呈现，从而揭示我思维中的谬误，或提炼我内在的真理。

In relationships, I have seen Revelation take place in three ways. The first is as the force that moves you from stage to stage, usually teaching you through pain and problems. The pain of Disillusionment reveals the false light of Glamour. Introspection reveals the source within you that creates the illusions and false concepts. The Revelation stage exposes the essential you that resides beyond your emptiness and your doubts. Soul Relationship reveals to you your true beloved. Thus every time we learn something of heartfelt value in our lives, we are experiencing Revelation.

在人际关系中，我观察到启示以三种方式发生。第一种是推动你从一个阶段走向另一个阶段的力量，通常是通过痛苦和问题来教导你。幻灭的痛苦揭示了光鲜亮丽的虚假光芒。内省揭示了你内心制造幻象和错误观念的根源。启示阶段展现了你内在的本质，它超越了你的空虚和怀疑。灵魂伴侣关系让你发现你真正的挚爱。因此，每当我们学习到生活中真正有价值的东西时，我们都在经历启示。

The second way is through the previously mentioned epiphanies that seem to be completely out of your hands, and may or may not happen to you. If you do not know the means by which these Revelations occur, it is pointless to idly wait for one, but equally harmful to close the door on the possibility. You don’t have to wait on the dock for your ship to come in—but be ready when it does.

第二种途径是通过前面提到的那些看似完全不受你掌控的顿悟，这些顿悟可能发生，也可能不会发生在你身上。如果你不知道这些启示是如何发生的，那么漫无目的地等待是徒劳的，但完全否定这种可能性同样有害。你不必在码头上等待你的船靠岸——但当它到来时，你要做好准备。

The third way gives you the power to choose Revelations without thinking that you must passively leave it up to the will of Heaven, or wait until you’ve fully graduated from the first three grades of “Relationship School.” One does not necessarily have to make one’s way from stage to stage in order to reach one’s Soul; there is always the opportunity to take a short cut through...

第三种方法赋予你选择启示的力量，而无需被动地听天由命，或等到完全从“关系学校”的前三个阶段毕业。一个人不一定非要一步一步地走完所有阶段才能抵达灵魂的彼岸；总有机会走捷径……

***

THE QUANTUM TUNNEL

量子隧道

———————————

“Dorothy... you’ve had the power to go home all along ... just click your heels together three times and say to yourself, ‘there’s no place like home... there’s no place like home, ... there’s no place like home.”

“多萝西……你一直都有回家的能力……只要你把脚后跟碰在一起三次，然后对自己说，‘没有比家更好的地方……没有比家更好的地方……没有比家更好的地方。’”

—The Wizard of Oz

——《绿野仙踪》

When I was in high school, our chemistry book had an interesting theory about the ammonia molecule NH 3 . The nitrogen atom is located in the centre of a triangle formed by three hydrogen atoms. The hydrogen bonding is so strong that the nitrogen particle should be imprisoned there, but scientists observed that it would disappear and instantaneously reappear outside of the triangle. Then in another instant, it would return to the centre of the molecular triangle. At the time, they hypothesized that the nitrogen went through a “quantum tunnel” outside of the observable reality and came back again, but in a different location. 90 I don’t know if they have updated that theory, but it is an adequate metaphor to describe Revelation.

我读高中时，化学课本里有一个关于氨分子NH3的有趣理论。氮原子位于由三个氢原子构成的三角形中心。氢键非常强，按理说氮原子应该被束缚在那里，但科学家们观察到它会消失，然后瞬间出现在三角形之外。接着，它又会在另一瞬间回到分子三角形的中心。当时，他们假设氮原子通过一个“量子隧道”进入了可观测的现实之外，然后又回到了另一个位置。<sup>90</sup> 我不知道他们是否更新了这个理论，但它用来描述《启示录》确实是一个恰当的比喻。

No matter how trapped we feel by a situation, once we have set an intention to know unconditional love, we have access to a quantum tunnel that can deliver us directly into the embrace of Soul Partnership. It all depends on our readiness. As a result of our surrender, we switch out of “doing” mode into a position of receiving, which is the key element to all conscious relationships. We can receive guidance, inspiration, and vision, any one of which can teleport us instantaneously out of any trap.

无论我们身陷何种困境，只要我们下定决心去体验无条件的爱，就能开启一条量子隧道，直达灵魂伴侣的怀抱。这一切都取决于我们的准备程度。当我们全然臣服时，便从“行动”模式切换到“接收”模式，而这正是所有觉知关系的关键所在。我们可以获得指引、灵感和愿景，它们中的任何一种都能瞬间将我们从任何困境中解救出来。

One example of the quantum tunnel effect comes from a time in my marriage when Su Mei and I were engaged in a Power Struggle, wondering once again if we would ever get through, or if we should start exploring separation before we completely stopped liking each other. I suddenly remembered my friend asking me one day if I wanted to know the secret to becoming abundant in my life. When I admitted that I did, he told me, “The secret is, you already are.” It reminded me of another statement from the movie Jonathon Livingston Seagull . It said something to this effect: If you want to get somewhere as fast as possible, the greatest speed is being there .

量子隧道效应的一个例子来自我和苏梅婚姻中的一段时期。那时我们正陷入一场权力斗争，再次怀疑我们是否还能走到最后，或者是否应该在彻底失去彼此之前开始考虑分居。我突然想起有一天朋友问我是否想知道如何才能拥有富足的人生。当我承认想问时，他告诉我：“秘诀就是，你已经很富足了。” 这让我想起电影《海鸥乔纳森》里的另一句话。大意是：如果你想以最快的速度到达某个地方，最快的速度就是身处那里。

From my miserable little spot in the Power Struggle I considered the wisdom of these words and decided to test them out. Where I wanted to be with my wife was in love; where I found myself was in the grips of a fight. Imagine if I could take one breath and be in love right away. I asked myself “if I were experiencing a loving partnership with Su Mei right now, how would it look?” From somewhere inside me came the idea to perform some service for my wife, which I immediately followed before I had time to think about whether I felt like it or not. She had told me before how much she enjoyed eating a certain dish I cooked, so I went directly to the kitchen. While making the meal for her I felt different, but only so long as I focused on the “giving” in the act. Then I asked myself, if I were deeply in love with Su Mei right now, what would I be feeling? I became more aware of a warmth in my heart, and a lighter, clearer sense in my head. It felt pretty good. Then I asked, if I were to see Su Mei as my beloved, how would she look to me? My mind was filled with an image of her as the beautiful, wise wife and friend I know her to be. Giving space for these loving experiences to grow soon created a closer bond to her, and the previous tension between the two of us gave way to a much more tender feeling. We had a great dinner together, something that seemed impossible an hour before. By my willingness to imagine “being there,” my Soul’s presence could be revealed. 91

在权力斗争中，我身处一团糟，痛苦不堪。我思索着这些话的智慧，决定付诸实践。我渴望与妻子相爱，而我却深陷争斗之中。试想一下，如果我能瞬间坠入爱河，那该多好。我问自己：“如果我此刻正与苏美享受着一段充满爱意的伴侣关系，那会是什么样子？” 一个念头突然涌上心头，想要为妻子做些事。我甚至来不及思考自己是否真的想做，就立刻付诸行动。她之前告诉我她很喜欢我做的某道菜，于是我径直去了厨房。在为她做饭的过程中，我感觉有些不同，但这种感觉只有在我专注于“付出”这个行为时才会出现。然后我问自己，如果我此刻深深地爱着苏美，我会是什么感觉？我感觉到心中涌起一股暖流，头脑也变得轻松清明。这种感觉真好。接着我又问自己，如果我把苏美视为我的挚爱，她在我眼中会是什么样子？我的脑海中浮现出她美丽、睿智的形象，她是我所认识的妻子和朋友。我允许这些美好的体验自然而然地滋长，很快我们之间的联系就更加紧密了，之前两人之间的紧张感也消散了，取而代之的是更加温柔的感情。我们一起享用了一顿丰盛的晚餐，这在短短一小时前还似乎是不可想象的。通过我愿意去想象“身临其境”，我的灵魂得以显现。91

Admittedly these tiny Revelations seemed to be created by my imagination, but what was it that provided the imaginative responses, and how did it occur to me at all to even consider such questions? I would like to say that it was all because of my commitment to the Truth and the evolutionary level of my soul, but I think there is a more relatable explanation than that. 92 First of all, imagination is not fantasy (although the lower mind will use it for such a purpose). Imagination is the Soul’s reminder of all that is possible. Second, the questions were inspired by my choice to see love rather than what was causing the fight. The Soul honoured my choice and employed my imagination to allow me to see the love that was already there, because love never goes. It was then up to me to act on what I imagined, and thus make what was possible a reality. For a time, I was a conscious embodiment of love. 93

诚然，这些微小的启示似乎是由我的想象创造出来的，但究竟是什么激发了这些想象性的回应？我又是如何想到要思考这些问题的呢？我本想说这一切都源于我对真理的执着以及我灵魂的进化程度，但我认为还有一种更易于理解的解释。92 首先，想象并非幻想（尽管低级思维会将其用于此目的）。想象是灵魂对一切可能性的提醒。其次，这些问题的灵感来源于我选择关注爱，而非引发争斗的根源。灵魂尊重我的选择，并运用我的想象力让我看到早已存在的爱，因为爱永不消逝。接下来，我便要根据我的想象采取行动，从而将可能性变为现实。有一段时间，我成为了爱的有意识的化身。93

It is the nature of this life to constantly reveal to you who you are, and what you carry within you. Therefore there is constant potential for Revelation, and all so-called “learning” is simply seeing what is already there. Revelation is the bridge between Soul and personality. The Soul continually reveals itself according to your personal willingness to accept what is being revealed. Revelation is the conduit from the Soul to your conscious mind. What is your Soul revealing to you about your partner this very minute?

生命的本质在于不断向你揭示你是谁，以及你内在蕴藏着什么。因此，启示的潜能永无止境，所有所谓的“学习”不过是看清早已存在的事物。启示是灵魂与人格之间的桥梁。灵魂会根据你个人接受启示的意愿不断展现自身。启示是灵魂通往意识的通道。此刻，你的灵魂正在向你揭示关于伴侣的什么呢？

The quantum tunnel exists in every stage of relationship, so it is possible to even move from Glamour into True Partnership if you and your partner are willing to come together for the sake of seeing beyond the personal veils. See each other the way your Souls see yourselves.

量子隧道存在于关系的每个阶段，因此，如果你和你的伴侣愿意为了超越个人表象而走到一起，甚至有可能从魅力阶段过渡到真正的伴侣关系。用你们灵魂看待自己的方式去看待彼此。

So how can you be in a Soul-inspired relationship? You already are.

那么，如何才能拥有一段充满灵魂的感情呢？其实你已经拥有了。

EMBRACING MY BELOVED (A Vignette)

拥抱我的爱人（小故事）

***

The first time I can honestly say that I saw my wife was about three years after I met her. Up to that point I had had a great appreciation and respect for her. Her innate spiritual wisdom, depth of beauty, kindness, generosity, acuity of mind, and passion were a source of inspiration and even wonder to me. I could not believe how lucky I was to have been given such a wonderful gift in my life. But my boundless gratitude and appreciation for Su Mei was transcended on the night that her essence was revealed to me. We were spending a fairly ordinary night together. One minute I was sitting beside her, sharing a quiet conversation, and the next minute I was seeing and touching her Soul. I was filled with a bliss that I had previously attributed to mysticism or enlightenment, and a thought materialized in my mind that I had been living with an angel for the last three years. Any attempt to describe it further could never do it justice. For days afterward I floated on a wonderful high, looking in awe at the true beauty in this world—and the worlds beyond.

我第一次真正“看清”我的妻子，是在认识她三年之后。在那之前，我对她一直充满欣赏和敬意。她与生俱来的灵性智慧、深邃的美丽、善良、慷慨、敏锐的头脑和热情，都令我深受启发，甚至惊叹不已。我简直不敢相信自己是多么幸运，生命中竟能拥有如此美好的礼物。然而，在她灵魂的真谛向我显现的那个夜晚，我对苏梅的无限感激和欣赏被彻底超越。那天晚上，我们一起度过了一个看似平常的夜晚。前一刻，我还坐在她身旁，与她轻声交谈；下一刻，我便看到了她的灵魂，触摸到了她的灵魂。我心中充满了一种幸福，这种幸福我之前一直认为是神秘体验或顿悟的感受。一个念头突然涌上心头：过去三年，我一直与一位天使生活在一起。任何语言都无法充分描述那种感觉。接下来的几天，我沉浸在一种美妙的幸福之中，敬畏地欣赏着这个世界——以及更广阔世界——的真正美丽。

Of course I didn’t stay up there. After a few weeks, Su Mei and I were wrestling with some dreary issue and we became estranged from that miraculous experience, but I carried with me the memory of the tranquility in my mind and the powerful love in my heart. For a brief time I was well beyond the walls of the Victim Prison. As far as I could see, what was beyond went on forever. I have had similar experiences since then, and each time my beloved is revealed to me, I lose some or all sense of separation. When I embrace my beloved, I experience myself being embraced.

当然，我并没有一直待在那里。几周后，我和苏梅被一些烦心事缠身，渐渐淡忘了那段奇妙的经历，但我心中却始终铭记着那份宁静和那份浓烈的爱。在那短暂的时光里，我仿佛挣脱了“受害者牢笼”的束缚。在我看来，外面的世界仿佛永无止境。此后，我又有过类似的经历，每次我与爱人重逢，我都会失去一部分甚至全部的分离感。当我拥抱我的爱人时，我感受到自己也被拥抱着。

Back in Chapter One, I mentioned how the initial stage of “falling in love” gives us a tiny glimpse of what relationship’s true potential is. Throughout this book I’ve pointed to ways I have been shown, or discovered personally, the various traps of relationship created by the lower mind. Each time we find a way through, we get another taste of the nectar of what I’ve come to call Soul Relationship. After spending even a little bit of time in this experience, we begin to be illuminated with the Revelation that, without exception, love is behind everything that happens . This allows us to trust life more as we endure the birthing processes that are inevitable with each step forward that the Soul takes.

在第一章中，我提到“坠入爱河”的最初阶段让我们得以窥见一段关系的真正潜力。在本书中，我多次指出，我曾亲身经历或发现过低级思维在关系中设置的各种陷阱。每次我们找到出路，就能再次品尝到我称之为“灵魂关系”的甘露。即使只是短暂体验，我们也会逐渐领悟到，无一例外，爱是万事万物背后的根本。这让我们更加信任生命，坦然面对灵魂每一步前进中不可避免的蜕变过程。

The more you are influenced by the Revelations in your relationship, the more clearly you can see the gift and lesson that is being offered behind every problem. The naturalness of your essence gradually seeps into your behaviour and the inclination grows stronger to choose the kinds of work and activities that best express your gifts. The decisions you are called to make are not win/lose decisions, but rather questions of how to discern the most appropriate course of action—or non-action—that would be of utmost benefit to everyone .

你越受关系中启示的影响，就越能清晰地看到每个问题背后蕴藏的礼物和教训。你内在的自然属性会逐渐渗透到你的行为中，你会越来越倾向于选择最能展现自身天赋的工作和活动。你所面临的抉择并非输赢之争，而是如何辨别最恰当的行动方案——或不作为——才能最大程度地造福所有人。

These are the kinds of understandings I have gained through Revelation. Revelation gives you a completely different perspective on the journey, allowing you to see the purpose behind the pain as well as the pleasure. Upon leaving that state and re-submerging yourself in the Power Struggles, disappointments, or stalemates that occur from time to time, the Revelation leaves an indelible imprint in your mind so that you can bring a little hope with you, along with faith that these discomforts will pass as you deepen your commitment to love.

这些都是我通过启示获得的领悟。启示赋予你对人生旅程截然不同的视角，让你看到痛苦和快乐背后的意义。当你从那种状态中走出来，重新投入到不时出现的权力斗争、失望或僵局中时，启示会在你的心中留下不可磨灭的印记，让你带着一丝希望和信念继续前行，相信随着你对爱的投入不断加深，这些不适终将过去。

Whether we take the journey of relationship stage by stage, or slide through the quantum tunnel, it is ultimately by the grace of our soul that love’s purpose is revealed, and we walk through the gates to…

无论我们一步一步地走过感情的旅程，还是穿越量子隧道，最终都是凭借我们灵魂的恩典，爱的意义才会显现，我们才会步入那扇通往……的大门。

89 Although you’d think that I would know better by now!

89 虽然你认为我现在应该更懂事才对！

90 This quantum tunnel theory is one of the few things I remember from chemistry class. Another one is how to cause sudden explosions in the lab.

90 量子隧穿理论是我从化学课上记住的少数知识之一。另一个让我印象深刻的是如何让实验室发生突发爆炸。

91 Of course, if you were to ask Su Mei how we got through that fight, she might tell you it was because she decided to let go of her position, and make love more important. I had a small Revelation that explained this: every step in a relationship towards love is taken simultaneously by both people.

91 当然，如果你问苏梅我们是怎么度过那场争吵的，她可能会告诉你，是因为她决定放下自己的立场，把爱情放在更重要的位置。我突然领悟到一点，这解释了这一切：一段关系中，通往爱情的每一步都是双方同时迈出的。

92 Or at least a more believable one.

92 或者至少是一个更可信的解释。

93 Which brings up the question: when we are not embodying love, what are we embodying—and thus expressing—to our partners, family, friends...and the world?

93 这就引出了一个问题：当我们没有体现爱的时候，我们体现的是什么——从而向我们的伴侣、家人、朋友……以及世界表达的又是什么呢？

# ↩

CHAPTER 6

第六章

SOUL PARTNERSHIP

灵魂伴侣

———————————

“Caterpillar sheds its skin to find a butterfly within”

“毛毛虫蜕皮是为了蜕变成蝴蝶”

—Donovan

——多诺万

When I write about Soul Partnership, I do not intend to draw a picture of what one looks like. Many people might assume that such a relationship would be monogamous by nature. Some might even conceive of it as being holy, in classical religious terms, with the partners having halos around their heads. Still others might hold some other image according to their beliefs and values.

当我谈到灵魂伴侣关系时，我并非意在描绘它的具体面貌。许多人可能会认为这种关系本质上是一夫一妻制的。有些人甚至会用古典宗教术语来理解它，认为它是神圣的，伴侣头顶仿佛有光环。当然，也有人会根据自身的信仰和价值观，对灵魂伴侣关系抱有其他的想象。

Personally, I am not convinced that monogamy is an essential ingredient to sacred relationships, nor do I feel that Soul Partners would comply with anyone’s conceptions of what such partners should look or act like. The more one walks the path of the Soul, the less one is influenced by the glamour of appearances and dogma.

就我个人而言，我不认为一夫一妻制是神圣关系的必要组成部分，也不认为灵魂伴侣会符合任何人对伴侣外貌或行为的固有观念。一个人越是追随灵魂的指引，就越不会受外表和教条的诱惑。

I am not inclined to describe a universal experience of Soul Partnership at all, since how I experience it is according to my individuality. What I hope to make clear in this chapter is that relationship is a spiritual path that reflects love’s plan for all of humanity. That your partner is your teacher is obvious, as is the fact that what you are being called to learn is the way of unconditional love. What people sought in monasteries, ashrams, and mountain tops can be experienced on your living room, a corporate board room, or a South Seas beach at Club Med. In learning to love your partner wherever you are, you learn to love everyone. Every encounter with another human being can then become a spiritual encounter that brings you closer to the realization of love’s plan.

我并不打算描述一种普遍的灵魂伴侣体验，因为我的体验完全取决于我的个人经历。我希望在本章中阐明的是，伴侣关系是一条灵性之路，它反映了爱为全人类制定的计划。你的伴侣是你的老师，这一点显而易见；你被召唤去学习的是无条件的爱之道。人们曾在寺院、静修中心和山巅寻求的，在你的客厅、公司会议室，甚至地中海俱乐部南海的海滩上都能体验到。无论身处何地，当你学会爱你的伴侣时，你也就学会了爱所有人。与他人的每一次相遇都可能成为一次灵性之旅，引领你更接近爱的计划的实现。

***

ALLOWING

允许

———————————

“Whisper words of wisdom, ‘Let it be...’”

“轻声细语，‘顺其自然吧……’”

—Paul McCartney

——保罗·麦卡特尼

Many years ago, I was thinking about gravestones. Not that I plan on being buried when I die, but I was thinking: if I was going to be buried, what words would I want on my gravestone? Out of the blue came the statement “His life was full of doo-doo.” This idea emerged from the sense that I was a very busy young man, always doing something. Doing, doing, doing! Busy, busy, busy. I was constantly pursuing some very important goal, which of course was important only for as long as I was chasing it. Once I reached the goal, all of its importance was immediately transferred onto some more distant goal. 94 No matter how many goals I reached—or failed to reach—I never questioned whether it was truly worth my time pursuing them. “Doing” was my life. It made me useful, provided me with a sense of importance, and gave my existence a certain purpose. But it was often very empty as well.

很多年前，我曾思考过墓碑的问题。倒不是说我打算死后被埋葬，而是我在想：如果我注定要被埋葬，我希望墓碑上刻些什么呢？突然间，“他的一生一团糟”这句话浮现在我的脑海里。这个想法源于我年轻时忙碌的感受，我总是忙个不停。忙，忙，忙！我总是在追求某个非常重要的目标，当然，这个目标的重要性只在我追求它的那段时间里才存在。一旦我实现了目标，它所有的意义就立刻转移到了更遥远的目标上。94 无论我实现了多少目标——或者失败了多少目标——我从未质疑过追求它们是否真的值得。“做事”就是我的生活。它让我觉得自己有用，让我觉得自己很重要，也让我的存在有了某种意义。但它也常常让我感到空虚。

Once again, my wife was instrumental in showing me what all the great sages have been trying to get through to us all along: it’s not what you do, but who you are that counts. In my relationship, I did everything I could to make the marriage work. In my mind, usefulness would make me irreplaceable. Being busy would keep the material aspects of our life stable and secure. My raison d’être was to provide and protect, because, well, that’s what I did to prove to my wife that I was worth keeping. Marriage and relationships were things that I had to do, so, like the rest of my life, my marriage was being contaminated with doo-doo. The problem is you cannot “do” relationship. You cannot “do” communication; you cannot “do” letting go or commitment. As you walk through the veil of the ego’s illusion and begin to serve relationship’s true purpose, the rules change drastically from doing to something else.

我的妻子再次让我明白了所有伟大的智者一直以来试图传达给我们的道理：重要的不是你做了什么，而是你是什么样的人。在我的婚姻中，我竭尽所能地维系着这段关系。在我看来，只要有用，我就无可替代。忙碌能让我们的生活物质稳定无虞。我存在的意义就是供养和保护，因为，嗯，我这样做是为了向妻子证明我值得她留住。婚姻和人际关系对我来说是必须要做的事情，所以，就像我生活的其他方面一样，我的婚姻也受到了各种糟粕的污染。问题在于，你无法“做”出一段关系。你无法“做”出沟通；你无法“做”出放手或承诺。当你拨开自我幻象的迷雾，开始真正理解关系的意义时，规则就会发生翻天覆地的变化，从“做”变成“做”。

When the spiritual teacher Guru Maharaji was a young man, he was asked what the most important word in the English dictionary was. His reply was, “let.” He must have been on the other side of the Wall when he said that, because Soul Relationships are all about allowing. You don’t just sit in a chair and remain inactive, of course. It is simply that your actions are more often directed by who you are in your heart, rather than who you think you have to be. When in the state of allowing, actions emerge from inspiration, creative thought and Revelations. When you look at the chart below, it is easy to see the vast difference in terms of quality of life, between doing and allowing:

当灵性导师古鲁·马哈拉吉年轻时，有人问他英语词典里最重要的词是什么。他的回答是“允许”。他当时一定处于一种超脱尘世的状态，因为灵魂关系的核心就在于允许。当然，你不会只是坐在椅子上无所事事。这仅仅意味着，你的行动更多地是由你内心的真实自我所引导，而不是由你认为自己必须成为的样子所引导。在允许的状态下，行动源于灵感、创造性思维和启示。看看下面的图表，你就能轻易看出“做”和“允许”在生活质量方面的巨大差异：

You may remember Chapter Three, where we discussed the principles of communication and the necessity of practicing those principles. In the Disillusionment stage, we are often preoccupied with “doingness” and feel the need for a formula to follow. I outlined what may have appeared to be such a formula (the eight questions), but my last words on the subject were about surrender. Because although the practice of guidelines is important, its real purpose is to prepare the individual to follow the steps that a person in conscious relationship would follow naturally . In Soul Partnerships there is less and less doing, and more and more allowing. Communication does not follow a formula, but flows out of an intuition that fills the heart, an inspiration that lights up the mind, and an illumination that reveals our deepest feelings.

你或许还记得第三章，我们探讨了沟通的原则以及实践这些原则的必要性。在幻灭阶段，我们常常执着于“行动”，并感到需要遵循某种公式。我概述了看似这样的公式（八个问题），但我最后谈到的是臣服。因为尽管实践指导原则很重要，但其真正的目的是帮助个体做好准备，去遵循一段有意识的关系中自然而然会遵循的步骤。在灵魂伴侣关系中，行动越来越少，接纳越来越多。沟通并非遵循公式，而是源于充满内心的直觉、照亮心灵的灵感以及揭示我们内心深处感受的启迪。

Typically, actions are not appropriate when the doing comes from a need-based compulsion. In Soul Partnerships the need for specialness is subordinated to the call for what is best for all concerned. The actions that follow this call have a sense of flow and emergence rather than the sense of pressure and emergency that so often accompany the ego’s compulsion to do. In order to live your life in the experience of allowing, you must be able to determine what is influencing your choices of action. Since personal feelings, desires and compulsions are so effective at interfering with your connection to Soul, it is important to develop an ability to allow us to choose freely. This ability I call...

通常情况下，当行动源于一种基于需求的强迫性行为时，这种行为是不恰当的。在灵魂伴侣关系中，对特殊性的需求服从于对所有相关人员最有利的呼唤。遵循这种呼唤的行动具有一种流动和涌现的感觉，而非小我强迫行动时常常伴随的压力和紧迫感。为了体验允许的人生，你必须能够确定是什么在影响你的行动选择。由于个人感受、欲望和强迫性行为会有效地干扰你与灵魂的连接，因此培养一种允许我们自由选择的能力至关重要。我称这种能力为……

IMPERSONAL DISCERNMENT

非个人化的辨别力

———————————

“In matters great and small, the heart always knows best.”

“无论大事小事，心总是最懂事的。”

—Anonymous

-匿名的

In the first three stages of relationship, many of us are largely preoccupied with the personal aspects of our existence. The misguided behaviours, the attractions, the fights, and the Victim-Persecutor-Rescuer entrapments all result from personal feelings related to the pursuit of needs. In those stages we think that the personal is always important. There is little room then for discernment or discrimination since all our decisions are influenced by personal bias. When you step across the threshold into Soul Relationship, you begin to recognize the impersonal nature of the soul, and its focus on a larger picture. Within that picture you can see love’s design for all human beings. In order for the soul to manifest that design in the world, sometimes the personal is willingly subordinated to what is more important—love. When love becomes the priority, personal requirements are handled in the most fulfilling way possible. Being able to determine the most loving course of action amidst all the personal influences, emotional biases, and self-doubts requires the development of your spiritual discernment.

在关系的最初三个阶段，我们中的许多人大多专注于自身存在的个人层面。那些误入歧途的行为、吸引、争吵以及受害者-迫害者-拯救者的角色陷阱，都源于追求自身需求的个人感受。在这些阶段，我们认为个人因素永远至关重要。由于所有决定都受到个人偏见的影响，我们几乎没有辨别力或区分能力。当你跨入灵魂关系的门槛时，你开始认识到灵魂的非个人化本质，以及它对更宏大图景的关注。在这个图景中，你可以看到爱为全人类所设计的蓝图。为了让灵魂在世间展现这一蓝图，有时个人因素会被心甘情愿地置于更重要的事物——爱——之下。当爱成为首要之事时，个人需求便会以最圆满的方式得到满足。能够在所有个人影响、情感偏见和自我怀疑中，做出最充满爱意的行动，需要你发展出灵性上的辨别力。

When I realized this, I became aware of how every true step forward in relationship involves making that choice for love. You can see this if you examine the past Power Struggles in your relationships. Each time you were willing to admit you were wrong, rather than stubbornly defending a position, you sacrificed what was of personal importance to you for the sake of love. Naturally the love benefited you, but when you were making that decision your ego could not see the benefit of your selfless choice, and would have defended its position to the death had its interests not been overshadowed by the power of your heart and soul. Every time you let go of an expectation, chose acceptance over blame, or expressed sincere appreciation instead of judgement, you chose what was important, rather than what seemed important, but was in fact only personal. The love was always there behind the scenes, waiting for you to choose it over everything else. It never pushed itself on you, never manipulated you, never took away your free will. It simply waited for your invitation. I have created another chart to outline some of the differences between the personal and the important. Hopefully this will help you in situations where discernment is required:

当我意识到这一点时，我明白了关系中每一个真正的进步都离不开对爱的选择。如果你回顾一下过去关系中的权力斗争，就能明白这一点。每次你愿意承认错误，而不是固执地捍卫自己的立场时，你都为了爱而牺牲了对你而言真正重要的东西。爱自然会让你受益，但在你做出这个决定时，你的自我意识无法看到你无私选择的好处，如果不是你的内心和灵魂的力量压倒了它的利益，它会誓死捍卫自己的立场。每次你放下期待，选择接纳而非指责，或者表达真诚的感激而非评判时，你选择的都是真正重要的东西，而不是那些看似重要但实际上只是个人利益的东西。爱一直都在幕后，等待着你选择它，而不是其他一切。它从不强迫你，从不操纵你，从不剥夺你的自由意志。它只是在等待你的邀请。我还制作了另一张图表来概述个人利益和重要利益之间的一些区别。希望这能帮助你在需要辨别是非的情况下做出判断：

Once again I ask you to simply get a sense of the natures of these two columns. It may be worth noting that the qualities of what is important are some of the qualities of the soul’s nature and what it supports in your life. I do not want to insinuate that your personal goals, points of view, feelings or desires are not important. I wish only to point out how much happier we will be when what is of personal importance to us is harmonious with what is important to our Soul.

我再次恳请各位理解这两栏内容的本质。值得注意的是，真正重要的事物所蕴含的特质，正是灵魂本质及其在生活中所支持的特质。我并非暗示您的个人目标、观点、感受或愿望不重要。我只是想指出，当我们个人重视的事物与灵魂重视的事物和谐一致时，我们会感到多么幸福。

You never need to seek, pursue, or earn love, because it is not hiding, running away, or demanding any price from you. You need only to allow a space for it in your awareness and the love will be there (because it already is). Thus, discernment becomes vital, so that you can rise above the emotions, volatile feelings, mental confusions, and personal compulsions, and perceive the one choice that would invite love in. Inevitably it is a choice that is best for you and your partner. I recall one occasion when such a choice involved ending a relationship with a wonderful girlfriend. Although we were getting along great, I could sense that my heart was telling me to move on. My girlfriend did not agree with my discernment, and seeing her unhappiness caused great guilt to surge through me, attempting to sway me away from my heart. However, my heart was quite clear that the choice to end our relationship was true. I also felt sure that, though she didn’t know it, somewhere in her mind my girlfriend was choosing to end the relationship as well. Trusting this inner knowing, I communicated to her what was in my heart. I didn’t try to rationalize or justify, but simply spoke what felt true. We parted tearfully and in peace. Even though we were breaking up, my experience was of being in a loving partnership with her. The next day she met the man who was to become her husband.

你永远不需要刻意去寻找、追求或赢得爱，因为它不会躲藏、不会逃避，也不会向你索取任何代价。你只需要在意识中为它留出一席之地，爱就会在那里（因为它本来就在那里）。因此，辨别力至关重要，它能让你超越情绪、变幻莫测的感觉、精神上的困惑和个人的冲动，从而觉察到那个能吸引爱的选择。而这个选择必然是对你和你的伴侣都最好的。我记得有一次，我面临着这样的选择，那就是结束一段与一位很棒的女友的感情。虽然我们相处得很好，但我能感觉到我的内心在告诉我应该继续前进。我的女友并不认同我的判断，看到她的不快乐，我感到深深的内疚，这试图动摇我的决心。然而，我的内心非常清楚，结束这段感情的选择是正确的。我也确信，虽然她自己并不知道，但她内心深处也在做出同样的选择。我相信内心的直觉，向她倾诉了我的心声。我没有试图辩解或解释，只是如实说出了我的感受。我们含泪告别，但彼此平静。虽然我们分手了，但我的感受却是与她曾拥有一段充满爱的伴侣关系。第二天，她遇到了未来的丈夫。

“We’ll have a picnic on the edge of the abyss, and turn our backs to the precipice.”

—From the movie, “Reuben, Reuben” (1983)

——出自电影《鲁本，鲁本》（1983）

The fact that we are nearing the end of this book in no way indicates that the Soul Partnership stage is the end of the journey. The experiences available from this point on are in fact countless. The heights and depths of humanity’s spiritual reality await the traveller for whom the trials, lessons, and gifts within the higher/deeper realms take on the characteristics of the mythical, symbolic, and increasingly purer aspects of energy.

本书即将完结，但这并不意味着灵魂伴侣阶段就是旅程的终点。事实上，从此刻起，我们将体验到无数种人生经历。对于那些能够领悟更高/更深层次领域中种种考验、教训和馈赠的旅者而言，人类精神现实的巅峰与深渊正等待着他们去探索，并最终领悟到其中蕴含的神话、象征以及日益纯粹的能量特质。

Once the commitment to a relationship based on the guidance of one’s soul is made, the process of integrating one’s personality with the Soul’s energy begins in earnest. To achieve this, it is necessary to gain mastery over one’s body, feelings, and mind. It was often believed in the past that to gain such mastery one must remove oneself from the distractions and temptations of society. This cloistered lifestyle often meant a commitment to chastity, poverty, and complete obedience to the authority of the temple. These days, everyday relationships have become our temples, and vows of poverty, chastity and obedience have been replaced by one’s responsibility to become a mature, discerning individual.

一旦基于灵魂指引而建立关系，将自身人格与灵魂能量融合的过程便正式开始。为了达成这一目标，必须掌控自己的身体、情感和思想。过去人们常常认为，要获得这种掌控力，就必须远离社会的纷扰和诱惑。这种隐居的生活方式通常意味着要恪守贞洁、清贫，并完全服从圣殿的权威。如今，日常关系已成为我们的圣殿，而清贫、贞洁和服从的誓言已被成长为成熟、有辨别力的个体的责任所取代。

Although there are many great books describing the glories an individual can experience, there is remarkably little writing on how these bounties are experienced and shared in the area of human relationships. In my perusal of the great spiritual works, philosophies, and esoteric teachings, little is written about the spiritual importance of human relationships, while much is written about man’s relationship to God and the “Higher Realms.” In my life I have received many great learnings from spiritual gurus and teachers. I have leapt in ecstasy with what might be called “cosmic experiences.” So far, however, most of my practical lessons about unconditional love have come through my wife, children, family, friends, acquaintances… in short, through my fellow human beings.

尽管有很多伟大的书籍描述了个人所能体验到的种种荣耀，但关于如何在人际关系中体验和分享这些恩赐的著述却少之又少。在我研读的伟大灵性著作、哲学和秘传教义中，鲜有提及人际关系的灵性重要性，而关于人与神以及“更高境界”的关系却著述颇丰。我一生中从灵性导师那里获得了许多宝贵的教诲，也曾体验过令人欣喜若狂的“宇宙体验”。然而，迄今为止，我关于无条件的爱的实践经验大多来自我的妻子、孩子、家人、朋友、熟人……简而言之，来自我的同胞。

At the Soul Partnership level, you have the opportunity to meet your first true teacher: your own soul. Until you recognize your soul, it is very difficult to recognize who your other teachers are, thus making it easy to be misled by the glamour of a so-called master, idol, priest, psychiatrist, psychologist, or talk-show host, 95 while at the same time completely missing the fact that your partner can be clearly expressing what your soul wants you to learn. Once you do recognize your teacher within, you begin to see this teacher manifest through other people, beginning with your most significant relationship and, in time, moving out from there. Ultimately, every encounter with another human being becomes a spiritual encounter, since each encounter is the opportunity to see everyone as a spiritual being in a human form.

在灵魂伴侣层面，你有机会遇见你的第一位真正的导师：你自己的灵魂。在你认清自己的灵魂之前，很难认清其他导师是谁，因此很容易被所谓的“大师”、“偶像”、“牧师”、“精神科医生”、“心理学家”或“脱口秀主持人”的光环所迷惑，同时完全忽略了你的伴侣其实可以清晰地表达你的灵魂想要你学习的内容。一旦你认清了你内在的导师，你就会开始看到这位导师通过其他人显现出来，首先从你最重要的关系开始，然后逐渐扩展到其他人。最终，与他人的每一次相遇都成为一次灵性相遇，因为每一次相遇都是一次将每个人视为拥有人类形态的灵性存在的机会。

This book has taken me over two years to complete. I believe it has taken this long because I wanted it to be, as much as possible, in complete and honest alignment with my own experience of relationship. Su Mei has been the biggest influence in keeping me honest. Being a stalwart loner for most of my life, I leaned on her innate sense of partnership to teach me the basics. I am a poor student: proud, stubborn, slow to catch on, and resistant to change. I also never had any intention of getting married before I met Su Mei, so I entered our relationship as a novice in such things as commitment, communication, and intimacy. As I wrote about each area of relationship, I had to experience it over and over again in order to feel that I knew what I was talking about to an adequate degree.

这本书我花了两年多的时间才完成。我相信之所以耗时这么久，是因为我希望它尽可能地完全真实地反映我自身的恋爱经历。苏美对我保持真诚影响最大。我一生中大部分时间都是个坚定的独行侠，因此我依靠她与生俱来的伴侣关系意识来学习恋爱的基本知识。我学习能力很差：骄傲、固执、反应迟钝，而且抗拒改变。在遇到苏美之前，我从未想过结婚，所以进入我们的关系时，我对承诺、沟通和亲密关系等诸多方面都一窍不通。在写作过程中，我反复体验恋爱关系的方方面面，才能觉得自己对所写的内容有足够的了解。

When I faced unhappiness in my marriage, I was tempted to throw this book away, believing that I had no right to preach what I was not practicing. I have always assumed that those who write books on relationship have mastered all aspects of it. If this is so, then I am an exception to this rule. I spend a lot of time on the edge of the abyss, and it has rarely, if ever, been a picnic. But I’ve noticed that one learns a great deal about this earth when one falls down a lot, 96 and I have learned much about relationship by examining the mistakes I make—having long believed that human beings get to heaven by mistake.

当我的婚姻遭遇不幸时，我一度想把这本书扔掉，因为我觉得自己没有资格宣扬自己没有实践过的东西。我一直以为，那些写关于人际关系书籍的人都精通其中的方方面面。如果真是这样，那我就是这条规则的例外。我常常徘徊在崩溃的边缘，这段经历几乎从未轻松过。但我发现，一个人跌倒得越多，就越能了解这个世界，96 而我正是通过反思自己犯下的错误，才对人际关系有了更深的理解——我曾一度认为，人类最终能上天堂，纯属偶然。

Neither Su Mei nor I know in what condition our relationship will be next year, next month, or tomorrow. I do know that, no matter what the outcome, or how things appear on the outside, we will be doing the very best we can to feel and express love every step of the way. That is true for every human being. I end this book with a passage that speaks to the purpose of this wondrous path of relationship—our bridge to the Soul.

苏梅和我都不知道明年、下个月，甚至明天，我们的关系会变成什么样。但我知道，无论结果如何，无论外人如何看待，我们都会尽全力去感受和表达爱，每一步都如此。这适用于所有人。本书的结尾，我想引用一段话，它诠释了这段奇妙关系的意义——它是我们通往灵魂的桥梁。

94 I made up a kind of mathematical equation which stated that the amount of importance a goal is given (I) is equal to how much we think we need it (N) multiplied by how difficult we think it is to reach (D) (I = N × D). I later revised it by adding how much better my chances were of getting sexually involved (S) with a woman I was interested in if I reached that goal (I = N x D + S).

94 我编造了一个数学公式，它表明目标的重要性 (I) 等于我们认为需要它的程度 (N) 乘以我们认为实现它的难度 (D) (I = N × D)。后来我对其进行了修改，加入了如果我实现了这个目标，我与心仪女性发生性关系的几率 (S) 的增加量 (I = N × D + S)。

95 And don’t forget workshop leaders and counsellors.

95 不要忘记研讨会负责人和辅导员。

96 One learns that the earth is hard, dirty, and causes lots of cuts and bruises. But it also produces beautiful flowers and coloured stones.

美好的事物终将绽放。

About the Author

作者简介

Chris Moon is a husband, father, life coach, lecturer, and workshop facilitator working in North America and Asia. For over 30 years, he has focused on the direct experience of true happiness and its transformational influence on interpersonal, family, and intimate relationships. His unique approach combines practical information with experiential learning, allowing for the beneficial application of this information into real life situations.

克里斯·穆恩是一位丈夫、父亲、人生教练、讲师和工作坊导师，他的工作遍及北美和亚洲。三十多年来，他专注于探索真正幸福的直接体验及其对人际关系、家庭关系和亲密关系的变革性影响。他独特的教学方法将实用信息与体验式学习相结合，使人们能够将这些信息有效地应用于现实生活情境中。

As an author, Chris wanted to approach the fields of relationship and “spiritual growth” with simplicity and humor because, as he put it, “I always enjoyed the humorous teachers in school—they made the driest subjects worth coming to class for. So I thought, maybe serious subjects like family dynamics, parenting and intimate relationship don’t have to be delivered so seriously.”

作为一名作家，克里斯希望以简单幽默的方式来探讨人际关系和“精神成长”领域，因为正如他所说，“我一直很喜欢学校里那些幽默的老师——他们让最枯燥的课程也变得值得来上课。所以我想，也许像家庭动力学、育儿和亲密关系这样严肃的话题，不必讲得那么严肃。”

Perhaps because of this approach, Chris’s books on intimate relationships have reached hundreds of thousands of readers in Asia and North America.

或许正是因为这种方法，克里斯关于亲密关系的书籍在亚洲和北美拥有了数十万读者。

Chris loves the great outdoors and enjoys skiing, biking, jogging, and hiking with his wife, Su Mei. Together they founded Vision Mountain Training Inc. They live in the desert.

克里斯热爱户外运动，喜欢和妻子苏梅一起滑雪、骑自行车、慢跑和徒步旅行。他们共同创办了Vision Mountain Training Inc.公司。他们住在沙漠里。

For more information on his work, visit www.visionmou ntain.com

欲了解更多关于他的作品的信息，请访问www.visionmountain.com
